ca_east_arete_3: From US-395 in Lone Pine, turn west on Whitney Portal Road and drive about 13 miles to the road end at Whitney Portal, about 8,300 ft. A Mt. Whitney Zone permit is required for both day and overnight trips into the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek during the quota season.

Take the Mt. Whitney Trail about 0.8 mile to the unsigned North Fork of Lone Pine Creek use trail and follow it past Lower Boy Scout Lake to Upper Boy Scout Lake. Climb north up talus to the saddle between Mount Carillon and Mount Russell above Tuleinyo Lake, then follow the exposed East Arete west over the east summit to the slightly higher west summit.
ca_north_arete_4: From US-395 at Tom's Place, turn south on Rock Creek Road and drive about 10 miles to the road end at Mosquito Flat, about 10,250 ft. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Follow the Little Lakes Valley trail south about 3.5 miles; just past a creek crossing, take the signed climbers' trail to Gem Lakes. From Gem Lakes climb up and left across talus toward Dade Lake to the base of the North Arete, then climb the arete to the summit block.
ca_north_arete_6: From US-395 in Bridgeport, take Twin Lakes Road about 13 miles to its end at Mono Village on Upper Twin Lake, about 7,100 ft. Overnight parking is at the resort for a fee, and a Hoover Wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Follow the Horse Creek Trail south up Horse Creek canyon past a talus field to about 9,200 ft, then take the use trail right up steep ground to a small lake on a bench. Continue up slabs to the glacier below the north side of the peak, go a short way up the East Couloir left of the arete to its base, and climb the arete to the summit ridge, trending southwest to the top.
ca_north_ridge_4: From US-395 in Lone Pine, turn west on Whitney Portal Road and drive about 11 miles to the signed Meysan Lakes Trailhead parking on the south side of the road, just past the Whitney Portal Campground turnoff. Parking is limited, and the trail is reached on foot through the campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.
ca_northwest_chute: From US-395 at Sonora Junction, about 17 miles north of Bridgeport, turn west on CA-108 and drive about 7 miles to Leavitt Meadows Campground. Overnight hiker parking is at the lot just as you enter the campground. A Hoover Wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Walk through the campground, cross the West Walker River on the footbridge and follow the West Walker River Trail south past Lower and Upper Piute Meadows, turning at the signed junction in Upper Piute Meadows to climb to Tower Lake. Go up to Tower Pass, cross the basin beyond, climb slabs to the northwest ridge, then leave it onto the west side and traverse into the Northwest Chute, scrambling class 3 to the summit.
ca_south_lake_peaks_traverse: From US-395 in Bishop, drive west on CA-168 about 15 miles and turn left on South Lake Road, then follow it about 7 miles to the road end above South Lake, about 9,800 ft. Overnight parking at the trailhead is limited and fills in summer; a wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.
ca_southeast_face_aka_the_waterfall_rout: From US 395 in Bishop, drive west on West Line Street (Highway 168) about 18 miles and turn right onto North Lake Road, a steep, narrow dirt road. At about 1.6 miles turn right into the hiker parking lot near the pack station, then walk about 0.6 mile up the road to the trailhead at the far end of North Lake Campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Follow the Piute Pass Trail west for about 1.4 miles. Just below Loch Leven, where the trail climbs a series of granite ramps, leave it and go cross-country northwest to the base of the southeast face, left of the Piute Crags. Climb the blocky water streak, taking the left of two cracks that split the lower face, then easier slabs above to the summit.
ca_southwest_slope_and_northwest_face: From US 395 in Bishop, drive west on West Line Street (Highway 168) about 18 miles and turn right onto North Lake Road, a steep, narrow dirt road. At about 1.6 miles turn right into the hiker parking lot near the pack station, then walk about 0.6 mile up the road to the trailhead at the far end of North Lake Campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Take the Piute Pass Trail past Loch Leven to Piute Pass, then leave the trail and go cross-country northwest across Humphreys Basin to the highest Humphreys Lake. Climb the southwest slope, most easily by the wide chute on its far left, to the broad gully that slants up and left to the notch northwest of the summit, then finish up the northwest face, with about 100 feet of easy class 4 below the top.
ca_the_mountaineer_s_route: From US 395 in Lone Pine, turn west at the stoplight onto Whitney Portal Road and drive about 13 miles to its end at Whitney Portal. A Mount Whitney Zone permit is required for both day and overnight trips on this route, and human waste must be packed out.

Start up the Whitney Trail and leave it where it crosses the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, about a mile up. Follow the climbers' path up the North Fork and over the Ebersbacher Ledges to Lower and Upper Boy Scout Lakes, then over slabs to Iceberg Lake. Climb the couloir above to the notch, then the steep final gully and face on the north side to the summit plateau.
ca_west_face_11: From US 395 in Independence, drive west on Market Street (Onion Valley Road) about 4.5 miles and turn left onto unpaved Foothill Road at the Shepherd Pass sign. Pass the stock trailhead, then turn west onto a small, rough dirt road and follow the main track to the Symmes Creek hiker trailhead. The roads are unpaved and can be rough. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

Follow the Shepherd Pass Trail up Symmes Creek, over the saddle into Shepherd Creek, and on past Anvil Camp and The Pothole toward Shepherd Pass. Below the pass, leave the trail and head southeast into the Williamson Bowl, crossing its boulder fields past the lakes to the base of the west face, then climb the class 3 chute to the summit plateau.
ca_mt_shasta_avalanche_gulch: From I-5, take the Central Mount Shasta exit into Mount Shasta city and head east on Lake Street, which becomes Everitt Memorial Highway. Follow it about 12 miles from town up the mountain to the large Bunny Flat parking area. A wilderness permit and, above 10,000 feet, a Summit Pass are required; both can be self-issued at the trailhead, along with pack-out waste bags.
ca_saber_ridge_traverse_south_to_north: Enter Sequoia National Park on Highway 198 through Three Rivers and follow the Generals Highway up to the Giant Forest Museum. Turn onto Crescent Meadow Road and drive about 2.5 miles to its end at the Crescent Meadow parking area, the start of the High Sierra Trail. A park entrance fee applies, the road is closed by snow in winter, and a wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.
ca_northwest_arete_2: Drive into Yosemite Valley on Hwy 41, 140 or 120 and follow Southside Drive east toward Curry Village. Private cars cannot drive to Happy Isles; park in the trailhead parking near Curry Village and walk or ride the valley shuttle to the Happy Isles stop. A park entrance fee applies, and overnight trips need a Yosemite wilderness permit.

Hike the Mist Trail or John Muir Trail past Vernal and Nevada Falls into Little Yosemite Valley, then follow the Merced Lake trail east past Bunnell Point. Leave the trail near its high point beyond Bunnell Point and climb southeast cross-country up one of the steep drainages below Mount Clark, through forest, slabs and talus, to the broad toe of the northwest ridge, then follow the exposed class 4 arete to the summit.
ca_northwest_buttress_2: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to the northeast end of Tenaya Lake, between Olmsted Point and Tuolumne Meadows, and park in the pullout along the lake's northeast shore. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

Walk south through the forest and across the meadow and creek near the east end of the lake, aiming for the toe of the buttress; faint climbers' trails in the drainage just left (east) of the buttress save most of the bushwhacking. Climb the long, mostly easy buttress to the summit.
ca_southeast_buttress_2: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to Tuolumne Meadows and park in the Cathedral Lakes trailhead lot beside the Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center; roadside parking at the trail's original start is not allowed. A short connector trail leads west to the Cathedral Lakes trail. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

Start up the Cathedral Lakes trail (John Muir Trail) and within the first half mile branch onto the climbers' trail along Budd Creek, which stays on the west side of the creek and ends east of the Southeast Buttress after about 1,500 ft of gain. Scramble west through the trees to the base of the buttress and climb about five pitches to the summit.
ca_tenaya_matthes_cathedral_traverse: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to the northeast end of Tenaya Lake, between Olmsted Point and Tuolumne Meadows, and park in the lot or pullouts along the lake's northeast shore. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.
ca_tuolumne_alpine_triple_crown: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.
ca_west_ridge_5: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.

From the dam, follow use trails southwest past the old Carnegie Institute station to the north side of Alpine Lake, then climb northwest to the East Ridge and follow it west to the broad summit plateau. Cross the plateau and drop down the sandy gully marked by a large cairn, then talus, to the base of the West Ridge, and climb the ridge (about 12 pitches, mostly 4th class with moves to 5.6) back to the summit.
co_a_walk_in_the_park: From Estes Park, take US 36 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Beaver Meadows Entrance, then turn left onto Bear Lake Road and follow it about 8 miles to the Glacier Gorge Trailhead at about 9,200 ft. The small lot fills very early; the park shuttle also stops here. A park entrance pass is required, and in the summer season a timed-entry reservation covering Bear Lake Road.
co_arapaho_peaks_traverse: From Nederland, drive south on CO 119 about 0.5 mile and turn west onto County Road 130, signed for Eldora. Continue through the town of Eldora; past the end of the pavement, stay right at the Hessie Trailhead turnoff and again at the next fork, then follow the rough dirt road about 4 more miles to the Fourth of July Trailhead at Buckingham Campground (about 10,200 ft). The road is passable to cars in summer only.

Take the Arapaho Pass trail past the Diamond Lake junction (about 1.1 miles) to the Fourth of July Mine ruins (about 2 miles). Turn sharply back to the northeast onto the signed Arapaho Glacier trail and follow it above treeline to the saddle on the peak's southeast shoulder at about 12,700 ft, then scramble loose rocky ground past a false summit to the top.
co_blitzen_ridge: From Estes Park, take US 34 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Fall River Entrance. About 2.1 miles past the entrance station, turn right onto Old Fall River Road; the Lawn Lake Trailhead lot is about 0.1 mile along on the north side of the road. A park entrance pass is required.
co_east_ridge_the_citadel_clear_creek_co: From I-70, take Exit 218 (between Georgetown and the Eisenhower Tunnel) to the north side of the highway, where the Herman Gulch Trailhead lot sits just off the exit at about 10,300 ft. The lot fills early on summer weekends.
co_glacier_gorge_traverse: From Estes Park, take US 36 west into Rocky Mountain National Park through the Beaver Meadows Entrance, then turn left onto Bear Lake Road and follow it about 8 miles to the Glacier Gorge Trailhead at about 9,200 ft. The small lot fills very early; the park shuttle also stops here. A park entrance pass is required, and in the summer season a timed-entry reservation covering Bear Lake Road.
co_longs_peak_keyhole_route: From Estes Park, take CO 7 south about 9 miles and turn right (west) at the sign for the Longs Peak Ranger Station and Campground, then drive about 1 mile up Longs Peak Road to the trailhead at about 9,400 ft. The lot fills well before dawn in summer; there is no entrance station here.

Follow the Longs Peak trail through Goblins Forest and past the Jim's Grove and Chasm Lake junctions to Granite Pass, then on to the Boulder Field and up to the Keyhole on the northwest ridge. From the Keyhole, follow the painted bullseyes across the Ledges, up the Trough gully, along the exposed Narrows, and up the slabs of the Homestretch to the summit.
co_pyramid_peak_northeast_ridge: From Aspen, drive west on Highway 82 to the roundabout, turn onto Maroon Creek Road and follow it about 9.5 miles to the Maroon Lake parking area at the road end. In summer the road is closed to private vehicles during the day, so plan on a parking reservation or the shuttle from Aspen; a fee is charged at the entrance station.

Take the Crater Lake trail about 1.5 miles to the junction near 10,100 ft and turn left onto the Pyramid Peak trail, which climbs steeply to the amphitheater below the north face. Cross the rock glacier on a faint cairned path, climb about 1,000 ft of loose scree to the northeast ridge saddle near 13,000 ft, then follow cairned ledges, the green wall and the west-side gullies to the summit.
co_south_ramp: From Estes Park, take US 36 to the Beaver Meadows entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park, turn left onto Bear Lake Road just past the station and drive about 9 miles to the Bear Lake parking area at the road end. A park pass is required, and in the busy season Bear Lake Road needs a timed-entry reservation; the lot fills early, and a shuttle runs from the Park and Ride about 5 miles up the road.

Take the connector down to the Glacier Gorge trail, turn left at the junction for Mills Lake and continue past Jewel Lake to Black Lake. Skirt the right side of the lake, climb the boulder field and grassy slopes behind it on an intermittent path, traverse left on grassy ledges toward the valley between McHenrys Peak and Arrowhead, then scramble slabs to the long ramp that angles up right and around the north side of the summit.
co_spiral_route: From Estes Park, take US 36 to the Beaver Meadows entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park, turn left onto Bear Lake Road just past the station and drive about 9 miles to the Bear Lake parking area at the road end. A park pass is required, and in the busy season Bear Lake Road needs a timed-entry reservation; the lot fills early, and a shuttle runs from the Park and Ride about 5 miles up the road.

Go counterclockwise around Bear Lake a short way and take the Fern Lake trail about 2.8 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. Drop left to Lake Helene, go counterclockwise around it and follow cairns over rock humps to the small lake below the south ridge, then climb talus and a gully to the ramp leading up right onto the ridge crest, where the roped climbing starts and spirals around the peak to the summit.
co_wetterhorn_peak_southeast_ridge: From Lake City, turn west on Second Street, then left onto Henson Creek Road. Near 9 miles turn right onto the rougher North Henson Creek Road, and near 11 miles reach the signed Matterhorn Creek junction, where cars without 4WD park. High-clearance 4WD vehicles can turn up the steep, rocky Matterhorn Creek road about 0.7 mile to the upper trailhead at a Forest Service gate.

Follow the trail north about 0.75 mile to a junction near 11,200 ft and turn right, switchbacking out of the trees, then turn left onto the Wetterhorn trail near 12,000 ft. Zigzag through the rocks to the 13,100-ft saddle on the southeast ridge, follow the ridge on a faint trail left of the crest, pass right of the Prow near 13,800 ft, and go through the notch to the final Class 3 slabs to the summit.
co_wham_ridge: From Silverton, drive south on US 550 about 5.3 miles toward Molas Pass to the Molas Trail parking area on the left; coming from Durango it is about a mile past the top of Molas Pass on the right. The lot is reachable in a standard car.

Follow the Colorado Trail down about 30 switchbacks to the Animas River, cross the footbridge, walk the railroad tracks briefly and climb the Elk Creek trail to the beaver ponds near 10,000 ft. Leave the Colorado Trail there for the unmaintained climbers' trail that climbs steeply south up Vestal Creek through deadfall into Vestal Basin, then climb the long quartzite slab of Wham Ridge, the north face of Vestal Peak, to the summit.
co_wilson_peak_southwest_ridge: From Telluride, drive west on Highway 145 about 6 miles and turn left onto the dirt Silver Pick Road. After 4 miles turn right onto FS 622 for 2.3 miles, then turn right at the Rock of Ages sign onto FS 645 and drive 2.2 miles to the trailhead. About 1 mile up FS 645 the road fords Big Bear Creek, which is usually manageable by mid-July.

Follow the Wilson Mesa Trail about half a mile to the Rock of Ages Trail and climb out of Elk Creek Basin into Silver Pick Basin on old mining roads, staying on the trail across private land, then switchback up talus to the Rock of Ages saddle. Cross the loose slope east to the Wilson Peak-Gladstone saddle, traverse south-side ledges onto the southwest ridge, follow it to the false summit, downclimb into the notch and make the exposed final moves to the summit.
co_castle_peak_northeast_ridge: From the roundabout on Highway 82 just west of Aspen, take Castle Creek Road south about 12.5 miles to the end of the pavement, where passenger cars park. Beyond here the road continues as Forest Road 102, a rough road suited only to high-clearance 4WD vehicles.

Follow Forest Road 102 about 1.3 miles to a footbridge creek crossing, then nearly 2 more miles to the Pearl Pass junction near 11,150 ft and turn right into Montezuma Basin. Walk the road to its end near 12,800 ft, climb the headwall into the upper basin, take the path to the northeast ridge crest near 13,700 ft, and follow the ridge to the summit; the final 250 ft is steep and loose.
co_grays_peak_north_slopes: From I-70 Exit 221 (Bakerville), cross to the south side of the interstate and take Forest Road 189 up Stevens Gulch. Stay straight at the junction after about 1 mile and continue roughly 2 more miles to the summer trailhead at about 11,280 ft. The road is rough and a good-clearance vehicle is recommended; the lot fills early on weekends.

Cross the bridge over Stevens Gulch creek and follow the Grays Peak Trail up the valley to the rocky flats near 12,300 ft. The trail climbs toward the east side of Grays; at the junction near 13,300 ft stay left (right goes to Torreys Peak), then switchback up the north slopes to the summit.
co_huron_peak_northwest_slopes: From US 24 between Buena Vista and Leadville, turn west on Chaffee County Road 390 at Clear Creek Reservoir and drive about 12 miles of dirt road to the old townsite of Winfield. Continue south about 2 miles on the rough 4WD road, staying right at the junction after 0.7 mile, to the trailhead at the road end. Passenger cars park near Winfield and walk the road.

Follow the Huron Peak trail into the forest, cross a stream after about half a mile, switchback up the slope, then head south to treeline near 11,900 ft. Cross the high basin to the east and switchback up Huron's northern slopes to the north ridge near 13,500 ft; the rockier ground between about 13,700 and 13,900 ft is the crux before the final slopes to the summit.
co_mount_elbert_northeast_ridge: From US 24 about 3.5 miles south of Leadville, turn west on Colorado 300 and drive 0.7 mile, turn left onto Lake County Road 11 for 1.2 miles, then turn right onto Halfmoon Creek Road. Follow the dirt road about 5 miles to the North Mount Elbert Trailhead on the left at about 10,040 ft. The parking area fills early on weekends.

Hike south to join the Colorado Trail, cross a footbridge and switchback through forest for about a mile, then turn right onto the North Mount Elbert Trail. Follow it to treeline near 11,900 ft and climb the northeast ridge, which steepens and turns rocky above 13,400 ft, to the flat crest near 13,900 ft and on southwest to the summit. On descent, stay on this ridge trail rather than the East Ridge trail.
id_diamond_peak_east_ridge: From Idaho Highway 28 in the Birch Creek Valley on the east side of the Lemhi Range, turn west on the signed Pass Creek Road, north of the old Blue Dome site. After the first couple of miles the road fords Pass Creek and turns rough; stay on the main track through a gate into the national forest. It ends as jeep tracks at a small saddle with a fire ring at about 8,000 ft, where parties park.

Follow the old jeep track and a worn climbers' path west up grassy slopes to a saddle near 9,300 ft, then climb the steep ridge to about 10,200 ft, where it bends northwest. Around 11,000 ft a series of 10 to 30 ft rock steps is best taken close to the crest, followed by a long stretch of Class 2 and 3 scrambling on or just left of the crest to the summit.
id_southwest_ridge: From Mackay, drive US 93 north about 20 miles and turn east onto Birch Springs Road, signed for Borah Peak, between mileposts 129 and 130. Follow the gravel road about 3 miles to the trailhead and campground at about 7,400 ft. The road is fine for most passenger cars in dry weather.

Take the climbers' trail east from the trailhead, climbing steeply through forest onto the open southwest ridge. Follow the ridge to Chicken Out Ridge near 11,800 ft and scramble along its Class 3 crest, downclimb to the saddle beyond, which often holds snow early in the season, then climb the steep, loose upper ridge to the summit.
id_thompson_peak_south_couloir: From Stanley, drive south on Idaho 75 about 4.3 miles and turn right on Redfish Lake Road. Follow it about 1.8 miles toward Redfish Lake Lodge to the large dirt backpackers' parking lot on the right. A free self-issued Sawtooth Wilderness permit is required.

Cross the road and follow the Fishhook Creek trail 0.8 mi to the signed Marshall Lake junction, then switchback north to the ridge top and follow it northwest toward Williams Peak. Where the trail bends north, stay left on the climbers' path across the loose south flank of Williams Peak to the high lake near 9,000 ft. Scramble the headwall break nearest Thompson to the saddle, go around the west side and climb the south gully to the summit.
mt_phantom_creek_trail: From I-90 at Columbus, take Montana 78 south through Absarokee, then turn right on Montana 419 and drive through Fishtail. About 1 mile past Fishtail turn left on West Rosebud Road and follow the signs for Mystic Lake to the road end beyond Emerald Lake Campground, at the Mystic Lake power plant.

Walk the West Rosebud Trail #19 west about 3 miles toward Mystic Lake, then turn left on the Phantom Creek Trail #17 and switchback steeply up to the Froze-to-Death Plateau near 10,000 ft. Cross the plateau southwest about 5 miles, staying north and west of Tempest Mountain, and drop about 600 ft to the Tempest-Granite saddle. Cross the snow bridge and climb the east ridge chimneys, 4th to low 5th class, to the summit.
mt_sacagawea_direct: From Bozeman, drive north on Bridger Canyon Road (Montana 86) past Bridger Bowl and over Battle Ridge Pass. Between mileposts 21 and 22 turn left on Fairy Lake Road (FS Road 74) and drive about 6 miles to the road end at Fairy Lake Campground. The road is rough and seasonally gated, and high clearance is recommended.

Take the Sacagawea Pass trail west through forest into the open meadows below the peak. Leave the trail in the upper basin and cross talus into the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea to the slab at the foot of the east side. Climb the steep slab, stay on the crest of the rib between two gullies, and exit onto the short ridge that leads to the summit.
or_hurwal_divide_traverse: From Joseph, head west on Airport Lane, which becomes Hurricane Creek Road, to the Hurricane Creek Grange. Turn left onto County Road 521, which becomes Forest Road 8205, and drive about 3.7 miles past Hurricane Creek Campground to the road-end trailhead. The road is rough and not suited to RVs. A free self-issued Eagle Cap Wilderness permit is required.

Walk the Hurricane Creek Trail about 1.8 miles to the unsigned, unmaintained Thorp Creek trail, ford Hurricane Creek and cross the wash of Twin Creek, then climb steep switchbacks through burned forest and blowdown to Thorp Creek Meadows, the last reliable water. Continue up Thorp Creek over fell fields and talus to the east ridge and follow it to the summit.
Follow the crest south over gendarmes, Class 3 with moderate exposure on the spine, or bypass them lower on the west side in scree, to the summit of the Matterhorn.
or_diamond_peak_south_ridge: From Highway 58 near Crescent Lake, take Forest Road 60 about 7 miles west, then continue on Forest Road 6010 about 6.5 miles west to Summit Lake. Forest Road 6010 is rough and not maintained for low-clearance vehicles; high clearance is strongly recommended.

Walk north on the Pacific Crest Trail, passing the Rockpile and Marie lakes junction at about 3.1 mi. About 1.3 mi farther, at a large open rocky viewpoint, take the cairned climbers' path west steeply up through the trees. Above treeline, climb loose rock and cinder to the false summit, then follow the narrow, exposed spine about 0.4 mi north to the summit.
or_middle_sister_north_ridge_hayden_glac: From Sisters, drive about 1.5 miles west on Highway 242 and turn left onto Forest Road 15. Follow it, paved at first and then washboard gravel, staying left at the Y at about 7 miles, to the road end at the Pole Creek Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Follow the Pole Creek Trail about 1.5 miles, go south on the Green Lakes Trail 0.7 mile, then west on the Camp Lake Trail 1.9 miles to an unmarked climbers' path on the west side of a clearing. Climb old moraine terraces west to the Hayden Glacier, rope up for crevasses, and ascend to the col between North and Middle Sister. Climb the steep north ridge about 900 ft from the col, staying on the crest, to the summit.
or_mt_bachelor_trail: From Bend, follow Century Drive, which becomes the Cascade Lakes Highway, west about 22 miles to Mt. Bachelor and turn into the West Village base area parking lot.

From the West Village base area, follow the signed summit hiking trail up through the ski area, on service roads and forest trail across the ski runs, then switchback up the steep, rocky upper ridge to the summit. This is a summer hike; in winter the mountain is an operating ski area.
or_mt_hood_south_side_hogsback: From US 26 just east of Government Camp, turn north on Timberline Road and drive about 6 miles to the parking lots at Timberline Lodge. Fill out the free self-issued climbing permit at the climbers' register in the Wy'east Day Lodge before starting. An Oregon Sno-Park permit is required to park from November through April.

Take the climbers' trail on the east edge of the ski runs past the Silcox Hut and the top of the Palmer lift at about 8,500 ft. Continue up the snowfield toward Crater Rock, past Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, and swing around its east side to the base of the Hogsback. Follow the snow ridge to the bergschrund, climb the Old Chute to the summit ridge, and walk east to the top.
or_northwest_ridge: From Bend, follow the Cascade Lakes Highway west about 27 miles, past Mt. Bachelor, to the Green Lakes/Soda Creek Trailhead on the north side of the highway at Fall Creek. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a Central Cascades Wilderness permit is required for day and overnight use during the summer permit season.
or_south_ridge_route: From Sisters, follow US 20 west about 20 miles toward Santiam Pass and turn north at the signed Pacific Crest Trail trailhead, just east of the pass summit, onto the short spur road to the parking lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Hike north on the Pacific Crest Trail about 4.7 miles to where a cairned climbers' trail cuts right, uphill into the woods below the south shoulder. Follow it up onto open slopes to a notch on the south ridge, then scramble north along the ridge, across the exposed ledge known as the Crawl, to the short low-fifth-class chimney and the final exposed scramble to the summit.
or_three_sisters_traverse: From Bend, follow the Cascade Lakes Highway west about 29 miles and turn left (south) at the sign for the Devils Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a Central Cascades Wilderness permit is required for day and overnight use during the summer permit season. Leave a second car at the Pole Creek Trailhead first.

Cross the highway and follow the South Sister climbers' trail about 1.5 miles up through forest, across a trail junction and onto the open plateau below the South Ridge. Climb the ridge on steep scree past the Lewis Glacier's moraine lake to the crater rim and follow the rim around to the summit.
Descend South Sister's Northwest Ridge on snow or scree and drop to the saddle with Middle Sister above Camp Lake, then climb large talus to Middle Sister's summit.

Descend north on snow or scree, steep snow or ice early in the season, along the upper edge of the Collier Glacier to the Prouty Point saddle. Climb loose slopes onto North Sister's ridge on paths that alternate between west-side ledges and the east side at gaps, cross the exposed Terrible Traverse snowfield, climb the loose Bowling Alley gully, and move up and right to the summit block.

Reverse the ridge to the Prouty Point saddle, descend the lateral moraine on the north side of the Hayden Glacier, and follow a climbers' path down beside a creek to the Pole Creek Trail. Cross Soap Creek and follow the trail past the Green Lakes junction and through the old burn to the trailhead, roughly 5 miles from the saddle.
or_west_ridge_2: From the junction of OR 138 and OR 230 near Diamond Lake, drive OR 138 north about 1.5 miles to the Mount Thielsen Trailhead and Sno-Park on the east side of the highway. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required to park, and an Oregon Sno-Park permit from November through April.

Follow the Mount Thielsen Trail east through lodgepole pine, passing the Spruce Ridge Trail junction, to its crossing of the Pacific Crest Trail. Keep climbing the west ridge on the unmarked climbers' path above timberline, over loose pumice and scree, to the base of the summit spire, then make the short, steep, exposed hand-over-hand climb to the top.
wa_abernathy_peak_north_ridge: From Winthrop, take SR 20 across the Methow River bridge at the south end of town and turn right onto Twin Lakes Road. In about 1.5 miles turn right onto Wolf Creek Road, then follow the signs onto gravel Forest Service road to the Wolf Creek Trailhead at about 2,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Follow Wolf Creek Trail #527 up the Wolf Creek valley about 10 miles to its end at Gardner Meadows. The trail drops a couple of hundred feet to the creek right away, then rolls up and down through burned forest, entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness early on.

From the last campsites, cross Wolf Creek on a faint path toward Abernathy Lake; it soon fades into old burn and deadfall. Stay high above the lake and make a rising traverse into the upper basin to the small tarn with cabin remains, where the stream just below is the last reliable water. From the tarn, climb the spur ridge to the north ridge crest, with a few exposed class 3 moves.
Follow a short boot path south along the crest past old mining cables and equipment. Where it fades, scramble class 2-3 boulders and scree on or near the crest to the summit.
wa_abernathy_peak_south_ridge: From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road west about 22 miles; it becomes FR 44 and then gravel FR 4440. The Scatter Creek trailhead, at about 3,100 ft, is about 50 yards past the Slate Creek Trail sign. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Follow the Scatter Creek Trail through timber beside Scatter Creek, climbing steep switchbacks into the wilderness, about 4.5 miles to Scatter Lake at about 7,050 ft. From the lake, climb the talus slope about 500 ft to the south ridge crest near 7,600 ft, then scramble north along the crest past a series of gendarmes on loose rock to the summit.
wa_accendo_lunae_lib_west_face_var: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 and follow the bumpy gravel road about 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end. FR 7601 is normally closed in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a day-use Enchantment permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Take the trail up Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles, and leave the Lake Stuart Trail at its junction around 2.25 miles for the Colchuck Lake Trail. It climbs steeply, finishing over boulders and moraine to the north end of Colchuck Lake, about 4 miles and 2,280 ft from the car. Fill water here.

Follow the trail around the lake onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail and climb talus and heather to about 400 ft above the lake, then break left through dense brush to the base gully below the wall. The route starts with Let It Burn on the wall's lower left, reached over loose 3rd and 4th class rock, and about ten pitches finish up the West Face to the summit.
wa_agnes_mountain_south_ridge: No road reaches High Bridge from outside the valley. Take the passenger ferry or a floatplane up Lake Chelan to Stehekin, then the seasonal shuttle bus about 11 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road to High Bridge at about 1,600 ft, where the Agnes Creek Trail (PCT) starts.

Follow the PCT/Agnes Creek Trail south 8-10 miles to the Spruce Creek confluence. Cross Agnes and Spruce Creeks on logs and climb steeply northwest off-trail through brush, talus and slabs to Upper Blue Basin and a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass (about 6,760 ft). Then go over Point 7458, climb the south-side snow couloir to the south col (about 7,480 ft), and follow the ridge and summit-block chimney to the top.
wa_alpine_lookout_round_mountain_trail: From Leavenworth, drive US 2 west about 17.5 miles (or about 18 miles east from Stevens Pass) to just past the Nason Creek Rest Area and turn north onto the unsigned Butcher Creek Road, FR 6910; the turn is on a curve with fast traffic. Follow good gravel about 4.5 miles, then take spur FR 6910-170 a short way to the Round Mountain Trailhead at about 3,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Climb Round Mountain Trail #1529 steeply for about 1.6 miles and 1,400 ft through forest and old burn to Nason Ridge Trail #1583. Turn left (west) and follow the crest about 3 miles of ups and downs, across the narrow knife edge at Ninemile Saddle, to the short spur that climbs right to the staffed lookout.
wa_argonaut_peak_east_ridge: From I-90 Exit 85 east of Cle Elum, follow SR 970 about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Keep right onto North Fork Teanaway Road, which becomes gravel FR 9737 at 29 Pines Campground. Continue just under 4 miles and, just before the Beverly Creek bridge, turn right onto FR 9737-112, a rough one-lane spur best with high clearance, for about 1.4 miles to its end at about 3,650 ft.

Take Beverly Turnpike Trail #1391 up Beverly Creek, bearing left at about 0.5 mile rather than onto the Bean Creek trail. At about 3.1 miles turn right onto Fourth Creek Trail #1226.1, cross Fourth Creek Pass (about 6,000 ft), and descend to Ingalls Creek at about 6 miles and ford it. Leave the Ingalls Creek Trail and climb north into the Porcupine Creek basin, working up beside the southeast ridge to its foot.

Climb about eight pitches up the crest of the southeast ridge, blocky and lichen-covered low down, to the southeast spire. Make two single-rope rappels or one double-rope rappel into the notch beyond, then continue to the true summit on the west spire.
wa_argonaut_peak_northeast_couloir: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail to around the Colchuck Lake junction, then leave it, cross Mountaineer Creek and bushwhack south toward Argonaut's north side, using talus to avoid the slide-alder slope. Snow usually starts near 4,700 ft. Climb the drainage to the couloir just east of the Northeast Buttress, follow it about 1,200 ft as it narrows, exit on a mid-fifth-class or icy pitch, and scramble to the A-frame summit blocks.
wa_beckey_davis: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the lake's south end, climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles, then cross the Core past Tranquil and Isolation lakes and go cross-country north over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn below Prusik's south face.

Walk up from the tarn to the foot of the south face and find two large V-shaped features; the route starts in the chimney immediately left of them, to the right of the classic line in the middle of the face.

Climb seven pitches, about 650 ft: left out of the chimney onto knobs, up face and cracks to Snafflehound Ledge, traverse right, take the 5.9 dihedral crux, then the crack and gully past a chockstone to the notch east of the summit horn, finishing with a friction traverse and jam crack to the summit.
wa_big_chiwaukum_west_ridge: From Leavenworth, drive west on US-2 about 21.5 miles and turn left onto White Pine Road (FS Road 6950); follow it to the road end at the Whitepine Creek Trailhead, ignoring right-hand turns into private or gated land. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Follow Whitepine Creek Trail #1582 up the valley about 2.5 miles and bear left onto Wildhorse Creek Trail #1592, climbing through forest into the Wildhorse basin to about 5,400 ft, where the trail passes directly west of the summit. Leave the trail, climb through meadows to the west ridge, follow it east to below the headwall, and scramble ledges to the top.
wa_bonanza_peak_north_ridge: There is no road to Holden Village. Take the Lady of the Lake boat up Lake Chelan to Lucerne, then ride the Holden Village bus about 11 miles up FS Road 8301 to the village at about 3,300 ft; reserve the bus seat in advance. A free self-issued Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is required.

From the west side of the village, hike the Railroad Creek Trail about 1 mile and turn right onto Holden Lake Trail #1251, climbing about 4 miles to Holden Lake. Continue toward Holden Pass, then take the climbers' path through slide alder to the Mary Green Glacier at about 7,300 ft. Climb its north edge past the bergschrund, scramble loose gullies and ribs to a notch on the upper ridge, and follow the exposed ridge to the true summit.
wa_boving_christensen: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the lake's south end, climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles, then cross the Core past Tranquil and Isolation lakes and go cross-country north over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn below Prusik's south face.

Walk up from the tarn to the west end of the south face, find the outside corner where it turns onto the west side, and walk about 100 ft right along the base to the start. Four pitches, about 450 ft, of crack, slab, face and corner climbing reach the West Ridge; the route tops out on the ridge rather than at the summit.
wa_buck_mountain_south_ridge: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR-207 north 4.2 miles past the Wenatchee River crossing and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road. After 1.3 miles turn left onto Chiwawa River Road (FS Road 62) and drive about 22 miles, the last 11 on rough gravel, keeping left at the final junction for the Trinity Trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the kiosk.
wa_bulls_tooth_standard: Drive US 2 to Stevens Pass and park in the large lot signed for the Pacific Crest Trail on the south side of the highway, just east of the ski area buildings, at about 4,060 ft. Fill out the free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit before starting.

Follow the Pacific Crest Trail south up through the ski area to a 5,150 ft ridge in about 2 miles, switchback down the far side, cross a service road and power lines, and continue past Lake Susan Jane. At just under 5 miles, turn off at the junction with the Icicle Creek Trail, which leads along the shore of Josephine Lake.

Follow the Icicle Creek Trail around the lake, down steeply to its outlet and on past the Whitepine Creek Trail junction. At just over 8 miles from the pass, turn onto the Chain Lakes Trail and climb steeply, about 2,000 ft in 2 miles, into the Chain Lakes basin. Continue past the lakes, climb talus to the gap between the basins, and drop steeply to Upper Doelle Lake.
wa_cannon_mountain_northeast_ridge: From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto the signed gravel Eightmile Road (FR 7601), crossing Icicle Creek and climbing a washboarded, potholed road. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Climb steep, bushy, loose burned slopes to the northeast ridge crest, then scramble southwest over big blocks, Coney Lake below to the east, about half a mile to a band of towers near 7,980 ft. Drop right (west) and traverse about 0.3 mile of loose ribs near 7,900 ft, climb the large loose gully beyond about 500 ft back to the crest, and walk south to the summit block, finishing by friction on its east side.
wa_cannon_mountain_south_slopes: From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive 4.2 miles to the paved Snow Lakes Trailhead lot at about 1,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park. Day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment permit at the trailhead; overnight stays from May 15 to Oct 31 need a quota permit.
wa_cardinal_peak_nw_couloir_north_ridge: From US 97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FR 51) just after the bridge and drive about 32 miles up the valley to FR 5606, about 2 miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FR 5606 north about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead, about 3,940 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee is required.
wa_cashmere_mountain_northeast_ridge: Take Eightmile Lake Trail #1552 about 2.8 miles to the junction past Little Eightmile Lake, go right on Trail #1554 to Lake Caroline and on toward Windy Pass, then go cross-country east onto the west end of the mountain. Below the summit pyramid, cross to the north side of the ridgeline and traverse the north-facing scree field east to the low point on the northeast ridge; early in the season this is steep snow with poor run-outs.
Follow the ridge crest straight up at the summit pyramid, mostly class 3 with a few class 4 moves, with the north face dropping away steeply behind you.
wa_cashmere_mountain_se_route: From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601, signed for the Eightmile Trailhead. The trailhead is 3.1 miles up this washboarded, potholed road at about 3,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and the area is within the Enchantment permit area, so fill out the self-issued day-use permit.

Start up the Eightmile Lake Trail and, not far in, push through brush onto an unsigned old logging road. From it, climb about 1,000 ft of ashen, deadfall-choked burn, then go cross-country up and left toward the southeast gullies, crossing a snowfield to the broad gully between the south and southeast ridges. Climb it at class 2 to 3, staying center or right, to about 8,150 ft, then scramble the last 360 ft to the summit.
wa_cashmere_mountain_west_ridge: Hike the Eightmile Lake Trail #1552 about 2.8 miles to the junction just past Little Eightmile Lake and go right onto Trail #1554, signed for Lake Caroline. Pass Lake Caroline and Little Lake Caroline toward Windy Pass; at about 6,850 ft leave the trail and head east cross-country to the camp area near 7,100 ft (last reliable water), then climb north-northeast to the broad col on the peak's west side at about 8,000 ft.

Follow the west ridge to about 8,200 ft and weave past the gendarmes: stay low on the south side past the western spires, then cross onto the north side and keep traversing low. Once the end of the summit formation is in sight, climb the class 3 gully directly above to a notch with a view down the far side, then scramble the crest, with one short corkscrew move, to the table-sized summit block.
wa_chalangin_peak_little_giant_pass_luah: From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north 4.4 miles, turn right on Chiwawa Loop Road for 0.4 mile, then take the second left onto Chiwawa River Road (FS Road 62) and drive about 19 miles to the Little Giant Trailhead at 2,600 ft. The road turns to rough gravel and dirt after about 11 miles. No parking pass is needed; fill out the free wilderness permit at the trailhead.

Ford the Chiwawa River and climb the trail to 6,409 ft Little Giant Pass, then descend about 2,200 ft into the Napeequa valley and follow the river, off-trail higher up, to camp near Butterfly Butte. Climb west through larch and pumice to a bench near 6,800 ft above the glacier, keep north of the ice across slabs and tarns below the north ridge, and take the northeastern notch by a scree gully near 8,000 ft to the loose crest and summit.
wa_chalangin_peak_southwest_face: From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north toward Lake Wenatchee and continue onto White River Road (FS Road 6400), following it about 10 miles to its end at the White River Trailhead at 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_chelan_butte_chelan_butte_trail: In Chelan, follow SR 150 (E Woodin Ave), turn left on Sanders St, then left on Farnham St, continue onto S Saunders St, and turn left on E Iowa Ave to the trailhead parking lot on the left. A Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass is required to park.

Climb the jeep track from the lot and take the marked hiking-trail cutoff about a quarter mile in. The trail climbs steadily with lake views to a short side trip to the Elephant Head viewpoint, then steepens along the ridgeline to the radio and TV towers, where a final 100 ft of road reaches the summit, about 3.7 miles from the trailhead.
wa_colchuck_balanced_rock_col_east_lake_: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn south onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow this rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and day trips need the free self-issued permit at the trailhead.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.25 miles, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge near 1.5 miles, to the signed junction and turn left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail. Cross the creek again on a second log bridge, then climb increasingly steep, rocky switchbacks to the lake, about 4 miles from the trailhead.

Where the trail meets the lake, take the left fork and stay high on the ridge, ignoring the spurs that drop to the water. Follow it to the small dam at the lake's north end and cross the outlet creek on or just below the dam.

On the far side pick up the path and follow it south about 100 yards to a slight clearing with boulders and talus on the left. Head up the talus, angling slightly left into the woods, to a short rock step; pull up on roots and branches with the rock on your left rather than climbing it head-on.
wa_colchuck_balanced_rock_west_face: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn south onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow this rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and day trips need the free self-issued permit at the trailhead.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.25 miles through forest along Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge near the 1.5-mile mark, to the signed junction where the Colchuck Lake Trail splits left.

Turn left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek again on a second log bridge, and climb increasingly steep, rocky switchbacks about 1.75 miles to a broad granite slab overlooking the lake.

Follow the lakeshore climbers' path around the lake toward the slopes below Aasgard Pass. About 400 ft above the lake, leave that path and traverse left (north) through dense slide alder toward the foot of the leftmost gully; cairns are sparse and easy to lose.
Climb the leftmost gully about 1,000 ft to its top, then contour east on easy ground into the talus cirque below the West Face. Snow can linger in the gully into early summer.

Boulder-hop the cirque to a left-facing, lightly vegetated corner at the foot of the wall and scramble up to a ledge where the first pitch starts; if you are under black streaks or a large pale rock scar you are too far right. Climb nine pitches of sustained cracks and corners, finishing with an exposed boulder move to mantel onto the summit block.
From the summit block, scramble to the webbing-slung horn on its east side for the single 30 m rappel.
wa_colchuck_peak_east_ridge: From the trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake Trail along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and take the Colchuck Lake Trail, which crosses the creek and switchbacks up through boulder fields for another 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft.

Follow the lakeshore trail to the boulder field at the lake's south end and climb the moraine and basin onto the Colchuck Glacier. Ascend the glacier, keeping climber's right away from rockfall off Dragontail, to the col between Colchuck Peak and Dragontail, then turn right and scramble the Class 2-3 ridge west to the summit.
wa_colchuck_peak_holsten_hilden: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required. In winter the road is usually gated well below the trailhead, adding miles on foot or ski.

From the trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake Trail along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and take the Colchuck Lake Trail, which crosses the creek and switchbacks up another 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft.

From the south end of the lake, climb the basin to the Colchuck Glacier below the northeast face. Past the North Buttress Couloir, start below the Hidden Couloir, right of the Northeast Couloir, on two 60 m ice pitches. Climb snow, mixed ground and the M6 chimney to a notch on the north ridge, then finish up the last couloir of the North Buttress Couloir line to the summit.
wa_colchuck_peak_north_buttress_couloir: From the trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake Trail along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and take the Colchuck Lake Trail, which crosses the creek and switchbacks up to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft. When the lake is frozen, parties often cross it directly.

Go around to the far, south side of the lake, climb up onto the lateral moraine and follow its crest right toward the glacier. The couloir is the first major gully the moraine leads into; cross or skirt the moat, climb about 2,000 ft of snow to the notch at its top, and continue to the summit.
wa_colchuck_peak_northeast_couloir: From the trailhead, follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and take the Colchuck Lake Trail, which crosses the creek and climbs steep, rooty switchbacks for another 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake. Fill water here; it is the last easy source.

Follow the lakeshore path to the inlet at the south end, then leave the trail and climb talus, heather benches or snow up the basin to the toe of the Colchuck Glacier. Instead of heading up-glacier toward the col, traverse the glacier's climber's-right margin toward the north face to the narrow slot of the couloir, crossing the moat at the glacier's edge.

Climb the couloir on snow and ice up to about 60 degrees until it runs into a steep wall, exit left along the wall's base on steep snow or ice to the summit ridge, and scramble the last short mixed steps to the summit.
wa_der_dihedral: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required.

From the trailhead, follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek about 2.6 miles to the signed junction, turn left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, cross the creek and switchback up to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft.

Follow the lakeshore trail to the south end of the lake, past the campsites, then cross the large talus blocks on the cairned climbers' path and gain the crest of the Colchuck Glacier's lateral moraine below Dragontail's north face.

Follow the moraine and talus toward the toe of Backbone Ridge, but stop a couple of ridgelines short of it, lower on the face. The start is little travelled and not well cairned; look for a clean left-facing dihedral a pitch or two up the initial ridge.

Climb broken rock to the clean left-facing dihedral, jam it past the roof, and continue up the corner system until the route merges with the Northeast Arete around two-thirds height; follow that finish and scramble to the summit.
wa_dragontail_peak_backbone_ridge: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required.

From the trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake Trail along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction, turn left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross the creek and switchback up to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft.
wa_dragontail_peak_east_ridge_aasgard_pa: From the trailhead, follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction, turn left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, cross the creek and switchback up to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft.

Follow the trail along the lake's west shore, across the boulder field at the south end and around to the inlet below Aasgard Pass, then climb the cairned path up the pass, about 2,200 ft in three quarters of a mile. Stay left: a few hundred feet up the path crosses to the left of the creek, and at about 6,400 ft keep left of the small cliff band with the waterfall and ignore side paths toward it.

From the top of the pass, head right along a short ridge above a tarn and up the boulder field on cairns, then cross the small, nearly crevasse-free Snow Creek Glacier (about 30 degrees at its steepest) to the east-ridge saddle at about 8,500 ft. From the saddle, follow about 300 ft of bootpath and easy Class 3 granite up the ridge to the summit.
wa_dragontail_peak_r2: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required. In winter the road is usually gated well below the trailhead, adding miles on foot or ski.
wa_dragontail_peak_r3: From the trailhead, follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek about 2.5 miles to the signed junction, turn left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, cross the creek and switchback up to Colchuck Lake at about 5,570 ft. Camps are along the shore toward the south end.
Follow the trail along the lake's west shore to the boulder field at the south end, then climb talus and the moraine onto the Colchuck Glacier below the Colchuck-Dragontail col.

Climb the glacier to Colchuck Col, the saddle between Colchuck Peak and Dragontail. It is mostly snow early in the season and firm neve or ice with talus showing later; carry crampons and an axe, and look for a snow finger on the right if a band of blue ice spans the snowfield.

The couloir entrance is not at the col but a couple hundred feet toward Dragontail along the base of the ridge. Climb the couloir, firm 40-45 degree snow early in the season and loose Class 3 talus by late summer, to the notch that cuts right through the ridge.

From the notch, descend the steep, narrow snow finger on the far side, or leave the couloir about 30 ft below the notch and climb about 20 ft of Class 4 rock to the ridge. Traverse the easier snow and talus below the south side of the ridge, exposed in places, and scramble up to the summit.
Descend to the saddle southeast of the summit, then make the long traverse east across the snow slope to Aasgard Pass.
wa_dragontail_peak_r4: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required. In winter the road is usually gated well below the trailhead, adding miles on foot or ski.
wa_emerald_peak_se_ridge: From US-97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FS Road 51) and drive about 32 miles up the valley, then turn right onto FS Road 5606, about two miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FS Road 5606 about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_emerald_peak_west_route: From US-97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FS Road 51) and drive about 32 miles up the valley, then turn right onto FS Road 5606, about two miles past Silver Falls Campground. Follow FS Road 5606 about 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_enchantment_enchainment: From US-2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow the potholed gravel road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; day visitors self-issue a free Enchantment permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a lottery permit. FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, typically November to May.
wa_enchantment_peak_southwest_scramble: From US-2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow the potholed gravel road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; day visitors self-issue a free Enchantment permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a lottery permit. FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, typically November to May.
wa_energizer_bunny: From US-2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow the potholed gravel road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; day visitors self-issue a free Enchantment permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a lottery permit. FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, typically November to May.

Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles and turn left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail, crossing Mountaineer Creek and climbing to Colchuck Lake. Follow the west shore to the boulder field at the south end and climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles. From the pass go cross-country east through the Core past Isolation and Tranquil lakes to Perfection Lake, then scramble north up granite toward Prusik Pass to the tarn.

From the tarn, scramble a short way up granite to the base of Prusik Peak's south face. The route starts just left of Solid Gold under a roof and climbs about five pitches, joining Solid Gold's final corner crack near the top.
wa_esmeralda_peaks_east_gully: From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Follow it north as it becomes the North Fork Teanaway Road to the end of pavement at 29 Pines Campground, then continue straight on gravel FR 9737 for about 10 miles to its end at the Esmeralda Basin and Ingalls Lake trailhead, about a mile past the De Roux campground. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_esmeralda_peaks_scramble: From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Follow it north as it becomes the North Fork Teanaway Road to the end of pavement at 29 Pines Campground, then continue straight on gravel FR 9737 for about 8.5 miles and take the left fork into the De Roux campground and trailhead, about a mile short of the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; self-issue the free wilderness permit at the kiosk.

Take the Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 west, crossing the North Fork Teanaway and then De Roux Creek on bridges. About a mile in, keep right where the De Roux spur branches left, on the trail signed for Gallagher Head Lake, and climb the valley past several waterfalls and a rock-hop creek crossing to the trail's last switchback, where it crosses a talus ridge beside a house-sized boulder.

Leave the trail on the boulder's climber's left and climb northeast up about 1,100 ft of sustained Class 2 scree and talus with no marked path; the line beneath the southwest ridge and the talus farther to climber's right both go. The top 100 to 150 ft is loose broken rock to the walk-up west summit.
wa_fifth_of_july_mountain_scramble: From US-97A just south of the town of Entiat, turn west onto the Entiat River Road and follow it about 38 miles up the valley; it becomes FR 51 and then FR 5100, turns to gravel at Cottonwood Campground, and ends a short way beyond at the Entiat River Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_flora_mountain_southwest_slope: There is no road to Stehekin. From Chelan, take the Lady of the Lake passenger ferry (or a floatplane) up Lake Chelan to Stehekin Landing, then ride the park shuttle bus about 4.4 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road to the Harlequin Bridge stop.

Cross Harlequin Bridge, follow the road past Harlequin Camp and the airstrip to the Stehekin River Trail, and take it about 3 miles southeast to the signed Devore Creek Trail. Climb that about 4 miles to Bird Creek Camp, then go cross-country up to the saddle south of Enigma Peak near 7,460 ft, drop about 600 ft east to cross upper Castle Creek, and climb the loose talus of the southwest ridge to the summit.
wa_fortress_mountain_east_ridge: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north 4.3 miles and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then turn left onto the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62) and follow it about 23 miles, paved and then gravel, to the large Trinity lot just before the gate at the road end. The last stretch is rough and rutted; high clearance helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_fortress_mountain_northeast_face: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north 4.3 miles and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then turn left onto the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62) and follow it about 23 miles, paved and then gravel, to the large Trinity lot just before the gate at the road end. The last stretch is rough and rutted; high clearance helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_fortress_mountain_southwest_face: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR-207 north, turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200). Follow it about 22 miles, the last stretch on rough gravel, and keep left at the final junction where the Phelps Creek road climbs right, to the Trinity Trailhead at the road end at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued Glacier Peak Wilderness permit are required.

Follow Buck Creek Trail #1513 about 9 to 9.5 miles, through forest and an old avalanche debris field near 4,500 ft. At about 5,800 ft an unmarked way-trail bears right; take it to Pass No Pass (about 6,400 ft) and the benches beyond, where the face comes into view. Climb grass and scree into Class 2-3 talus and slab, staying right of the loose central gully on slabbier rock or following the south ridge, to the talus summit.
wa_fortune_peak_east_slope: From I-90 Exit 85 east of Cle Elum, take SR-970 to Teanaway Road and follow the North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends at 29 Pines Campground, take the right fork, FR 9737, about 10 miles to its end at the Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (about 4,270 ft). A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Follow the Esmeralda Basin Trail a short way and turn right onto Ingalls Way #1390, climbing to Ingalls Pass (about 6,500 ft). Take the upper of the two trails above Headlight Basin toward Lake Ingalls for about half a mile, then leave it and go cross-country up the east slopes (firm snow early season, loose talus after melt-out) to the ESE ridge at about 7,050 ft. A good boot path follows the ridge to the summit.
wa_fortune_peak_standard_route: From I-90 Exit 85 east of Cle Elum, take SR-970 to Teanaway Road and follow the North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends at 29 Pines Campground, take the right fork, FR 9737, about 10 miles to its end at the Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (about 4,270 ft). A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Follow the Esmeralda Basin Trail #1394, staying on it where Ingalls Way branches right early on. Higher in the basin, turn right onto the trail toward Lake Ann and switchback up to the saddle above the lake. From the saddle a climbers' boot path follows the ridge north, on or just right of the crest, gaining about 800 ft in half a mile to the summit; expect loose rock and lingering snow early in the season.
wa_full_tilt_tempest_wall_free_version: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, take Icicle Creek Road 8.4 miles and turn left onto FR 7601. Follow the bumpy dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end (about 3,400 ft). A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a self-issued day-use permit; overnight camping at Colchuck Lake needs an Enchantments permit.

Take Trail #1599, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. At the junction where the Stuart Lake trail continues, take the Colchuck Lake Trail, recross the creek on a second log bridge, and climb steep, rocky trail to the north end of the lake at about 5,560 ft, 4 miles from the car.

Follow the trail along the lakeshore to the boulder field at the south end, then take the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' path up talus and heather to about 400 ft above the lake. Cut climber's left through 15-20 minutes of slide alder and heather to the gully below Colchuck Balanced Rock; Full Tilt starts a few hundred feet down the gully, right of the West Face start, after a loose 3rd/4th-class scramble. Five pitches lead to the summit ridge.
wa_gorillas_direct: Follow the Esmeralda Basin Trail a short way and turn right onto Ingalls Way #1390. It switchbacks up past several waterfalls; stay on it where the Longs Pass trail branches right, and continue to Ingalls Pass at about 6,500 ft.

Follow the trail through Headlight Basin and past Ingalls Lake toward Stuart Pass, then take the climbers' trail onto the talus shoulder below the West Ridge and contour to the amphitheater midway between Stuart Pass and Goat Pass. The route starts at a splitter crack on a ledge 15-25 ft above the snow and climbs the roughly 1,000 ft West Face Wall to the upper West Ridge; follow the ridge to the summit.
wa_greenwood_mountain_west_ridge: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR-207 north, turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200). Follow it about 22 miles, the last half on rough dirt, then turn right at the signed Phelps Creek turnoff and climb FR 6211 about 2 miles to the Phelps Creek Trailhead at the road end (about 3,500 ft). High clearance helps on these roads.
wa_helmet_butte_standard_route: From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north about 4 miles and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then after 1.3 miles turn left onto Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 62). Follow it about 22 miles and keep left at the final junction to the Trinity Trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued wilderness permit are needed. The road has been closed below the trailhead at times, so check its status first.

Hike the Buck Creek Pass trail about 8.8 miles to roughly 5,600 ft. Just after the main stream crossing, take the unmarked path breaking right (ignore the false trail before it) and follow it north as it braids, staying uphill, to Pass No Pass near 6,380 ft. Turn sharply left and traverse uphill to the southwest to the summit block, and take it by easy rock on its south side rather than the false south summit beside it.
wa_hoodoo_peak_sawtooth_scramble: Follow Libby Creek Trail No. 415 southwest through mixed conifer, crossing small tributaries on logs or rocks, about 1.4 miles to a spring in the patchy burn scar.
Continue climbing on the trail about 0.3 mile to the signed Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness boundary.
Keep on Trail No. 415 through mixed burned and live forest to the ford of the North Fork of Libby Creek, with an established campsite on the far bank. This is the last reliable water.

Continue up Trail No. 415 to the decaying old cabin standing in the trail at roughly 4.5 to 5 miles. There is no sign; the cabin is the junction. Going straight past it leads to Libby Lake, which is not on this route.

Take the faint boot path leaving to the right of the cabin into open forest. It gives out in a large clearing, from which the ridge is visible to the north; cross scree and lingering snow patches to the foot of the boulder field.

There is no defined line and no cairns: pick a way up the loose boulder field to gain the ridge crest, then follow the crest north, boulder-hopping on Class 2 ground with an occasional Class 3 move. Traverse climber's right of the summit spire and hook around it rather than climbing it head on. Test blocks before weighting them.
wa_iron_peak_teanaway_scramble: From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. After 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road, and where the pavement ends keep right onto Forest Road 9737. Continue up the road toward Esmeralda Basin; Trail 1399 leaves the right side of the road about half a mile past De Roux Campground, at about 3,800 ft. Parking is roadside, with no pass, water or restrooms.
wa_king_kong_gorillas_direct_direct: Take Ingalls Way Trail No. 1390 from the parking area, passing the turnoff to Longs Pass, and follow it as it switchbacks steadily up past several waterfalls to Ingalls Pass, about 3 miles.
wa_leche_la_vaca: From US 2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 7601 and follow the bumpy dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park, and a free self-issued permit covers a day trip; overnight stays need an Enchantments permit.

Hike the Colchuck Lake Trail through forest along Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge near 1.5 miles. At the signed junction take the Colchuck Lake fork, then climb steepening rocky switchbacks and a boulder moraine to the lake, about 4 miles and 2,280 ft of gain. Fill water here.

Continue along the lake toward its south end onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail and climb talus and heather to about 400 ft above the lake. Cut climber's left through a dense band of slide alder and heather to the base gully below the rock, then scramble loose 3rd and 4th class terrain to the start on the left side of the wall, near Scarface. Five pitches lead to the summit block, the last a long traverse up and left.
wa_let_it_burn: From US 2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 7601 and follow the bumpy dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end, at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park, and a free self-issued permit covers a day trip; overnight stays need an Enchantments permit.

Hike the Colchuck Lake Trail through forest along Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge near 1.5 miles. At the signed junction take the Colchuck Lake fork, cross the creek again on a log bridge, then climb steepening rocky switchbacks and a boulder moraine to the lake outlet, about 4 miles and 2,280 ft of gain. Fill water here.
wa_lichtenberg_mountain_southeast_ridge: From the first major switchback on Smith Brook Road, pick up the Lichtenwasser Lake fishing trail, which leads roughly southeast and then south through forest to the lake at about 4,700 ft. In winter, leave the road at the hairpin near 3,970 ft, head southwest, then hold a bearing of about 177 degrees true to the lake.

From the south end of the lake, leave any path and climb southwest, on a bearing of about 248 degrees true, up open and lightly wooded slopes to the broad 5,640-ft saddle on the southeast ridge; this slope is the avalanche terrain on the route. Turn right (northwest) at the saddle and follow the ridge crest to the summit, with a little easy scrambling on blocky rock and cornices to watch for in winter.
wa_luahna_peak_east_slopes: From US 2 at Coles Corner, drive WA 207 north about 10.5 miles and turn right onto White River Road (FR 6400). Follow it about 10 miles to its end, passing Tall Timbers Ranch and keeping left at the unsigned fork beyond it, to the trailhead at about 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.
wa_luahna_peak_southwest_slope_southeast: From US 2 at Coles Corner, drive WA 207 north about 10.5 miles and turn right onto White River Road (FR 6400). Follow it about 10 miles to its end, passing Tall Timbers Ranch and keeping left at the unsigned fork beyond it, to the trailhead at about 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.
wa_martin_peak_west_ridge: There is no road to this trailhead. Take the Lake Chelan ferry from Chelan or Field's Point Landing up-lake to Lucerne Landing, then ride the Holden Village bus 11 miles up the gravel road into Holden Village, where the Railroad Creek Trail starts. Reserve the ferry ahead and confirm both the ferry and the bus are running before you plan the trip. A free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is required.

Follow Railroad Creek Trail #1256 about a mile up-valley to the fork, then take the Holden Lake Trail about four miles and 1,700 ft up to Holden Lake. Above the lake a climbers' path gains about 1,100 ft over heather benches to Holden Pass near 6,400 ft, the saddle between Bonanza and Martin. Go east straight up the ridge out of the pass, linking gullies on the right (south) side of the crest by cairns, to a steep Class 4 gully just below the summit.
wa_massie_peak_west_route: Walk the Chiwawa River Trail #1550 upstream through forest to the unsigned junction: a large boulder jutting into the trail on the east side, opposite an 'M' with an arrow carved into a tree on the west side. A false set of markers has existed about a mile short of the real one, so do not turn off on arrows alone.

The river is forded immediately below the junction, with piled driftwood the only help across. It can run thigh-deep and swift with early-season snowmelt, so cross in the morning when flows are lowest, and fill water here.

Across the river, pick up the old sheep-drive path, which climbs steeply for about 2 miles on axe and burn blazes and intermittent boot track to Massie Lake at about 5,900 ft. The blazes thin out with height and there is no reliable water on the way.
Follow the broad ridge crest to the summit over talus and heather, generally Class 2 with a few short Class 3 steps near the summit block. Shaded sections can hold snow and ice into midsummer.
wa_mcclellan_peak_southwest_scramble: Snow Lakes Trail #1553 crosses Icicle Creek and climbs steadily through forest up the Snow Creek drainage on long, relentless switchbacks to Nada Lake, with a loud creek just above it that is a reliable water source.
Continue past Nada Lake to Lower and Upper Snow Lakes. The crossing on the logjam between the two lakes is the known hazard here, worst at high water or on a pre-dawn start.

Above the Snow Lakes the tread becomes a rougher climbers' path that switchbacks steeply into the core Enchantments basin past Lake Viviane to Leprechaun Lake, near 7,000 ft. Leave the trail at the flat, open ground by Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes; there is no reliable water beyond the lakes.

Climb steep talus, scree or snow, often firm and icy late in the season, to the crest of McClellan Ridge, keeping west of the rock tower called the Prong; drifting farther west into the Chessman towers dead-ends.
