From the crest, drop a short way and wrap onto the south side of the peak, then scramble Class 3 rock to the summit.
wa_milk_n_honey: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the bumpy dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end. FS Road 7601 is typically closed November to May. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and day climbers fill out the self-issue Enchantment permit at the trailhead.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail up Mountaineer Creek through forest, crossing on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. At about 2.25 miles, take the Colchuck Lake Trail where it splits from the Stuart Lake Trail. It crosses Mountaineer Creek again on a log bridge, then climbs steep, rocky tread and a boulder moraine to the lake's outlet. This is the last water.

Follow the trail around the lake to the foot of Aasgard Pass and take the cairned climbers' path about 400 ft up steep talus and heather. Then break climber's left through 15 to 20 minutes of dense slide alder and heather to the gully system below the wall. Loose 3rd and 4th class scrambling leads to the base. Climb the route to the summit.
wa_mount_berge_southwest_route: Little Giant Trail #1518 reaches the unbridged ford of the Chiwawa River within the first tenth of a mile, and there is no way around it. Expect it waist-deep and swift in early season. It is reliably safe only in late-summer and fall low water.

Past the ford, climb Trail #1518's steep, badly eroded switchbacks, about 500 ft per mile at first and then a far steeper pitch, to a small spring a few hundred feet below Little Giant Pass. Fill up here: it is the last dependable water before the high basins.
Continue a few hundred feet up the trail to Little Giant Pass at 6,463 ft, where the maintained tread ends.
wa_mount_bigelow_scramble: Start up Eagle Lakes Trail #431 and cross Crater Creek on a bridge. Where the Crater Creek Trail #416 splits off, continue straight on #431.
Stay on Eagle Lakes Trail #431 as it climbs steadily through forest to an established campsite about halfway to the lakes.

Continue up #431 through subalpine fir and larch, past an overlook of Lower Eagle Lake, to a junction. The left branch goes to Lower Eagle Lake and Horsehead Pass. The Upper Eagle Lake spur, #431A, goes right.
Take the right-hand spur, Trail #431A, about half a mile up to Upper Eagle Lake. This is the last reliable water.

From the lake's northwest shore, climb northwest through the larch stand, staying right of the prominent rock wall above the lake. Veer right to a notch, then take easy slabby rock above the lower cliff band. Route-finding is tricky while snow lingers in the notch.

Above the lower band, traverse left beneath the next cliff band rather than drifting right onto the better rock, which cliffs out at the end of the ridge. Then climb steep, loose scree and rock to just below the summit block, where an exposed chimney step of about 8 ft and a sandy gully guard the finish.
Climb the chimney step and the sandy gully to the saddle. The top holds on the step are poor, set in sand and small pebbles. From the saddle, turn right and follow the easy ridge to the true summit.
wa_mount_fernow_southeast_face: Hike up-valley on Phelps Creek Trail #1511, mostly flat maintained tread through forest, to the Glacier Peak Wilderness boundary.
Continue on the flat, forested Phelps Creek Trail about another mile to where it meets Leroy Creek. A large waterfall is visible up-valley. This is the last easy water before the basin.

Ford Leroy Creek and leave the maintained trail for the unsigned but well-beaten climbers' path on the creek's north side. It climbs very steeply, about 2,000 ft in 1.5 to 1.9 miles, into Leroy Basin at about 6,100 ft, a heather-and-boulder cirque with good tent sites and running water.

From camp, go cross-country up heather benches, meadow and rock to the notch on Seven Fingered Jack's ridge, roughly an hour. Cairns are sparse and Fernow is not visible from the basin, so navigate by map and GPS.

Drop about 1,000 ft off the far side of the notch to the loose, rocky moraine at the foot of the Gloomy Glacier. This crossing is avalanche terrain early in the season. Every foot of the descent has to be regained on the way out.

Cross beneath the glacier remnant, where open crevasses have been reported, so rope up or give it a wide berth. Then climb onto the broad, very loose talus and scree below the summit. The narrow band of solid slabs near the snowmelt seeps gives the firmest footing.

Keep climbing mostly class 2-3 talus. Take care on the exposed traverse across a sloping, gravel-covered slab with a big drop below it. Above about 8,800 ft, steep class 3-4 choss leads to the summit block, then roughly 200 ft of exposed, loose class 4 scrambling through a narrow notch to the top.
wa_mount_howard_south_slope: From Stevens Pass, drive east on US-2 about 8.5 miles; from Leavenworth, drive about 26 miles west. Just past milepost 73, about 0.4 mile beyond the highway department buildings, turn north onto an inconspicuous, rutted dirt road to the Rock Mountain Trailhead. Parking is limited to a few cars, and there is no restroom. No pass or permit is required.

Climb the Rock Mountain Trail to the Nason Ridge Trail junction at about 3.2 miles and turn right toward Rock Lake. Continue past the lake and over the col, losing height to Crescent Lake, the last water. From its northeast side, go up the talus below the cliff band and through brush to an upper talus field. Drift right around the cliff, climb a loose Class 3 gully, then follow talus and paths to the summit.
wa_mount_lyall_south_route: There is no road in. Take the passenger ferry or a floatplane up Lake Chelan to Stehekin, then ride the valley shuttle up the Stehekin Valley Road to High Bridge, and plan around both timetables. You need a free self-issue wilderness permit but no parking pass.

Take the trail south up Agnes Creek to Swamp Creek Camp. Cross Swamp Creek on a log, turn uphill near 4,000 ft beside a side stream into the west basin, and work east below the peak. Go south along a larch-dotted scree slope to the 7,300-ft notch on the southwest ridge. Drop about 100 ft around the buttress, traverse beneath the white rock band, and climb the exposed Class 3 gully and loose boulders to the top.
wa_mount_mastiff_south_route: Hike the Merritt Lake Trail as it switchbacks up through forest for about 2.5 miles to Merritt Lake, where there are established campsites, a privy, and the last dependable water before the ridge.

Continue past the lake junction onto the Nason Ridge Trail and follow it north about a mile, watching for an unsigned boot path breaking off uphill toward the peak's south slopes. There is no cairn, post or blaze; if the trail starts losing height toward Lost Lake, you have passed the turn and should come back.

Follow the boot path steeply uphill through forest. Above treeline it fades into open heather and loose talus with no maintained tread and no water, so note landmarks for the descent, especially in fog.

Gain the ridge and climb it until it turns into a rocky, jagged crest. Follow the moat between rock and snow just to the left, stepping up onto the rock to cross ledges, wrap the big rock tower on its right side close to its base, then scramble dirt and ledges to a knoll and a final snowfield. The summit is broad and flat; the register sits off to the south of the flat area rather than on the high point.
wa_mount_maude_r1: Walk the Phelps Creek Trail #1511 up the valley, the same tread used for Spider Meadow, about 3.5 nearly flat miles to Leroy Creek near 4,140 ft. Cross on a large log or by rock-hopping; it is awkward in early season when the creek runs high.

On the north side of the creek pick up the unsigned but well-worn climbers' trail, which climbs steeply at roughly 1,200 ft per mile and then eases into the Leroy Basin meadows at about 6,100 ft, with good camping and water.

Climb cross-country above the basin over meadow, scrub, talus and usually snow to the col between Seven Fingered Jack and Maude, northwest of the summit. From the col descend about 400 ft toward the Entiat side in alternating downclimbs and traverses until the face comes into full view, then climb it at 35 to 45 degrees, favoring the rib on the right to stay clear of the cornice, and walk the summit ridge to the top.
wa_mount_maude_r2: From US-2 at Coles Corner, about 20 miles east of Stevens Pass, turn north on SR 207. Just past the bridge over the Wenatchee River turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto the Chiwawa River Road, FR 62, and follow it more than 20 miles as it turns to rough gravel. Turn right onto Phelps Creek Road, FR 6211, and drive about 2 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,500 ft. Fill out a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit at the trailhead.

Hike the Phelps Creek Trail about 3.5 miles to Leroy Creek, climb the climbers' trail on its north side into Leroy Basin, and continue to a bivy on ledges above the south side of Ice Lake. Traverse talus to the access notch at about 7,200 ft (not the decoy notch near 6,900 ft), rope up and descend onto the Entiat Glacier, cross its ablation zone below the rock spur, and climb the icefall and about 900 ft of fourth- and low-fifth-class rock to the summit.
wa_mount_maude_r3: From US-2 at Coles Corner, about 20 miles east of Stevens Pass, turn north on SR 207. Just past the bridge over the Wenatchee River turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto the Chiwawa River Road, FR 62, and follow it more than 20 miles as it turns to rough gravel. Turn right onto Phelps Creek Road, FR 6211, and drive about 2 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,500 ft. Fill out a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit at the trailhead.

Hike the Phelps Creek Trail about 3.5 miles to the Leroy Creek ford, then climb the steep climbers' trail on the north side of the creek into Leroy Basin at about 6,100 ft. Traverse onto the peak's west side and take the second gully right of the north tower: its shallow right fork, a brief Class 4 step right into the next couloir, and slabby Class 3 to the ridge crest. Then traverse south, passing towers on the west side, to the summit.
wa_mount_stuart_girth_pillar: From US-2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road, FR 7601, and follow the rough, potholed dirt road about 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end. The road is closed in winter, typically November into May. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park, and Enchantment permit rules apply: a free self-issued day permit, or a quota permit to stay overnight.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek past the Colchuck Lake junction and leave it where it turns uphill for Stuart Lake. Cross the creek and follow the climbers' path up the valley to the basin under the Ice Cliff and Sherpa glaciers, camping in the basin or on the moraine. Climb the Ice Cliff Glacier, keeping left of the icefall, then the ice cliff step, four moderate rock pitches, the pillar's crack pitches and easier ground past the false summit to the top.
wa_mount_stuart_ice_cliff_glacier: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake junction and stay right for Stuart Lake. About a mile to a mile and a half farther, the trail turns uphill and begins switchbacking away from Mountaineer Creek; that turn is where you leave it and stay low in the valley bottom on the climbers' path.

Gain the moraine and follow it to the toe of the North Ridge at about 6,600 ft, then cut hard left and traverse beneath the ice cliff without stopping. Pass the icefall on whichever flank is in condition, cross the cirque and the bergschrund to the couloir, and climb about 1,000 ft of it, taking the right fork, to the cornice exit near 8,600 ft. Traverse south of the false summit and follow the ridge to the top.
wa_mount_stuart_stuart_glacier_couloir: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail up the Mountaineer Creek valley about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake junction, near 4,500 ft.

Stay right on the Stuart Lake Trail rather than turning left for Colchuck Lake, and continue about a mile. Where the trail turns uphill and starts switchbacking away from the creek, leave it and stay in the valley bottom on the unmaintained climbers' path; it is often snow-covered and poorly marked in spring.

From the basin, continue west around the far side of the North Ridge rock rib onto the Stuart Glacier, watching for crevasses, and climb the glacier to the foot of the couloir at about 7,800 ft. The North Ridge should be on your left; if a hanging ice cliff is above you, you are still on the Ice Cliff side.

Cross the bergschrund, belaying it if the snow is sugary, and climb the 40 to 50 degree couloir as it narrows to a short steep step of ice or verglas, then a second shorter step. Above, the gully widens into a snowfield; climb a couple hundred feet of 50 degree snow to the notch on the upper West Ridge.

From the notch, drop about 10 ft onto the south side and follow ledges along the south flank of the ridge, then climb mid-fifth-class rock and a diagonal traverse into a gully that leads back to the crest. Class 3 ledges and short cracks lead to the summit block; a short 5.6 lieback near the top can be bypassed by a traverse. Expect rime and ice on the ledges early in the season.
wa_mount_stuart_the_gendarme: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road (FR 7600) and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and day parties fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail past the Colchuck Lake junction, leave it where it starts switchbacking, and follow the Mountaineer Creek valley to the basin below the Sherpa and Ice Cliff glaciers. Climb the North Ridge from its toe, or the upper ridge from the notch above the Stuart Glacier, to the Great Gendarme about 500 ft below the summit. Climb its two pitches or bypass it on ledges to the west, then continue up the ridge to the top.
wa_mount_stuart_west_ridge: From the signed Longs Pass junction on the Ingalls Way Trail, near 5,440 ft, turn right and climb steep, rocky, sparsely switchbacked trail about 1.2 miles to the pass, which gives the first clear view of Stuart's west side.

From the notch at the top of the approach gully, Long John Tower is directly ahead; pass it by the chimney on its left, or by the short dihedral with a fixed piton or the layback farther along the ledge, then regain the crest. Cross the exposed West Ridge Notch traverse, and higher up climb the 5.4 dihedral or 5.6 layback below the summit to easier fifth-class ground and the top.
wa_needle_peak_north_ridge: No road reaches Stehekin. Take the passenger ferry up Lake Chelan from Chelan or Fields Point Landing to Stehekin, then ride the shuttle bus up the Stehekin Valley Road to High Bridge, where the Pacific Crest Trail crosses the Stehekin River.

Follow the Pacific Crest Trail south up Agnes Creek about 8.5 to 9 miles to Swamp Creek Camp. Take the unmaintained Swamp Creek path and leave it near 3,200 ft, climbing steep, brushy slopes onto Needle Peak's long north ridge. Follow the ridge, turning cliff bands near 7,300 ft on the west, to the summit ridge and the broad summit.
wa_north_gardner_mountain_nw_couloir: From Winthrop, drive about 17 miles west on SR 20 (or about 115 miles east from Burlington) and turn south on FR 200, signed for Cedar Creek. Drive 0.8 mile to the trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issued wilderness permit is available at the trailhead.
wa_north_gardner_mountain_southwest: From SR 20 in Winthrop, turn onto White Avenue just after the bridge over the Methow River; it becomes Twin Lakes Road. At 1.3 miles turn right onto Wolf Creek Road, follow it 2.9 miles, then turn left onto Wildflower Road, which becomes FS Road 5005 in about half a mile. Follow the signs to the Wolf Creek Trail at the road end, about 4 miles on.

Follow Wolf Creek Trail #527 about 10 miles up the valley, crossing the North Fork of Wolf Creek and passing the Abernathy Lake junction, to Gardner Meadows. Leave the trail at the stream coming down from the north and climb its west bank to a small meadow basin near 6,200 ft, then work around gullies and cliff bands into the scree bowl below Point 8,487 and follow the ridge north past that false summit to the top.
wa_north_star_mountain_cloudy_peak_trave: Cloudy Pass is on Trail #1256, which climbs west from Lower Lyman Lake through open forest and meadows. Lyman Lake is reached up Railroad Creek from Holden Village, or from Phelps Creek over Spider Gap and down past the Upper Lyman Lakes.

From the pass, turn right and follow the ridge northeast up to Cloudy Peak (7,915 ft). Beyond it, lose elevation off its east side, either down the east ridge with some Class 3-4 or by dropping south of the summit around a cliff band, to reach the talus slopes that connect to North Star. Follow them northeast to the final 100 ft of rock to the summit, which is slick with lichen when wet.
wa_northeast_buttress_4: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, take Icicle Creek Road 8.5 miles and turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy dirt road about 4 miles to the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, the road is closed in winter, and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead.
wa_northwest_arete: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, take Icicle Creek Road 8.5 miles and turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy dirt road about 4 miles to the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, the road is closed in winter, and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead.
Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up the Mountaineer Creek valley, crossing the creek on a log footbridge, then switchback up to the signed fork where the trail flattens.
Stay right on the Stuart Lake Trail rather than turning onto the Colchuck Lake Trail. Continue to about 4,700 ft, where a faint boot path leaves the trail toward Mountaineer Creek.

Follow the faint path over and down to Mountaineer Creek, up the creek to about 4,780 ft, then bushwhack to a boulder field below Argonaut. Traverse the boulders south-southwest on cairns and cut through slide alder, keeping to talus on climber's right where you can, then climb through trees, talus and dry creek beds past waterfall slabs into the north basin.
Climb out of the basin onto the steep granite slab at the foot of the snow finger. It is slick and exposed when wet, icy or partly snow-covered.

Continue up into the snow finger, which steepens past 40 degrees near its top. Carry an axe and crampons: it can be firm or icy late in the season, with loose, dirty rock where the snow has pulled back.
Finish up the top of the snow finger to the small col at the very foot of the Northwest Arete, where the roped climbing starts.

Climb about seven pitches of blocky Class 4 to 5.6 up the arete. The crux is a flake taken au cheval followed by one insecure move to a good ledge; above it, take the right-hand of two corners, then traverse left off it to reach the summit ridge and the west summit, the true high point.
wa_nw_ridge_2: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, take Icicle Creek Road 8.5 miles and turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy dirt road about 4 miles to the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, the road is closed in winter, and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead.

Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up the Mountaineer Creek valley, crossing the creek on a log footbridge, then switchback up to the signed fork where the Colchuck Lake Trail splits from the Stuart Lake Trail.
Take the Colchuck Lake Trail across the creek and up steep switchbacks to the north end of Colchuck Lake, the last water on the route.

Work around the eastern shoreline and talus to the obvious gully that splits toward the notch above Jabberwocky Tower. Climb it (loose, holding steep snow into July, with rope-up terrain near the top) to the notch, step onto Class 3 ground on the NW Ridge, then climb several pitches of low fifth class to 5.6 along the exposed crest to the summit area and the short, very exposed boulder problem on the top block.
wa_pinnacle_mountain_entiat_scramble: From US 97A in Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19) at the bridge and drive about 32 miles up the valley; it becomes FS Road 51 along the way. Turn onto FS Road 5606 and follow it about 3 miles to the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is available at the trailhead.
wa_prusik_peak_der_sportsman: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough, potholed dirt road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park; day trips need the free self-issued Enchantments day-use permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a quota permit.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles, turn right onto the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and switchback to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the south end climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree, then cross the upper Core past Tranquil and Isolation Lakes and go cross-country over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn, about 20 minutes below the south face.

Start about 50 ft left of the standard South Face line, on an easy left-slanting crack leading to a stembox; the 5.11+ crux comes on the first pitch, which ends at a two-bolt anchor. Six pitches of crack and corner climbing follow, finishing in a chimney with a loose block before the top.
wa_prusik_peak_solid_gold: Hike the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the signed Colchuck Lake Trail junction, turn right, cross Mountaineer Creek and switchback 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. Boulder-hop the east shore to the boulder field at the south end, then climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft in 1.25 miles of loose scree and dirt, staying climber's left of the cliff bands, to the 7,841-ft pass.
From the pass, drop gently east into the upper Core past Tranquil and Isolation Lakes and follow the cairned path down through the chain of lakes to the camps in the central basin.

Leave the main basin path and scramble north over granite slabs on a faint path toward Prusik Pass and Gnome Tarn, then traverse to the left end of the south face. Solid Gold starts just right of the outside corner where the face turns onto the west side, on a right-leaning crack system leading to a stembox.

Climb five pitches, about 450 ft: right-leaning cracks to a roof, a hand crack, slab and a chimney with some loose rock, then a finishing corner crack. The route tops out on the West Ridge below the true summit, not on the summit itself.
wa_prusik_peak_south_face_burgner_stanle: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough, potholed dirt road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park; day trips need the free self-issued Enchantments day-use permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a quota permit.
wa_prusik_peak_west_ridge: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough, potholed dirt road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park; day trips need the free self-issued Enchantments day-use permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a quota permit.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the signed Colchuck Lake Trail junction, turn right, cross Mountaineer Creek and switchback 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. Boulder-hop the east shore to the boulder field at the south end, then climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft in 1.25 miles of loose scree and dirt, staying climber's left of the cliff bands, to the 7,841-ft pass.
From the pass, drop gently east into the upper Core past Tranquil and Isolation Lakes and follow the cairned path down through the chain of lakes to the camps in the central basin.
From the basin camps, take the path toward Prusik Pass that leaves the west shore of Perfection Lake and climb north over granite to the pass, where the West Ridge begins.

Climb about four pitches: a long first pitch up a wide crack in a band of white rock onto the crest, then along the ridge to a slung-block belay below the 5.7 friction-slab crux with an old fixed pin, and a finishing pitch by a finger crack or a 5.7 off-width to the summit.
wa_raven_ridge_southeast_ridge_crater_la: From Twisp, take SR 20 southeast about 2 miles to SR 153 and follow it south about 12 miles to Gold Creek Loop Road (County Road 1029), then turn onto Gold Creek Road (County Road 1034), which becomes FS Road 4340. About 6 miles up, turn left onto FS Road 4340-300 (Crater Creek Road) and drive about 4.5 miles to the Crater Creek Trailhead at about 4,750 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required.

Start on Eagle Lakes Trail #431 and after about 0.7 mile, just beyond the bridge over Crater Creek, take Crater Creek Trail #416, which climbs steeply about 3.3 miles to Crater Lake. Above the lake there is no trail: follow the southeast ridge northwest to a col near 8,000 ft, keeping to the crest out of the loose flanking gullies, then scramble talus and boulders along the crest past false summits to the summit.
wa_raven_ridge_standard_route: From Twisp, take SR 20 east about 3 miles to SR 153 and follow it south to Libby Creek Road (County Road 1045), about 1.4 miles south of Carlton. Follow Libby Creek Road about 2.5 miles, turn left onto FS Road 43 for about 5 miles, left onto FS Road 4340 for about 1.2 miles, right onto FS Road 4340-700 for 1.5 miles, then left onto FS Road 4340-750 to its end at about 4,430 ft. Roadside parking for about ten cars; no toilet or water.

Follow Libby Creek Trail #415 about 5 miles, through a burned section, across the North Fork of Libby Creek and past an old cabin near 7,170 ft, to Libby Lake at about 7,640 ft. From the south end of the lake climb the narrower right-hand of two loose gullies, move left onto the firmer rib near 8,200 ft to reach the crest, then scramble east about half a mile over false summits to the eastern high point.
wa_reynolds_peak_scramble: From Twisp, drive west up the Twisp River Road (FR 44) for 18.3 miles and bear left onto FR 4435. Cross the Twisp River in 0.3 mile, turn right after the bridge to stay on FR 4435, drive 1.1 miles upriver and turn left onto Spur 4435-015, reaching the trailhead in another 0.3 mile at about 3,100 ft. A free self-issued Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

Follow Reynolds Creek Trail #402 up the north side of Reynolds Creek through forest for about 2.8 miles to around 4,800 ft, where the South Fork valley comes in from the south. The trail is primitive and sees little maintenance, so expect deadfall.
Climb scree, talus and, early in the season, snow up the gully out of the basin to the saddle on the ridge above. The gully often holds snow well into summer; carry an axe.

From the saddle, move into the loose gully that splits the summit block and climb it toward the notch in the crest. This is the Class 3-4 crux, with real exposure and rock that is sometimes snow-covered.
Scramble the exposed summit rocks to the true summit, the southern of the two horns. The lower north peak across the notch is not the high point.
wa_rikki_tikki_tavi: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow it about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead. FR 7601 is gated closed from late fall through spring.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles, and take the left fork onto the Colchuck Lake Trail at the junction. Climb the final boulder moraine to the lake's outlet at its north end, about 4 miles and 2,300 ft from the car. Fill water here.

Follow the trail counter-clockwise around the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. At about 400 ft above the lake, cut climber's left through dense slide alder and heather into the gully below the west face and scramble loose 3rd and 4th class ground to the base, then climb the route's five pitches to the summit ridge.
wa_saska_peak_emerald_saska_col: From US 97A at Entiat, turn onto Entiat River Road (County Road 19, which becomes FR 51) and drive 32.3 miles to FR 5606; if you reach North Fork Campground you have gone too far. Follow FR 5606 for 3 miles to the road end at about 3,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is self-issued at the kiosk.
wa_scarface_3: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow it about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead. FR 7601 is gated closed from late fall through spring.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles, and take the left fork onto the Colchuck Lake Trail at the junction. Climb the final boulder moraine to the lake's outlet at its north end, about 4 miles and 2,300 ft from the car. Fill water here.

Follow the trail counter-clockwise around the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. At about 400 ft above the lake, cut climber's left through dense slide alder and heather to the gully system below the west face; the start is the gully just left of the West Face route, very loose and exposed. Climb the route's six pitches to the summit ridge.
wa_sherpa_balanced_rock_ne_couloir: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow it about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; day trips self-issue an Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a quota permit. FR 7601 is gated closed from late fall through spring.

Take Trail #1599, keep right for Stuart Lake at the Colchuck fork, and leave the trail at the first switchback past the beaver meadows. Cross the outlet on logs and follow the unmaintained path south up Mountaineer Creek, taking the climber's-left branch into the Sherpa-Argonaut basin near 5,800 ft. Climb about 1,000 ft of scree into the couloir, up it to the notch on the east ridge, then ledges and one short 5.0 pitch to the top.
wa_sherpa_balanced_rock_standard: Reached from the Esmeralda (Longs Pass) trailhead over Longs Pass, down to Ingalls Creek and up the climbers' path into the Sherpa-Argonaut basin. From Table Rock in the basin, a short Class 3 scramble up heather and boulder slopes gains the notch on the crest east of the balanced rock.

Follow the crest west over blocks and sandy, exposed benches (Class 3-4) to the foot of the detached pillar. The pedestal at its base cannot be climbed unaided: gain it with a shoulder stand off a partner or a rope thrown over its point, then clip the fixed piton above.
From the pedestal ledge, climb bolt-protected 5.7 friction to the flat top of the block.
wa_sherpa_glacier: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR 7601) and follow it 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake trailhead at the road end, about 3,400 ft. The road is usually closed November through May. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; day trips self-issue an Enchantment day-use permit and overnight stays need an Enchantment quota permit.

Hike the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) along Mountaineer Creek and stay right toward Lake Stuart at the Colchuck Lake junction at about 2.2 miles. Leave the trail near the meadow and head southwest up the south fork of Mountaineer Creek; after a couple of miles a steep talus and boulder slope leads into the hanging valley beneath Sherpa Peak, and the lower snowfield above it leads to the glacier toe.

Rope up and climb the glacier southwest toward the obvious couloir in its northwest corner, weaving around crevasses. Cross the bergschrund where the glacier narrows and climb the 40 to 45 degree couloir up and right to the notch at its top.
wa_sherpa_peak_east_ridge: From the lot, follow the Esmeralda Basin trail 0.3 mile and turn right onto the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). Climb about 1.4 miles to the junction at about 5,440 ft, turn right onto the Longs Pass trail, and switchback steeply up open, rocky slopes about 1.2 miles to the pass.

Drop steeply off the north side of the pass on the boot path, about 1,400 ft, to Ingalls Creek; ford or rock-hop it and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail east about a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike junction. Leave the trail on the climbers' path up through timber and brush, climb the rib staying left of its crest, and at about 5,800 ft traverse right over the rib into the basin below Sherpa.

From the basin, angle climber's left (east) across a grassy slope and climb the talus and scree gully to the notch about 600 ft below and east of the summit. If you find yourself in a higher basin southwest of the summit, you have gone too far.

Gain the ridge crest on class 2 ground just past the notch, then follow the ridge west over class 3 and 4 blocks with some low fifth-class moves to the summit. Fixed slings sit at several obstacles; a 50m rope is enough.
wa_sherpa_peak_west_ridge: From the lot, follow the Esmeralda Basin trail 0.3 mile and turn right onto the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). Climb about 1.4 miles to the junction at about 5,440 ft, turn right onto the Longs Pass trail, and switchback steeply up open, rocky slopes about 1.2 miles to the pass.

Drop steeply off the north side of the pass on the boot path, about 1,400 ft, to Ingalls Creek; ford or rock-hop it and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail east about a mile to the Beverly-Turnpike junction. Leave the trail on the climbers' path up through timber and brush, climb the rib staying left of its crest, and at about 5,800 ft traverse right over the rib into the basin below Sherpa.

Climb class 2 snow and talus up the basin past the flat table-rock shelf at about 7,400 ft to the notch at the west foot of the ridge, on the col between Stuart and Sherpa; aim for the notch closest to Sherpa.

Climb blocky class 4 ridge trending climber's left to a cave belay, then take the crack out of the cave (the crux, about 5.4 to 5.5). Continue left to a platform with a rappel anchor, scramble across a short gully, climb to the lowest point of the summit ridge, and follow it on exposed class 4 to the summit block.
wa_sherpa_peak_north_ridge: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR 7601) and follow it 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake trailhead at the road end, about 3,400 ft. The road is usually closed November through May. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; day trips self-issue an Enchantment day-use permit and overnight stays need an Enchantment quota permit.
wa_south_headwall: From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east 7 miles and turn left on Teanaway Road. After 7.1 miles bear right onto the North Fork Teanaway Road; where the pavement ends 5.9 miles later, keep right on FR 9737. Stay left at the Beverly Campground fork, keep right at the fork signed Trail 1394, and drive to the Esmeralda trailhead at the road end, about 9.5 miles of gravel. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued wilderness permit are required.

From the lot, follow the Esmeralda Basin trail 0.3 mile and turn right onto the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). Climb about 1.4 miles to the junction at about 5,440 ft, turn right onto the Longs Pass Trail (#1229), and switchback steeply up open, rocky slopes about 1.2 miles to the pass.

Drop the steep, eroded boot path off the north side of the pass to Ingalls Creek, cross it, and follow the Ingalls Creek Trail west to the first major clearing west of Ulrich's Couloir. Climb the clearing and the loose scree above it to the enclosed cirque at about 8,700 ft, then take about five pitches, none harder than 5.7, up the centre of the headwall, topping out just southwest of the true summit.
wa_southwest_rib_2: From US 97 between Leavenworth and Blewett Pass, about 7 miles south of the US 2 junction (near milepost 178), turn west onto Ingalls Creek Road. Cross Peshastin Creek, bear left, and drive to the trailhead at the road's end, about 1,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park; fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead.
wa_star_peak_sawtooth_nw_ridge: From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road about 10.7 miles and turn left onto Buttermilk Creek Road, crossing the Twisp River. Stay left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) and follow it roughly 4 miles, then turn right onto the Road 500 spur and follow it about 2.7 miles to the West Fork Buttermilk Creek trailhead at road's end, about 4,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park.

Hike Trail #411 up the West Fork Buttermilk Creek, fording the creek several times and passing long stretches of blowdown, to the trail's high point at 7,480-ft Fish Creek Pass. Do not descend to Star Lake; leave the trail at the pass, gain the ridge crest directly above it, and follow the knife-edge northwest ridge to its steep, loose final few hundred feet and the summit.
wa_star_peak_sawtooth_scramble: Follow Trail #411 up the West Fork Buttermilk Creek valley about a mile to the crossing of the West Fork. In high water look for the downed-log crossing about 100 ft upstream of the original ford; this is the last easy, reliable water for several miles.

Continue up Trail #411 through the old burn, where long stretches of blowdown interrupt the tread and further fords of the West Fork come early in the season, until the trail breaks out into the lowest larches at about 6,800 ft.
Keep climbing through open larch country to Fish Creek Pass at 7,480 ft, the high point of the trail and the first clear view of Star Lake and the Star Peak massif.
From the pass the trail drops slightly for about half a mile into the Star Lake basin at about 7,460 ft. Camp at least 200 ft from the lakeshore.

Pick up the climber's path out of the basin and follow it as it switchbacks about 600 ft up steep, loose scree to the notch just west of Point 7912; the rocky point beside the notch confirms it is the right one. If snow still fills the bowl the path vanishes, so navigate to the notch.

From the notch, turn onto the peak's southwest ridge, where broken blocky rock and sandy patches replace the scree, and rock-hop through large, unstable talus. Stay on or near the established line rather than dropping into the steeper loose gullies below it.
Follow the ridge to the summit, with a little easy hands-and-feet scrambling on the final approach. Descend the same line; do not shortcut down the unstable boulder field on the peak's east side.
wa_switchback_mountain_scramble: From Twisp, take SR 20 east about 2 miles and continue south on SR 153 about 12 miles, then turn right onto Gold Creek Loop Road and follow it to Gold Creek Road. Drive Gold Creek Road about 5 miles, turn left onto Forest Road 4340-200, and follow it about 3.6 miles to the Foggy Dew Trailhead at road's end, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park.

Follow Foggy Dew Trail #417 up the valley on the north side of Foggy Dew Creek through pine and fir forest. At about 3.4 miles a steeper, switchbacking section passes Foggy Dew Falls, a two-tiered cascade in a narrow cleft and the last easy, reliable water before the open basins.
From Cooney Lake, fill water and continue up the trail for roughly another mile on open larch and scree slopes to Cooney Pass, the 7,900-ft saddle on Switchback's southeast side.

Leave the tread where it meets the broad southeast ridge and follow the easy crest toward the summit on open rock and talus. Watch for the similar neighboring summit along the same crest; if you walk easy ridge for the better part of a mile you are heading for the wrong peak.
Continue up the crest as it steepens into a field of large, mostly stable blocks, with a few exposed class 3 steps possible in the last stretch to the 8,321-ft summit.
wa_the_direct_north_ridge_w_gendarme: Follow Trail #1599 past the Colchuck Lake fork (keep right). About a mile beyond, where the trail turns uphill and switchbacks right toward Stuart Lake, leave it and stay in the valley; cross Mountaineer Creek on logs and follow its south fork upstream, then climb steep talus into the hanging valley below Sherpa Peak. A faint path leads to the moraine; keep the Ice Cliff Glacier on your left to the lowest rock of the ridge.

Start from a big ledge with a small tree about 150 ft above the toe and climb the three hard opening pitches, then simul-climb up and right to the large notch at about 8,200 ft. Stay left of the crest, follow the exposed knife-edge to the Great Gendarme, climb its dihedral and offwidth, then traverse right back to the crest and finish up broken ground to the summit.
wa_the_scoop_2: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (Forest Road 7601) and follow the bumpy, potholed dirt road about 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at road's end, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued wilderness permit for a day trip.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge near 1.5 miles, to the junction where the Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A forks left. Take it across a second Mountaineer Creek crossing and up steepening, rocky switchbacks to the north end of Colchuck Lake, about 4 miles and 2,280 ft from the trailhead.

Cross the outlet below the small dam at the lake's north end and follow the climbers' path up and across the timbered hillside into the west cirque, then boulder-hop talus to the wall. The Scoop starts right of the West Face and the Tempest, left of Rikki Tikki Tavi; climb three pitches to Launch Ledge, the Scoop corner above it, and on to the summit block.
wa_the_tempest: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and follow it about 8.5 miles to the Bridge Creek Campground turnoff. Turn left onto FS Road 7601 and drive about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee and a self-issued Enchantments day-use permit are required; FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, usually November to May.

Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up the Mountaineer Creek valley, crossing the creek on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. At the signed junction at about 2.5 miles fork left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, then switchback up a boulder moraine to the outlet of Colchuck Lake at about 4 miles and 5,570 ft. Fill water here; there is none higher.

Follow the trail around the west shore of the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. Climb about 400 ft of talus and heather, then break climber's left through a dense band of slide alder and heather to the gully below the wall and scramble loose 3rd/4th class to the base. Climb the route's nine pitches to the summit block.
wa_the_tipping_point: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and follow it about 8.5 miles to the Bridge Creek Campground turnoff. Turn left onto FS Road 7601 and drive about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee and a self-issued Enchantments day-use permit are required; FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, usually November to May.

Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up the Mountaineer Creek valley, crossing the creek on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. At the signed junction at about 2.5 miles fork left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, then switchback up a boulder moraine to the outlet of Colchuck Lake at about 4 miles and 5,570 ft. Fill water here; there is none higher.

Follow the trail around the west shore of the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. Climb about 400 ft of talus and heather, then break climber's left through a dense band of slide alder and heather to the gully below the wall and scramble loose 3rd/4th class to the base. Climb the route, joining Let It Burn's upper pitches, to the short boulder problem onto the summit block.
wa_this_my_friend: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and follow it about 8.5 miles to the Bridge Creek Campground turnoff. Turn left onto FS Road 7601 and drive about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee and a self-issued Enchantments day-use permit are required; FS Road 7601 is closed in winter, usually November to May.

Follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up the Mountaineer Creek valley, crossing the creek on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. At the signed junction at about 2.5 miles fork left onto Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, then switchback up a boulder moraine to Colchuck Lake at about 4 miles and 5,570 ft.
Follow the trail along the west shore of the lake toward its south end, where the climbers' path toward Aasgard Pass leaves the shoreline and starts to climb.

Climb the cairned Aasgard Pass path steeply up talus and boulders, keeping to climber's left at the larch grove and again at the cliff band with the waterfall near 6,400 ft; do not follow side paths toward the waterfall. At about 7,250 ft the path crosses the largest braid of the creek draining the pass, the last water.
Continue up the path five to ten minutes past the crossing to between 7,300 and 7,400 ft, where the route leaves the trail.

Make a rising traverse right across loose, unstable scree to the base, about 300 ft below where the top of Aasgard Pass meets the toe of Dragontail; the route starts below the right side of the right-hand of two bushes on the first belay ledge. Climb the five pitches to the top of the East Face.

The route is not set up for rappel. Work south and west across broken 3rd/4th-class ground, descend a clean gully to a large ledge, then scramble southwest to walkable ground and join the standard Dragontail descent, following cairned, braided paths to the top of Aasgard Pass.
wa_tupshin_peak_scramble: No road reaches this trailhead from outside. Take the Lady of the Lake or Lady Express passenger ferry from Fields Point Landing up Lake Chelan to Stehekin Landing, then ride the Stehekin shuttle (or walk) about 4.4 miles up the valley road to Harlequin Bridge. Cross the bridge; the Stehekin River Trail starts at the south end of the airstrip. Plan around the boat schedule, since missing the last boat costs a night.
Follow the Stehekin River Trail down-valley through forest about 3 miles toward Weaver Point to the signed Devore Creek Trail junction, about half a mile before the campground.

Turn onto the Devore Creek Trail and switchback steeply up into the Glacier Peak Wilderness, continuing up the Devore Creek valley to Bird Creek Camp at about 4,200 ft, the only designated camp on this stretch. Above here the trail is brushy and can carry heavy blowdown.

Leave the maintained trail and work up the ridge north of Bird Creek through steep brush, slide alder and blowdown, about 1,000 ft or more of gain with little open forest, to a camp with running water in the lower Bird Creek basin, roughly 5,400 to 5,800 ft.

Traverse around the cliff bands into the upper basin on the east side of the peak, to the talus fan at the foot of the continuous cliff band, marked by a snow finger at the bottom of the wall that lingers most summers. Carry an axe early in the season.

Kick up the snow finger to the ramp system and scramble rambly, loose rock, including a short class 4 step of about 20 ft, up the summit pyramid to the low-fifth chimney and flake. Wear a helmet; the rock releases on its own.
Climb the short 5.2-5.4 chimney/flake past a small chockstone on sparse protection, then scramble class 3-4 gully ground through a notch in the final rock band to the small, exposed true summit.
wa_union_peak_se_route: Start up Smithbrook Trail #1590 from the lot; a tributary of Rainy Creek crosses the trail about 0.2 mile in. It is the only reliable water on the route, so fill up here.
Continue up the trail as it switchbacks through old growth, about a mile from the trailhead, to the saddle at Union Gap, where it ends at the Pacific Crest Trail.

Walk north on the PCT a short distance and take the first path breaking left off it at a standing dead snag about 10 ft tall. Follow the line of cairns set out from the snag north to the high point of the boulder field.
From the top of the boulder field, climb the steep, brush-choked slope to gain the southeast ridge at about 5,200 ft. The brush is very slick when wet, and the slope is avalanche-prone in snow.
Follow the southeast ridge crest northwest to the summit; the line is obvious once on the crest.
wa_witches_tower_south_face: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up through forest along Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles. About 2.5 miles from the trailhead, bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail; the right fork continues to Lake Stuart.

Cross the creek on a second log bridge just past the junction, then climb through a boulder-filled talus slope and increasingly steep, rocky switchbacks to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead. Fill up here; it is the last reliable water before Aasgard Pass.

Follow the rough path along the lake's west shore, boulder-hopping in places, to its south end. Then climb the loose, eroded boot track up Aasgard Pass, roughly 2,200 ft in under a mile of scree and talus that often holds snow or ice into July; an ice axe is advisable.
From the pass, head south across talus, often over a lingering snow patch, to the west shore of Brynhild Lake.
Leave the west shore of the lake and work up talus, or snow early in the season, toward the tower to reach its base.

Swing around behind the tower to its south side, scramble up toward the band of white rock, take the airy ledge around onto the east side, then climb the large black blocks to the top. The true summit is across a four-foot slot that has to be jumped; nothing is harder than Class 3.
wa_witches_tower_southwest_corner: Turn off US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy, potholed dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at the road end, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek, and about 2.5 miles in bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail. Cross the creek on a log bridge and climb through a talus slope and steepening switchbacks to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead. It is the last reliable water.

Follow the rough path along the lake's west shore to its south end, then climb the loose, eroded boot track up Aasgard Pass, roughly 2,200 ft in under a mile of scree and talus that often holds snow or ice into July.

From the pass, head south across talus toward the tower and climb snow or Class 2 rock to the col just southwest of it. From the col, climb the sharp ridge about 100 ft, step a few feet right onto the south face (Class 4), make the 5.5 step-up, climb a short face, then scramble to the summit, jumping a four-foot slot near the top.
wa_witches_tower_west_buttress: Turn off US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy, potholed dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at the road end, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 along Mountaineer Creek, and about 2.5 miles in bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail. Cross the creek on a log bridge and climb through a talus slope and steepening switchbacks to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead. It is the last reliable water.

Follow the rough path along the lake's west shore to its south end, then climb the loose, eroded boot track up Aasgard Pass, roughly 2,200 ft in under a mile of scree and talus that often holds snow or ice into July.

From the pass, head south across the basin to the col behind the tower, then cross a steep snowfield (ice axe essential) to the base of the buttress on the west side. Two pitches follow: mostly Class 4 on solid granite, a short Class 5 chimney partway up, and a friction section to the top.
wa_baring_mountain_east_face: In Baring, turn north off US 2 onto 635th Place NE, across from the store. Cross the railroad tracks, keep left at the junction just beyond, and follow the road as it becomes FS Road 6024, about 4.3 miles in all, to the Barclay Lake Trailhead at the road end, about 2,280 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_baring_mountain_northwest_ridge: In Baring, turn north off US 2 onto 635th Place NE, across from the store. Cross the railroad tracks, keep left at the junction just beyond, and follow the road as it becomes FS Road 6024, about 4.3 miles in all, to the Barclay Lake Trailhead at the road end, about 2,280 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Skip Trail 1055: walk the old logging road behind the toilet 0.3 mile to the first creek, where a cairn on the right marks a steep climbers' path that crosses the creek twice and climbs to the west ridge crest near 4,000 ft. Follow the crest east a mile, drop below the cliff bands on the south side, cross a wooded gully to the talus basin at 4,900 ft, climb the couloir to the 5,550 ft notch, then go north on easy Class 3 to the top.
wa_baring_mountain_oatmeal_man: From US 2 in Baring, directly across from the store, turn north onto 635th Place NE, cross the railroad tracks and keep left at the junction about 0.3 mile up, where the road becomes FS Road 6024. Follow the potholed gravel about 4 more miles to the Barclay Lake trailhead, with parking for about 20 cars and a vault toilet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_infinite_beauty: From I-90 Exit 80, drive through Roslyn and follow SR 903 north past Cle Elum Lake to Salmon La Sac, about 19 miles from Cle Elum. Just before the Salmon La Sac Campground entrance, turn right onto the gravel road to the Salmon La Sac trailhead, shared by the Waptus River and Cooper River trails. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit at the trail.

Hike Waptus River Trail 1310 about 9 miles to Waptus Lake and turn west (southbound) on the PCT toward its Waptus River bridge, where most parties camp. Shortly before the bridge, head northwest to a bench and pick up a faint fisherman's track up the east side of Shovel Creek to talus and the foot of the Mega Slab. Start at the slab's lowest point, climb to the southeast shoulder, then scramble to and climb the three-pitch summit block.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_se_mega_slab: From I-90 Exit 80, drive through Roslyn and follow SR 903 north past Cle Elum Lake to Salmon La Sac, about 19 miles from Cle Elum. Just before the Salmon La Sac Campground entrance, turn right onto the gravel road to the Salmon La Sac trailhead, shared by the Waptus River and Cooper River trails. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit at the trail.

Hike Waptus River Trail 1310 to Waptus Lake and turn west (southbound) on the PCT to a camp near its Waptus River bridge. From there follow the old, unmaintained path along Shovel Creek to the foot of the Mega Slab at about 3,700 ft. Climb the slab to the shoulder at about 6,700 ft, then cross the west side of the summit block on exposed scrambling and heather benches to a short, exposed final pitch with a chimney to the true summit.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_southwest_face: Follow the closed Middle Fork road and Dutch Miller Gap Trail 1030 up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie past Hardscrabble Horse Camp and Pedro Camp to Dutch Miller Gap at 5,000 ft. Northeast of the gap, go up the left-hand of two parallel gullies, about 1,000 ft of class 3-4 to a white fan of rock, then traverse right across heather and broken rock to the second notch northwest of the summit block. Three short pitches to 5.6 lead to the top.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_timeless_treasu: From I-90 Exit 80, drive through Roslyn and follow SR 903 north past Cle Elum Lake to Salmon La Sac, about 19 miles from Cle Elum. Just before the Salmon La Sac Campground entrance, turn right onto the gravel road to the Salmon La Sac trailhead, shared by the Waptus River and Cooper River trails. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit at the trail.

Hike Waptus River Trail 1310 about 9 miles to Waptus Lake and turn west (southbound) on the PCT to a camp near its Waptus River bridge. From camp, follow the faint track along Shovel Creek through forest to a bench around 3,400 ft, then hop talus to the foot of the Mega Slab at about 3,700 ft. Walk the base to the middle of the slab, climb it to the southeast shoulder, then take the three-pitch summit block to the top.
wa_big_snow_mountain_east_buttress: From I-90 Exit 34, follow 468th Ave SE north 0.6 mile and turn right onto the Middle Fork Road, FS Road 56. After about 12 miles, cross the large concrete bridge and turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, then drive about 6 rough, potholed miles to the locked gate at the Dingford Creek trailhead (1,400 ft). High clearance is recommended; the road beyond the gate is closed to vehicles.
wa_big_snow_mountain_east_ridge_hardscra: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.6 mile and turn right onto the Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12 miles, pass the large Middle Fork Trailhead lot, and bear right onto the rough, potholed gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Drive about 6 more miles to the gate at the Dingford Creek Trailhead, around 1,400 ft; high clearance is recommended. The road beyond the gate is closed to vehicles.
wa_big_snow_mountain_north_slope_dingfor: Take the Dingford Creek Trail #1005 from the gate, climbing steeply past Pumpkinseed Falls at about 1 mile, then more gently with several stream crossings to a fork at about 3 miles. Bear left at the fork (right goes to Hester Lake) and follow long, sometimes overgrown switchbacks to Myrtle Lake at about 3,800 ft, roughly 5.5 miles from the trailhead.

The maintained trail ends at Myrtle Lake. Bushwhack southeast through marsh and dense brush to the stream draining Big Snow Lake, then climb its steep, boulder-filled ravine between cliffs, boulder hopping at first and then class 3 scrambling on wet, mossy rock, to emerge at Big Snow Lake at about 4,900 ft.
From the shore of Big Snow Lake, follow the path to the right, working counterclockwise around neighboring Snowflake Lake just to the west and up onto the heather bench above it.

Follow the heather bench around Snowflake Lake to its end at the base of the slope, then go straight up the moderately steep stream gully, a snow couloir early in the season, on snow, talus and crumbly class 2-3 rock. Above the gully, easy snowfields and the upper rock fields lead up the northwest flank to the 6,680 ft summit.
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes: Follow the Denny Creek Trail #1014 up the valley past the waterfalls and up steeper switchbacks to Hemlock Pass, about 4 miles. At the crest of the pass turn right onto the ridge and hold a bearing of about 33 degrees, skirting cliff bands mainly on their left, to the plateau and meadow on the ridge. Continue up the ridge, keeping left (south) of the talus field, to the traverse on the south side of the west shoulder.

Traverse the south side of the west shoulder to the summit block, then scramble the loose rock on the left, or when snow-free go around the exposed north side. The first high point may be a false summit, with a short exposed traverse to the true top at 5,801 ft. Helmets are recommended.
wa_burnt_boot_peak_north_ridge: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE and turn right onto the Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12 miles past the Middle Fork Trailhead lot, bear right onto the rough gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and drive about 6 more miles to the gate at the Dingford Creek Trailhead. The road beyond the gate is closed to vehicles, so the old Dutch Miller Gap road end is reached by walking or biking the closed road east up the valley.
wa_cathedral_rock_northeast_buttress: Leave I-90 at Exit 80 and follow SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald and along Cle Elum Lake for about 14.8 miles to where the maintained road ends, then continue about 12.3 miles on the gravel Cle Elum Valley Road (FR 4330) and the short NF-153 spur to the Cathedral Rock trailhead for Trail #1345, at about 3,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Take Trail #1345 across the bridge over the Cle Elum River, entering the wilderness at about 0.5 mile, and climb through old growth past the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles to Nosh Nosh Wahtum, the lake at about 4,850 ft, 2.5 miles in.
Continue on Trail #1345 as it opens into meadows with Cathedral Rock ahead, climbing to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at 5,550 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead.

Walk north on the PCT for a couple of minutes, then cut across the meadow to a stand of trees where parties cache gear. Make a rising traverse under the east face, past meadows and across loose talus, to a short steep snowfield below the buttress. From its top exit left into the moat, simul-climb easy ground and a ledge system rightward to the crest, and climb about seven pitches (5.7) up the buttress to the summit.
wa_cathedral_rock_northeast_ridge_2003_v: Take Trail #1345 across the bridge over the Cle Elum River, entering the wilderness at about 0.5 mile, and climb through old growth past the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles to Nosh Nosh Wahtum, the lake at about 4,850 ft, 2.5 miles in.
Continue on Trail #1345 as it opens into meadows with Cathedral Rock ahead, climbing to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at 5,550 ft, about 4 miles from the trailhead.

Walk north on the PCT a couple of minutes, cut across the meadow to the stand of trees used as a gear cache, and traverse under the east face across talus to the short steep snowfield on the northeast side. Exit left into the moat and climb the original Northeast Ridge's first pitch, then traverse left and up over loose class 4+ to the left-facing corner with yellow-speckled rock and roofs, and follow the variation above to the summit.
wa_cathedral_rock_northwest_couloir: From I-90 take Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), follow Bullfrog Road to the roundabout, then SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald along Cle Elum Lake to Salmon la Sac. Bear right just before the campground onto gravel Cle Elum Valley Road (FR 4330) and drive about 12 miles to the Cathedral Rock Trailhead (#1345) near Tucquala Meadows, at about 3,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; fill out the free self-issue wilderness permit.

Take Trail #1345 west, crossing the Cle Elum River on a footbridge near the start, then climb steadily through forest. Continue straight at the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles; the trail reaches Nosh Nosh Wahtum and its campsites along the lake's northeast shore at about 2.5 miles.

Continue on Trail #1345 past the lake, up through subalpine meadow and then steeper, rockier switchbacks to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at about 5,550 ft, roughly 4 miles from the car.

Join the PCT southbound toward Deep Lake for a few tenths of a mile. At the first switchback where it starts down toward Deep Lake, take the Peggy's Pond trail #1375, a primitive path that traverses beneath Cathedral Rock to the pond. The last stretch is narrow and steep with real drop-offs and loose rock, and holds snow into early summer.

Traverse around the pond, then climb heather and small trees onto the northwest flank and loose rubble in the lower corral to the top of the funnel. Follow a dirty ledge rightward to the couloir entrance about 200 ft south of the funnel, stem past the chockstone in the enclosed chimney, then climb the couloir and a sloping slab using a big flake as a handrail. Broken slopes lead to the summit.
wa_cathedral_rock_southeast_face_chimney: Take Trail #1345 west, crossing the Cle Elum River on a footbridge near the start, then climb steadily through old-growth forest. Continue straight at the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles; the trail reaches Nosh Nosh Wahtum along the lake's northeast shore at about 2.5 miles.

Continue on Trail #1345 past the lake into subalpine meadow and blueberry slopes, with Cathedral Rock ahead, then switchback up steeper, rockier tread to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at about 5,550 ft, roughly 4 miles from the car.

Leave the trail at the pass and work up broken talus, heather benches and easy rubble on the south and southeast flank to the base of the tower. Climb the chimney cleft cutting the southeast face, left of the Southwest Face route, on gritty, fractured rock with thin protection, then follow the broken ridge crest and a short scramble to the summit boulder.
wa_cathedral_rock_standard: Take Trail #1345 west, crossing the Cle Elum River on a footbridge and entering the Alpine Lakes Wilderness at about half a mile. Continue straight at the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles and pass Squaw Lake (Nosh Nosh Wahtum), the last reliable water, at 2.5 miles. Beyond the meadows the trail switchbacks up rockier tread to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail at about 5,550 ft.

Follow the PCT less than half a mile to the Trail #1375 (Peggy's Pond) junction, where two climbers' paths head for the peak; the left one looks wrong from a distance but avoids a scree slope. Scramble the gully on the right side of the rounded spur to the summit rock near 6,400 ft, climb the gully left of the South Buttress, then one or two Class 4 pitches up the southwest face to the ridge crest and scramble to the summit.
wa_chair_bryant_traverse: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.
wa_chair_peak_northwest_ridge: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.

Follow the Snow Lake Trail to the Source Lake fork, then the climbers' path and snow up the basin toward Chair Peak's east face; about two hours in you reach Thumbtack Rock, the small pinnacle that marks the turn. Turn right there and climb a grassy gully over the ridge onto the northwest side, then head for a saddle with trees on it; the route starts up the gully just left of that saddle.

Climb the gully left of the treed saddle to the crest and belay from trees on its south side. Scramble down and left to the chockstone-capped chimney, work around and over the chockstone onto the ridge, then follow the easier, run-out crest past a false summit to the true summit, avoiding the loose, harder lines off the crest.
wa_chair_peak_voie_de_chaise: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.

Take the summer trail toward Source Lake; where it meets the talus, hold your height rather than dropping, pass the small cliff bands on your right, and leave the trail at a longer talus field marked by a large cairn. Climb up and left to the snow patch under the east face, up it and the last loose scree hugging the base, then go left past the end of the rock band to the first bolted line. Eight bolted pitches and a short exposed scramble lead to the summit.
wa_chair_peak_west_ridge: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), head north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental ski area parking lot, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 begins. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park.

Follow the Snow Lake Trail to the signed unmaintained spur toward Source Lake and take climbers' paths upslope toward Chair Peak, the same start as the Northeast Buttress. Traverse slabby ground, snowy and glide-cracked early in the season, round onto the west side to a 220 ft couloir below the ridge's low point just east of a distinct tower. Climb the couloir, then follow the crest to the summit.
wa_chikamin_peak_southeast_slopes: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), head north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and take the first right after about 0.1 mile, signed for a parking pass; the main Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lot is to the right where the road splits. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.
wa_chimney_rock_east_face_direct: From I-90 Exit 80, go north on Bullfrog Road through two traffic circles onto SR 903, then follow SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.
wa_east_face_6: From I-90 Exit 80, go north on Bullfrog Road through two traffic circles onto SR 903, then follow SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.
Follow Pete Lake Trail #1323 up the Cooper River valley, about 4.5 nearly flat forested miles, to the lake.
Continue on the trail beyond the lake to its junction with the Pacific Crest Trail near Lemah Meadow.

Turn north on the PCT, not toward Spectacle Lake, and follow it roughly a mile to where it crosses a wide old avalanche path with heavy blowdown near Chimney Creek and switchbacks sharply. Stop at that first switchback and look west for twin waterfalls spilling out of the hanging basin below the Chimney Glacier.

Leave the PCT at the switchback on a faint climbers' path, marked only intermittently with flagging and cairns, that climbs the forest right of the falls between two rounded rock outcrops and a cliff band. Do not follow it up a rocky gully; the line continues left through vine maple and alder, crosses three brushy ravines, and breaks out at Sunrise Knob, the rock buttress above the falls.

From camp, make your way onto the lower Chimney Glacier and rope up. Cross it and break through the cliff band onto the upper glacier, usually by the rock-and-snow gully just left of the icefall (a snow finger far to the left and the icefall itself are the alternatives), then cross the upper glacier to the foot of the gully that leads to the U-Gap, where the moat separates ice from rock.

Cross the moat where conditions allow and climb the loose gully toward the U-Gap. About 15 ft below the gap, leave it on the east side onto exposed ledges that wrap around the South Peak to the Main Notch, drop about 50 ft and take a reddish ramp up to the Key Ledge below the summit tower, then climb three pitches of class 4 and low fifth class, the last a chimney that tops out a few feet from the summit cairn.
wa_east_ridge_6: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), head north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and take the first right after about 0.1 mile, signed for a parking pass; the main Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lot is to the right where the road splits. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

Hike north on the PCT through Commonwealth Basin and up the switchbacks to the Kendall Katwalk, then on past Ridge and Gravel Lakes to the foot of Bumblebee Pass. A steep, loose climbers' path climbs to the pass and drops into the basin below Thomson's south face; climb heather and talus to a notch at about 5,600 ft on the east-southeast ridge, traverse left along the crest on class 2-3 ground, and climb a short exposed class 4 step to the summit.
wa_four_brothers_southwest_route: From I-90 Exit 80, go north on Bullfrog Road to SR 903 and follow it through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 17 miles. Turn left on FR 46, pass the Cooper Lake turnoff and continue about 7 miles to Cooper Pass, then stay on the main road about 3 miles down to the signed Mineral Creek trailhead in the valley. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued wilderness permit.
wa_garfield_mountain_infinite_bliss: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.4 mile and turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Drive about 12.3 miles to the fork just past the Taylor River bridge, keep right on the Middle Fork Road, and continue about 1 mile to a small gravel pullout with room for about five cars, at roughly 1,170 ft. Washouts on this road have at times added a mile or more of walking.

Walk 100 to 200 yards farther along the road and take the unsigned but well-worn climbers' path leaving on the left at a cairn. It climbs steeply through forest switchbacks for 30 to 45 minutes; a large cairn of flat white rocks about 50 yards below the slab marks the approach to the base, where the bolt line starts.
wa_garfield_mountain_preiss_route: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.4 mile and turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12.2 miles to the Garfield Ledges trailhead, just across the Taylor River bridge at the fork with the Taylor River Road. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.
wa_garfield_mountain_southwest_ledges: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.4 mile and turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Drive about 12.3 miles to the fork just past the Taylor River bridge, keep right on the Middle Fork Road, and continue about 1 mile to a small gravel pullout with room for about five cars, at roughly 1,170 ft. Washouts on this road have at times added a mile or more of walking.

Walk 100 to 200 yards farther along the road and take the unsigned but well-worn Infinite Bliss climbers' path leaving on the left at a cairn. It climbs steeply through forest switchbacks for 30 to 45 minutes; leave it just before it turns left to the base of the bolted slab.
wa_gunnshy_peak_standard_route: From the spur road near the trailhead, take the faint climbers' path east into the forest rather than the maintained lake trail. Cross Barclay Creek on logs, leave the old roadbed and zigzag steeply up to a headwall at about 3,600 ft. The path veers east beneath cliff bands and drops briefly into the waterfall gully; climb steeply out the far side to where cairns lead onto moderate ground.

Keep heading east beneath a buttress, not north into slide alder and devil's club, and follow cairns through meadows along Tailgunner's south ridge to the saddle near 5,400 ft. Bypass Point 5,760 by dropping about 200 ft around its east side, make a rising traverse above Gunn Lake through talus and heather to the east ridge near 5,950 ft, then traverse west along and just south of the crest, scrambling to the summit.
wa_guye_peak_improbable_traverse: From I-90 Exit 52 (West Summit) at Snoqualmie Pass, turn north onto Alpental Road, pass under the freeway, keep right at the fork just beyond the Pacific Crest Trail access, and drive about 1.4 miles to the Alpental Ski Area lot, with the Snow Lake trailhead across the road. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. Do not drive or park on the private Strasse roads off the access road.
wa_guye_peak_r1: Traverse up the talus to the rocky streambed at its north end (often dry), scramble up the streambed, where some parties belay the steepest part, and exit right onto the very large tree-covered ramp that rises across the face from north to south.
Follow the ramp south across the face; most parties scramble it, some belay. At its end, climb about 40 ft of solid rock to a second, grassy ramp and the notch.
Pass through the notch to climber's right into a wide gully, where the crux pitch begins.
Climb the steep crack and face for about 30 ft, then Class 4 through rock and alpine trees for about half a rope length to the top.

Follow the climber's path around the east side of the middle summit to the notch between the south and middle summits and rappel the loose, mossy slab into the gully (not from the tree at its top). Descend the gully and slabs east around the north summit, scramble an easy gully to the notch on its north side, and follow the scrambler's trail down to the saddle.
wa_guye_peak_r2: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn left (north) under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental ski area parking and the Snow Lake trailhead, around 3,100 ft.
