A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is available at the trailhead.

Take the climbers' path that leaves the pavement about 100 ft south of the Snow Lake Trail sign, the one that serves Snoqualmie Mountain and Cave Ridge rather than the West Face talus. It climbs steeply through forest past a clearing near 4,000 to 4,200 ft to the saddle between Cave Ridge and Guye Peak, about 1.5 miles in.

From the saddle, scramble the steep gully and ridge up to Guye's north summit, class 3 when snow-free and considerably more serious under snow. Around 4,840 ft the gully runs into a large rock face: take the left-hand option (a steep snow traverse in season), not the right, which leads into an awkward moat.
wa_guye_peak_southeast_gully: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road. In about 0.1 mile take the first right, signed for the parking pass, and in another 0.1 mile keep right for the main Pacific Crest Trail North lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.
wa_hibox_mountain_standard: Take I-90 to Exit 62 (Kachess Lake), turn left off the ramp and follow FR 49 (Kachess Lake Road) toward Kachess Lake. Follow the signs toward Lake Kachess Campground and turn left on FR 4930 (Box Canyon Road), which ends at a large lot and the Rachel Lake trailhead about 4 miles from the turn, around 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issue wilderness permit.

Follow Rachel Lake Trail #1313 about 2 miles to a brushy avalanche clearing near 3,300 ft; just past it take the unmarked climbers' path uphill on the right. Pass the first cliff band on the right, go left around an outcrop, and take a gully on the right through the second band. Climb the meadow and talus to the south side of the summit block, traverse east to the east-side gully, and climb its short class 3 notch to the top.
wa_hourglass_gully_winter: Take US 2 east past Gold Bar about 7 miles. Just as the highway curves left toward the large bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right onto Mount Index Road, drive about a quarter mile on dirt, and turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068 into the parking lot about 500 ft ahead, around 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Hike Lake Serene Trail #1068 about 4.1 miles to the north end of the lake, then traverse talus and boulders around the west shore to the south end. Head east to the saddle, climb the brushy ridge running southwest from it to the cliffs, traverse under them, and take the first wide gully on the right, the Hourglass. Climb it through the constriction, exit onto the upper ridge, and follow the knife-edged crest to the summit.
wa_huckleberry_mountain_east_ridge: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road. In about 0.1 mile take the first right, signed for the parking pass, and in another 0.1 mile keep right for the main Pacific Crest Trail North lot, around 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Hike the PCT north past the Kendall Katwalk to Ridge Lake, then past Alaska Pass and around Alaska Mountain. About 9 to 10 miles in, when the summit is due west, leave the trail and climb west up steep heather and talus to the rocky buttress near 6,100 ft. Take the right-hand ridge line linking tree patches, traverse left to a blocky ramp, drop about 20 ft to the notch, and climb the summit block.
wa_huckleberry_mountain_south_face: Leave I-90 at Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road, and in about 0.1 mile turn right onto the dirt spur into the PCT North Trailhead lot at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.

Follow the PCT north up to the Kendall Katwalk, then on past Ridge Lake and Gravel Lake and around Alaska Mountain to where the trail runs above Joe Lake, about 10 miles. Leave the trail through heather and scree slopes to the base of the south face, start near its right side on steep, sandy, broken rock, and move slightly left over two pitches (5.7) to the summit.
wa_iron_cap_mountain_south_route: From US 2 about 1.9 miles east of Skykomish, turn south on Foss River Road (FR 68); the pavement ends at 1.2 miles. Stay right at the Y at 3.5 miles, and at 4.7 miles, just before a bridge, turn left onto FR 6835 (the sign is easy to miss) and drive 1.9 miles to the West Fork Foss trailhead at about 1,600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park; self-issue the free wilderness permit at the kiosk.

Follow the West Fork Foss Lakes Trail #1064 past Trout Lake at 1.6 miles, then climb to Copper Lake at about 4.2 miles and continue past Little Heart Lake to Big Heart Lake at 7.3 miles, where the maintained trail ends on the rocky rise above the outlet.

Go cross-country south over the south end of Atrium Ridge, past small tarns and Little Chetwoot Lake, to the camps near Chetwoot Lake's east-end outlet. Cairns are sparse through the boulder fields, so carry a map or GPS track.

Climb talus and heather toward Point 6077, pass it on the east, and gain the west ridge for easy Class 3 scrambling. Downclimb a short third-class step into a notch, then follow the wide ramp below the summit block to the broad north ridge and easy red-tinged rock and dirt to the summit.
wa_j_tnar: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar, just as the highway curves left toward the large bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right onto Mount Index Road. In a quarter mile turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068 into the parking lot at about 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

Follow Lake Serene Trail 1068; at the signed junction at 1.7 miles the right fork goes to Bridal Veil Falls, so stay on the main trail, cross the creek, and climb the final 1.5 miles and about 1,300 ft on stairs, roots and rocks to the lake. Fill water here; there is none above.

Take the unofficial path around the right-hand (west) side of the lake, down granite slabs to the talus fan, and up the talus toward the wall. The last of it is steepening mossy slab and brush that parties commonly rope up for; rack up low near the lake, since the base is a rockfall alley.
wa_kendall_peak_cliff_north_face: Leave I-90 at Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road, and in about 0.1 mile turn right onto the dirt spur into the PCT North Trailhead lot at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park.
wa_kendall_peak_standard: Leave I-90 at Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road, and in about 0.1 mile turn right onto the dirt spur into the PCT North Trailhead lot at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and the roughly 50-car lot fills early on weekends; self-issue the free wilderness permit at the trailhead.
wa_la_bohn_peak_southwest_slopes: From US 2, about 0.5 mile east of the Skykomish Ranger Station, turn right (south) onto Foss River Road (FS Road 68) and drive 4.2 miles to the signed East Fork Foss River trailhead lot on the left, at about 1,650 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued wilderness permit are required.

From the gap head west up boulders and heather onto the east ridge and follow it over a false summit and a short, blocky knife-edge to the summit. Stay off the north side of the summit block, which drops away in a cliff.
wa_lemah_mountain_east_route: From I-90 Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), go north on Bullfrog Road 2.8 miles through two roundabouts and continue on SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Forest Road 46, about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left (west) on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued wilderness permit are required.

Cross the moat and climb the short cliff step onto the glacial remnants and snowfields on the peak's southeast side, then work across a series of cliff bands to the col between Lemah Two and the main peak. Finding the correct gully and cliff-band line up to the col is the route-finding crux, especially in fog or lingering snow, and the rock is loose.

From the col climb north toward the summit, then traverse west across the exposed ridge, going around or over a small summit block; the final 30 ft traverse west and climb the northwest ridge to the top. Gain the ridge where it looks easiest rather than following the snow-filled gully just left of the summit rocks, which tops out on loose third- and fourth-class ground.
wa_lemah_two_goatshead_spire: From I-90 Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), go north on Bullfrog Road 2.8 miles through two roundabouts and continue on SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Forest Road 46, about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left (west) on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued wilderness permit are required.
wa_little_big_chief_mountain_northeast_f: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.6 mile and turn right onto the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FS Road 56). Follow it about 12 miles to the main Middle Fork trailhead, cross the large concrete bridge, and turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Drive this heavily potholed road about 6 miles to the parking area at the gate, at about 1,650 ft.

Walk past the gate and follow the old Middle Fork road and then the Dutch Miller Gap Trail #1030 up the valley, about 14 to 15 miles in all, past Hardscrabble Horse Camp and the Williams Lake junction to Dutch Miller Gap. From the gap climb about 500 ft of heather and rock steps onto the northeast ridge to an open bench, cross a snowfield into the cirque below the east face, and climb the short belayed pitches to the summit.
wa_lundin_peak_south_face_left: From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and after 0.1 mile turn right at the Forest Service sign into the Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lots, at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_mount_daniel_daniel_glacier: Take the Cathedral Rock Trail #1345, which crosses the Cle Elum River on a bridge and climbs past Squaw Lake to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail, about 4.5 miles. Follow the PCT briefly toward Deep Lake; at the first switchback down, take the spur to Peggys Pond, about half a mile of steep, narrow path along ledges with sheer drop-offs and loose rock.

Follow braided boot paths northwest then west across heather and talus, gaining about 1,500 ft in a mile to the broad southeast ridge near 7,000 ft, with the Hyas Creek Glacier on your right and Circle Lake below on your left. Traverse climbers' trail and scree below the East Summit to the 7,600-ft saddle, then cross loose talus, snow and the rocky glacier margin to the West Summit, staying on rock off the glacier ice.
wa_mount_hinman_hinman_glacier: From the trailhead follow Necklace Valley Trail #1062 up the East Fork Foss River. The first 5 miles are nearly flat, gaining only about 600 ft and entering the Alpine Lakes Wilderness at about 1.5 miles, to the crossing of the East Fork Foss near an established camp. There is no bridge: cross on logs or ford, ideally in the morning when early-season runoff is lowest.
Across the river the trail turns steeply uphill, climbing roughly 2,400 ft in about 3 miles on rooty switchbacks into Necklace Valley. The grade eases at Jade Lake, the first of the valley's lakes.

Continue on the trail past Emerald and Opal Lakes through the swampy Necklace Basin to its head, where the maintained trail ends. From there a cairned climbers' path climbs through meadow, heather and boulder talus, roughly 1,000 ft, to La Bohn Gap on the ridge crest above the La Bohn Lakes. Stay out of the waterfall drainage to the left; routefinding is poor in fog.

From La Bohn Gap head north-northeast into the basin above the gap, then swing east-northeast up the snowfield and glacier remnant below the summit ridge. Carry ice axe and crampons for firm morning snow, and watch for moats or crevasses early in the season.
From the top of the snowfield scramble east up loose scree and broken ridge ground to the broad, multi-humped summit ridge, then follow the crest east to the true high point near its east end.
wa_mount_index_bluebell: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar (near milepost 35), just as the highway curves left toward the bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right (south) onto Mount Index Road. Follow the gravel road about a quarter mile, turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068, and park in the lot about 500 ft ahead at roughly 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.
wa_mount_index_north_face: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar (near milepost 35), just as the highway curves left toward the bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right (south) onto Mount Index Road. Follow the gravel road about a quarter mile, turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068, and park in the lot about 500 ft ahead at roughly 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.

Follow Lake Serene Trail #1068, first along an old road and then climbing through forest. At about 1.7 miles stay left where the signed Bridal Veil Falls spur branches right, cross the creek, and climb the final 1.5 miles on steps, roots and rock into the basin at the lake's north end, about 3.6 miles and 2,000 ft from the trailhead.
wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar (near milepost 35), just as the highway curves left toward the bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right (south) onto Mount Index Road. Follow the gravel road about a quarter mile, turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068, and park in the lot about 500 ft ahead at roughly 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.
wa_mount_index_northeast_buttress: From US 2 about 7 miles east of Gold Bar (near milepost 35), just as the highway curves left toward the bridge over the Skykomish River, turn right (south) onto Mount Index Road. Follow the gravel road about a quarter mile, turn right at the sign for Lake Serene Trail 1068, and park in the lot about 500 ft ahead at roughly 600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.

Follow Lake Serene Trail #1068, first along an old road and then climbing through forest. At about 1.7 miles stay left where the signed Bridal Veil Falls spur branches right, cross the creek, and climb the final 1.5 miles on steps, roots and rock into the basin at the lake's north end, about 3.6 miles and 2,000 ft from the trailhead.
wa_mount_persis_west_ridge: From US 2 about 0.6 mile east of milepost 33, roughly 2.5 miles east of Gold Bar, turn right (south) onto Forest Road 62. Follow it about 3.5 miles to the FR 6220 junction and bear left, go a little over a mile to a second junction and bear left again, then drive the last rough mile to a small pullout near the road end at about 2,800 ft. A Hampton Resources recreation permit is required, and a locked gate adds about 5 miles of road.

The boot path starts up the steep, well-trodden, unmarked gully directly opposite the pullout. It climbs very steeply for about a mile through clearcut and young forest into older timber, at times pulling on trees, to the west ridge crest. Follow the ridge east across talus past Point 5017, drop about 100 ft, and climb past two small ponds to the true summit.
wa_mount_price_hester_lake_route: From I-90 Exit 34, turn north on 468th Ave SE and in about 0.6 mile turn right onto the Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12 miles to the Taylor River junction, stay right on the Middle Fork Road, and continue roughly 6 miles on rougher road to the Dingford Creek Trailhead at about 1,400 ft, with parking on the right. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and higher clearance helps on the last stretch.
wa_mount_roosevelt_standard: From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, go north under the freeway and take the second right onto Alpental Road, then drive about 1.3 miles to the Alpental Ski Area lot; the Snow Lake trailhead is at the north end of the day-use lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.

Follow Snow Lake Trail #1013 up the valley past the Source Lake overlook spur at about 1.75 miles, then climb about 500 ft to the saddle at the wilderness boundary and descend about 400 ft to Snow Lake.
Continue around Snow Lake's north end toward Gem Lake, then climb about a mile through a rock field and meadows to Gem Lake.
Walk to Gem Lake's west shore, where an unmaintained climbers' boot path leaves the lake and heads up the steep ridge to the west. It is easy to lose in fog or fresh snow.
Follow the boot path up the steep, westward-trending ridge, skirting left (east) of a band of buttresses, to where it tops out near 5,400 ft.
Take the short, cairned scree slope and rising traverse west, about 200 ft of gain, into the small snow-and-talus basin below the two summit humps; the gully rises out of this basin.
Climb the loose gully of rock, heather and dirt as it turns north and steepens, to the short, semi-exposed ramp below the summit block.
Follow the ramp to the final roughly 20 ft Class 2-3 rock step and climb it to the top. Make sure you are on the higher, southerly hump; the lower north hump is a common false summit.
wa_mount_teneriffe_kamikaze_trail: From I-90 Exit 32 (436th Ave SE), turn north over the freeway and drive 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way. Turn left, and in 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. In 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, the paved Mount Teneriffe Trailhead lot is on the left. A Discover Pass is required to park.
wa_mount_teneriffe_standard_route: From I-90 Exit 32 (436th Ave SE), turn north over the freeway and drive 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way. Turn left, and in 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. In 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, the paved Mount Teneriffe Trailhead lot is on the left. A Discover Pass is required to park.
wa_new_york_gully: From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, go north under the freeway and take the second right onto Alpental Road, then drive about 1.3 miles to the Alpental Ski Area lots at the road's end. Winter climbers commonly park in the groomer lot about 200 ft past the main day lot.

Walk up the open hillside toward the Alpental waterfalls, cut left into the trees at their base through two steep cliff bands, then move right onto the Phantom Slide and climb it to about 4,900 ft before trending left to the northwest-shoulder notch near 5,200 ft. Downclimb about 200 ft, traverse to the first obvious gully and climb it to a col between gendarmes, rappel into Enigma Gully and climb its snow to the summit.
wa_red_mountain_snoqualmie_standard: Follow the PCT north about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and bear left onto Commonwealth Creek Trail #1033 into Commonwealth Basin, crossing the creek (last water). Where the trail levels near a small tarn below Red Mountain's west slope, leave it at a cairn in the middle of the path and follow the faint boot path up the west slope, staying near the crest on climber's right, over about 900 ft of loose class 2-3 rock to the summit.
wa_sky_mountain_s_route: Drive US 2 to Stevens Pass, about 65 miles east of Everett, and park in the large ski area lot on the north side of the highway. Walk to the small utility building near the east end of the lot, where the unsigned path begins. No parking pass is required.

Take the gravel service road on the left side of the utility building, passing beneath the powerlines (a steeper boot path across from the building cuts off the switchbacks). Stay left, then bear right, pass the vehicle gate about a quarter mile up, and keep climbing the road to where it flattens and forks at about 5,050 ft.

Leave the service road at the fork and follow the faint, cairned climbers' path northwest through heather and huckleberry for about a quarter mile to the lake. Fill up here; there is no water beyond it.
Follow the path along the lake's south shore, then climb about 100 ft to the gap in the ridge crest just northwest of the lake, where the views open to the north.
Follow the undulating ridge west, regaining height several times, and traverse beneath the band of loose, rocky high points on the crest.

Beyond the rocky points, pass the lower sub-summit that most parties mistake for the top: make the steep traverse across its south side, then a short final climb to the true summit at the end of the ridge.
wa_slippery_slab_tower_ne_face: Drive US 2 east past Skykomish about 12 miles to the sharp hairpin turn. Immediately after the Tunnel Creek bridge, turn right onto unsigned FS Road 6095 (only possible from the eastbound lane) and follow the narrow, potholed gravel road 1.2 miles, keeping left at two quick forks, to the trailhead at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit are required.
wa_snoqualmie_mountain_the_snostril: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to the Alpental parking lots at the road end, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at the Snow Lake trailhead lot.

Approach as for New York Gully: climb the slope above the lots toward the Alpental waterfalls, go left into the woods below them and straight up through two steep cliff bands, then move right onto the Phantom Slide path and follow it up toward the northwest face. The route starts in a corner just right of a large cave, roughly halfway between the Thunder Basin exit gully and the Snot Couloir.
wa_south_face_8: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road, take the first right (signed for the parking pass), and keep right where the road splits in 0.1 mile to the PCT North trailhead lot at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Follow the PCT north about 2.5 miles to the signed junction and take Commonwealth Creek Trail #1033 into Commonwealth Basin. Just past the creek crossing (last water), leave the trail and go cross-country northwest through open timber and talus into the cirque below the south face. Start at the face's low point directly beneath the summit and climb about four low fifth-class pitches, over a slab and a steeper final pitch, to the top.
wa_south_gully_south_spur: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead parking, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The side roads named Strasse are private and closed to climbers, on foot as well as by car.

From Alpental Road, work onto Guye Peak's south side on public ground and find the single obvious gully cleaving it. Scramble the gully until one or two chockstones force you briefly left onto the face, regain it, and follow the South Spur to the south summit. For the high point, traverse north over the middle summit, make the roughly 30 m rappel from slung trees into the gap, and scramble up to the north summit.
wa_south_rib: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead parking, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The side roads named Strasse are private and closed to climbers, on foot as well as by car.

Walk up the Sahale ski track toward Guye for about 3/4 to 1 mile; where it fades, climb the boulder field and slide alder to the base of the cliff. Traverse east along the base past Blood Sport to a taller talus fan, go up it to the rib, and climb about five pitches of low fifth-class rock, dirt and trees to the south summit. For the high point, traverse north over the middle summit, rappel into the gap, and scramble to the north summit.
wa_southwest_face: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is required.

Follow the Snow Lake Trail about 1.5 miles, fork off toward Source Lake, cross the talus and start up the standard line toward Pineapple Pass. Before the pass, break off north of the gully to three low-angle open-book corners just past the South Face start, and climb about four pitches: corner to a slung tree, a left-facing slab, face left of three cracks under a small roof, then the upper South Face to the summit.
wa_spire_mountain_scramble: Leave the road on the side away from the river and climb steeply, off-trail, through downed timber; the first 600 ft are steep but brush-free. After crossing an old logging road, traverse obliquely left to a saddle at about 2,300 ft, where you cross a second old overgrown logging road.
Continue uphill from the saddle; at about 2,700 ft the slope narrows into a well-defined, fairly brush-free hogsback. Follow its crest to where it ends at about 3,300 ft.
From the top of the hogsback, continue straight uphill as the slope steepens toward the large cliff bands that block the north end of the peak at roughly 4,200 to 4,400 ft.

Traverse southeast beneath the cliff bands onto the mountain's west and northwest side to about 5,400 ft below the summit spires, then turn uphill and climb the wide gully and slope to the saddle just northwest of the summit. Watch for a moat or schrund as you near the saddle, depending on the season.

From the saddle, scramble southeast along the airy crest, mostly class 3, to a short exposed mantle step of about ten feet near 6,100 ft where many parties rope up. Stay on the crest; ground to the north and east steepens quickly into permanent snow and cliffs.
Above the step, continue a short way up the ridge to the summit.
wa_summit_chief_mountain_south_route: From I-90 Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), turn north on Bullfrog Road for 2.8 miles through two traffic circles, then take SR 903 north through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to the junction with Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 16.8 miles from I-90. Turn left on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about a mile to the Pete Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit are required.

Follow the Pete Lake Trail #1323 up the Cooper River on gentle, mostly flat forest tread about 4.5 miles to Pete Lake, then continue to a fork about five miles in and turn right. After about 0.6 mile, turn right again onto the Pacific Crest Trail.
Climb the PCT north up its long series of switchbacks for about 4.5 miles to about 5,500 ft. The Vista Lakes tarns lie just east of the trail at that height; this is the last reliable water.
Leave the PCT and head cross-country west and north-west from the lakes over easy terrain on Vista Ridge, over Point 5965, then drop to Summit Chief Pass.

From the pass follow the ridge north-west, staying below the cliffs and gendarmes and west of Summit Chief Lake, across sloping slabs cut by slots and gullies into the talus basin south-east of the summit. Dropping to about 6,000 ft to take the scree avoids the worst of the slabs.

Climb steep hardpan, talus and the snowfield below the south-east face toward the point where the mountain steepens at about 7,000 ft and a moat forms. Avoid the first, left-most snow finger, which dead-ends in a deep notch; head for the upper right corner of the snowfield.
Past the moat, exit onto steep dirt and scree and take a left-slanting ramp up to the small notch in the south ridge skyline.

Cross the notch into the southwest gully system: a steep gully, often icy in the morning, then loose rock, steep dirt and a slightly outward-dipping slab. Exit by the gully on the right just below the summit.
wa_tailgunner_peak_w_route: Drive US-2 east from Monroe to Baring. At milepost 41, across from the store, turn left onto 635th Place NE, cross the railroad tracks, go 0.3 mile and keep left at the junction. The road becomes FR 6024 (Barclay Creek Road); follow it 3.9 potholed miles to the road-end trailhead at about 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Cross Barclay Creek. The footlog is gone, so use a stout logjam about 200 yards upstream of the old spur road, or rock-hop or ford at low water. On the far bank, bushwhack a short way to an overgrown corrugated metal culvert. It marks an old logging road where the Tailgunner climbers' path begins.
Follow the climbers' path up the overgrown logging-road tread and on through forest with fallen limbs and blowdown, steepening to an open rock knob at about 3,600 ft.

Continue up to the base of a huge cliff near 4,000 ft, then angle right about 150 yards to the waterfall ravine. Get past the waterfall with a short class 2-3 scramble down and back up. The rock is slick when wet.

Climb on to about 4,400 ft, where the path forks. The spring line runs straight into Tailgunner Couloir, which holds steep snow early in the season. The summer line curves back to the left and climbs a brushy weakness in the cliff band.
Above the cliff band, keep climbing to Tailgunner Pass, the broad saddle at about 5,320 ft with Tailgunner rising to the west and Gunn Peak to the north.
Above the headwall, a short, exposed scramble leads to the summit. The narrow summit ledge can be icy while snow lingers.
wa_the_tooth_fairy: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn north under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area lot, about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.

Hike the Snow Lake Trail about 1.6 miles to the Source Lake turnoff and go left. Cross the Source Lake basin near 4,000 ft, crest the lip into Great Scott Bowl at about 4,400 ft, and climb toward Pineapple Pass. Below the pass, traverse left (west) along the base, past the Southwest Face, to the bolt line on the west-facing wall. Climb six bolted pitches, then a short scramble to the true summit.
wa_the_tooth_indentured_servant: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn north under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area lot, about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.

Hike the Snow Lake Trail about 1.6 miles to the Source Lake turnoff and go left. Cross the Source Lake basin and climb Great Scott Bowl toward Pineapple Pass. Traverse left (west) along the base of the cliff, past the Tooth Fairy, about 500 ft to the large gully that splits the cliff. Climb the five bolted pitches on its left side. Then clip one more bolt and scramble about 100 m of North Ridge to the true summit.
wa_three_queens_middle_peak: From Cle Elum, drive Highway 903 north about 17 miles, past Lake Cle Elum, and turn left onto Cooper Lake Road (FR 4600). Follow FR 4600 about 7 miles, past the Cooper Lake turnoff, to Cooper Pass. Stay on the main road about 3 miles down to the small signed Mineral Creek trailhead in the valley bottom, at about 2,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.
wa_tooth_chair_traverse: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn north under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area lot, about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.

Hike the Snow Lake Trail about 1.6 miles to the Source Lake turnoff and go left. Cross the Source Lake basin near 4,000 ft and climb Great Scott Bowl south toward Pineapple Pass. Near 5,100 ft, bear right up a rocky gully, keeping left of a large horn, to the pass. From Pineapple Pass, rope up and climb the South Face (5.4) to the summit.
wa_traverse_of_mount_index: Follow Lake Serene Trail #1068, first on an old road bed and then into forest. At about 1.7 miles stay on the main trail where a signed spur goes right to Bridal Veil Falls; the trail crosses the creek and climbs steeply on stairs, roots and rock for the last 1.5 miles into the basin, reaching the lake's north end about 4 miles from the car.

Traverse the west side of the lake over talus and very large boulders to its south end, then climb steep brush and a gully (snow into early summer) onto the bushy northeast spur. Climb the spur, the gully on the north face and the North Rib to a grassy bench, go left to heather and the crest, then follow the crest right over the false summit and a line of exposed gendarmes to the true North Peak summit.
wa_treen_peak_scramble: Climb the steep, unmaintained miners' path straight up the forested flank of Green Ridge to the point where the trail forks.
Stay left where the right-hand branch drops northeast toward Green Ridge Lake, and keep climbing steeply up the ridge to its high point near 4,840 ft.
Leave the ridge trail at the high point and go cross-country a short way north to the small tarn, with Treen Peak in view ahead.
From the tarn, descend north about 800 ft into the basin to the shore of Upper Garfield Mountain Lake. This drop has to be re-climbed on the way out.
Climb north from Upper Garfield Mountain Lake through steep forest to Charlie Brown Lake.

From the outlet, work onto the peak's southeast slopes and thread up through broken cliff bands and loose duff to a broad talus field near 4,850 ft. From the top of the talus angle left into the obvious gully, walled by rock on both sides, and climb it to the notch beside a protruding rock on the south ridge. Carry an axe and traction if snow lingers.
Above the notch, climb a few hundred feet of easy but steep heather to the summit ridge and follow it to the top. The north side of the ridge is corniced.
wa_tye_peak_e_route: Walk up the gated service road from the lot, past a ski-area utility tower near 0.75 mile. About a mile in, take the easy-to-miss, cairn-marked left fork off the road; staying right on the road leads to a cell tower instead.
Follow the left fork on a short traverse through heather and huckleberry to the shore of Skyline Lake.

From the lake, climb northwest through timber to the low point in the crest of Skyline Ridge. The correct gap drops about 150 ft at close to fifty degrees on its far side; a gap you can simply walk over is the wrong one.
Descend the steep back side of the gap, mossy loose rock and brush when snow-free and liable to cornice in winter, to the head of a small creek on the north side of the ridge. This is the last water.
Climb the steep wooded slope beyond the creek into gentle meadows near 4,900 ft, then up through thinning timber to the crest of Tye Ridge, where the brush clears onto open heather benches.
Follow the crest of Tye Ridge north to the saddle between Sky Mountain and Tye Peak.
From the saddle, climb the ridgeline directly to the broad summit, staying on the highest ground to avoid cornices in winter and loose talus in summer.
wa_vanishing_point: Walk the level Barclay Creek trail about a mile to a bridge over a large creek. Do not cross: just before it, break right into the forest around a large boulder and follow open forest or the creek bed to an open boulder field and an open wash. A technical approach on fixed lines, hand lines and about 800 ft of roped slab, passing a chossy waterfall on its right, leads to the base of the tower; the route's 14 pitches top out on the tower.
wa_wing_peak_northwest_ridge: From US-2 at Baring, near milepost 41, turn north onto 635th Place NE across from the convenience store and cross the railroad tracks. After 0.3 mile keep left on 635th Place NE; it becomes FR 6024, which you follow about 3.9 potholed miles to its end at the Barclay Lake Trailhead at about 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Follow Barclay Creek Trail 1055, then bushwhack along Barclay Creek and up Tailgunner Creek to an old, overgrown logging road. A bootpath climbs forest to about 4,000 ft, crosses a Class 2-3 waterfall ravine, and follows the grass and snow of Tailgunner Couloir to Tailgunner Pass. From the pass, climb the northwest ridge's steep snow faces and rock benches to an exposed snowfinger below the summit horn, then a short rock step to the top.
wa_a_servant_to_liberty: Drive SR-20 over Washington Pass and continue east a short way down to the big hairpin turn below the pass, and park off the road at the curve at about 5,100 ft. The highway over the pass is closed in winter.

Walk back up the road toward the pass to a pond on its south side, and from the pond's east end follow the cairned climbers' path about a mile through forest to the East Face talus. Climb the first three pitches of Freedom or Death, step right onto Thin Red Line just below its third anchor, and follow this route's eight pitches; from the top, scramble to the summit roped.
wa_accidental_discharge_east_face: From SR 530 about 8 mi north of Darrington, turn east on the Suiattle River Road (FS Road 26) and follow it about 20 mi to the Downey Creek Trailhead at about 1,440 ft. Park on the south side of the road just past the Downey Creek bridge; the trail starts on the north side. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required. The road has a long history of washouts, so check its status first.
wa_around_the_cave_we_go: Drive SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass, at about 5,200 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 mi to a small meadow and take the climbers' path that branches left just past a small stream. Follow it up slabs, talus and meadow to the steep, loose gully between Liberty Bell and Concord Tower and climb it to the notch on Concord's north side, where the climbing starts; the route leads from there to the summit.
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud: From SR-20 near milepost 82, turn north on Baker Lake Road (FS Road 11) and drive about 14 mi to the Baker Dam turnoff. Cross the dam on FS Road 1106, turn left on FS Road 1107 and follow it 8 to 9 mi to a signed spur on the left, which ends at the Anderson and Watson Lakes Trailhead in about 1 mi. The road is long and rough; high clearance helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Follow the Anderson-Watson Lakes Trail #611 through forest to the Anderson Butte Trail junction and stay left. Continue to the next junction, where the right fork drops to Lower Anderson Lake; bear left and climb to the saddle where the trail enters the Noisy-Diobsud Wilderness.
Stay on the trail as it drops from the saddle to the Watson Lakes.
From the basin, sidehill across slippery vegetation, brush and cedar thickets, then climb mossy slabs toward the steep, loose dirt-and-scree gullies that lead up to Bacon's south ridge.

Climb the steep, loose gully onto Bacon's south ridge, where broad snow slopes lead onto the toe of the Diobsud Creek Glacier. Rope up here. When snow-filled the gully is avalanche terrain, and it goes far more easily on firm morning snow.
Stay roped and probe across the glacier toward the summit block, then follow the flat, often windy summit ridge over a short snow arete and scramble the dry rocks to the summit.
wa_beyond_redlining: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 28 mi (about 17 mi past the Verlot Public Service Center) and turn right on Sunrise Mine Road (FS Road 4065). Follow this rough gravel road about 2.3 mi to its end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, at about 2,350 ft. High clearance is recommended, and a Northwest Forest Pass is required.
wa_big_four_mountain_dry_creek_route: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 26 mi (about 14.5 mi past the Verlot Public Service Center) to the Big Four Picnic Area and Ice Caves Trailhead, at about 1,640 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Take the ice caves trail, then leave it and cross the South Fork Stillaguamish on a sound fallen log (no bridge). Go southeast about a mile through pathless forest to Dry Creek and follow its bed to the headwall. Climb into the upper basin by class 3-4 ledges and ramps when dry, or a hidden snow chute in snow. The couloir system and an exposed class 4 traverse on red slabs gain the summit ridge; follow it over the first bump to the higher true summit.
wa_big_four_mountain_northwest_ridge: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east past the Verlot Public Service Center and about 13 miles beyond the bridge just past it to the Big Four turnoffs on the right. Pass the picnic area entrance and turn in a quarter mile later at the Ice Caves Trailhead lot, at about 1,640 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required to park; day passes are sold at the lot.
wa_big_four_mountain_spindrift_couloir: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east past the Verlot Public Service Center and about 13 miles beyond the bridge just past it to the Big Four turnoffs on the right. Pass the picnic area entrance and turn in a quarter mile later at the Ice Caves Trailhead lot, at about 1,640 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required to park; day passes are sold at the lot.
wa_big_four_mountain_tower_route: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east past the Verlot Public Service Center and about 13 miles beyond the bridge just past it to the Big Four turnoffs on the right. Pass the picnic area entrance and turn in a quarter mile later at the Ice Caves Trailhead lot, at about 1,640 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required to park; day passes are sold at the lot.

Follow the Ice Caves trail toward the basin below the north face, then traverse to the base of the prominent gully on the northeast side. Climb the gully to the first tower, work west onto it and up, rappel into the notch, and climb the remaining two towers; a long, steep, exposed snowfield then leads to the summit.
wa_big_kangaroo_west_face: From the pullout, pick up the cairned climbers' trail on the west side of Early Winters Creek and follow it about half a mile through open timber to the edge of a talus and boulder field. Leave the trail here rather than continuing south toward Kangaroo Pass, and rock-hop across the creek; there is no bridge, so take care in peak snowmelt or after rain.

Once across, follow an open boot-track and light bushwhack through slide alder and slabs, trending east into the basin below Big Kangaroo. Around 6,000 ft, head up the broad, shallow west-facing gully marked partway up by a single chockstone. Rope up below the chockstone: three short pitches pass it, traverse around the summit block, and climb the exposed 5.6 summit slab.
wa_big_snagtooth_west_ridge: From the summit of Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east about 3.5 miles and park in the long pullout on the right side of the road at about 4,320 ft, where the Willow Creek valley opens up toward Big Snagtooth.

Drop southeast through trees about 120 ft to Early Winters Creek and cross on a log near the mouth of Willow Creek. Climb steeply up the north side of Willow Creek, often brushy, until the slope eases near 5,000 ft, then continue into the upper basin near 7,000 ft. Turn south up about 400 ft of loose scree or snow to the west-ridge saddle, scramble the crest to the summit block, and climb the short chimney and friction slab to the top.
wa_black_peak_east_buttress: Drive SR-20 to Rainy Pass at about milepost 157.5 and turn into the Rainy Pass Picnic Site on the south side of the highway. The Lake Ann-Maple Pass trailhead (Trail 740) leaves from the paved lot at about 4,855 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; day passes are sold at the trailhead.
wa_black_peak_northeast_ridge: From Marblemount or Winthrop, drive SR-20 to the signed Rainy Pass Picnic Area trailhead at milepost 157, on the south side of the highway at Rainy Pass. A Northwest Forest Pass, interagency pass or day-use fee is required to park; overflow parking is along the highway.

Take the Lake Ann trail and keep right at the signed junction toward Heather Pass, then follow the unmarked climbers' path across two talus fields to Lewis Lake and up about 1,000 ft more to Wing Lake (~6,900 ft). From the lake, climb snow toward the low notch in the Northeast Ridge, following the moraine wide right before traversing back left, then climb the ridge, about five pitches of loose low-5th terrain, to the summit.
wa_blue_s_buttress: From Winthrop, drive SR-20 west through Mazama to the large pullout at the hairpin turn about a mile east of Washington Pass. From the west, follow SR-20 east over Rainy Pass and Washington Pass and descend to the hairpin.

Walk southeast through the boulder field and follow cairns through trees and talus to the drainage coming down from Poster Peak. Follow it uphill, cross it on cairns, and stay low near treeline below the buttresses, passing House Buttress, to Blue's Buttress, the southerly one with a large roof low down. Go around the roof's left side onto easy ledges and follow the ridge crest, 5.6 at most, to the summit.
wa_booker_mountain_south_ridge: Follow the Cascade Pass Trail up long switchbacks through forest and then across open slopes, 3.7 miles and about 1,700 ft of gain, to Cascade Pass at 5,392 ft.

Continue up the Sahale Arm trail toward Sahale Glacier Camp. Near the camp leave the trail and descend Sahale's south side by a snow-free gully near 6,600 ft into Horseshoe Basin, then traverse the basin at 6,400-6,600 ft past the Buckner buttress to a permanent snowfield and north-facing gully at 7,000-7,200 ft. Above, talus and slabs on the south ridge lead to a short, exposed 3rd-class gully and the summit.
wa_borrowed_time: From SR-530 in Darrington, turn south onto the Mountain Loop Highway at the three-way stop and drive 17.2 miles, then turn left onto FR 4096 about a mile past Bedal Campground. Follow this rough road to its end at about 2,800 ft; the upper part is steep and brushy. FR 4096 is not plowed, so in winter the approach starts lower on the road and is normally skinned.

Follow Bedal Creek Trail #705 up the drainage to the valley beneath Sloan's west face near 5,000 ft. Boot straight up the central weakness of the face, left of the obvious ice line on the right, to a flat basin below the first ice step, then climb six pitches: WI5, a WI4 corner, a WI3 gully under the hanging dagger, the M7 crux, a blue-ice traverse and a long 45-60 degree runnel to the summit ridge and the summit.
wa_boston_peak_southeast_face: From the pullout, follow the abandoned road about a mile to an old mine site, then the steep climbers' path through forest and slide alder, crossing Midas Creek, Morningstar Creek and the forks of Boston Creek, to emerge above treeline in Boston Basin. Low camp sits near 5,300 ft and high camp higher in the basin, about 3.2 miles and 3,100 ft from the road.

Rope up for the Quien Sabe Glacier. The big crevasses are low on the glacier, so most parties take its left side and traverse in beneath Sharkfin Tower; later in the season, end-run the bergschrund below the col on climber's right, then cut back up-left above it to the Sahale-Boston col at about 8,200 ft.

From the col, head toward Boston on loose rock and snow, crossing a short stretch of the upper Boston Glacier above the bergschrund, then climb loose 3rd- and 4th-class rock to a crux just below the summit ridge and scramble to the top.
wa_boston_peak_west_face: From SR-20 at Marblemount, take Cascade River Road east across the Skagit River and follow it about 20 miles to the Eldorado Creek trailhead at milepost 20. From late autumn to spring the road is gated here, three miles below its end at the Cascade Pass trailhead; foot and bicycle traffic may continue past the gate.

Bike, walk or ski the road beyond the gate to the Cascade Pass trailhead, climb the Cascade Pass Trail to its highest switchback, then leave the trail and angle up the slope to the northeast to about 6,400 ft.

Drop into the Soldier Boy drainage and make a rising traverse to the northwest corner of the Quien Sabe Glacier. Rope up and cross the glacier to the foot of the west face, below the lower of its two prominent gullies; the bergschrund at the base is turned on climber's right.

Climb two pitches of steep snow heading northeast, belaying first under a bulge and then where a gully opens to the east. Follow that large gully east on the third pitch, climb a fourth pitch to about 200 ft north of the summit, then cross the exposed ridge with a short rock step to the true top.
wa_boving_roofs: Drive SR-20 (the North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway just west of Washington Pass. The highway over the pass closes in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park.

Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.25 miles to the clearing where the main trail bends right toward the lake, and take the climbers' path up into the basin to the Y-shaped larch at the base of the Southwest Rib, left of the Southwest Couloir. Climb the first three pitches of the rib, go left at the ledge where the two stacked roofs come into view, pull through them, and finish up the remaining rib pitches to the summit.
wa_cascade_peak_east_ridge: Walk back down the road to the hairpin, drop down the embankment and cross the Cascade River, then go up and over the terminal moraine onto the apron at the foot of the C-J Couloir. Expect a short stretch of brush; it is about twenty minutes from the road.

Climb the couloir, roughly 3,400 ft of snow, to the Cascade-Johannesburg col at about 6,760 ft. The lower part sits under the Sill hanging glacier, so climb it while it is frozen and do not linger. The East Ridge rises west from the col toward Cascade Peak, on your right as you top out.

From the col the technical climbing starts with the crux, a loose, wide crack with few solid placements, then continues up loose, broken ground to the summit with real route-finding and no fixed anchors or cairns to follow.
wa_castle_in_the_sky: From Glacier, drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542) east about 12.5 miles and turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FS Road 32). Follow it 5.3 miles to the road-end parking at the Hannegan Trailhead. A recreation pass such as the Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit is required for camps inside the park.
wa_chockstone_route: Drive SR-20 (the North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway just west of Washington Pass. The highway over the pass closes in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park.

Hike the Blue Lake Trail a little over a mile to where the main trail bends right toward the lake, then take the climbers' path up through slabs, talus and heather into the basin below the west faces. Head for the foot of the huge cleft that splits North and South Early Winters Spires; this is the west-side gully, not the east-side couloir reached from the highway hairpin.

Climb a short step of low fifth-class slab and layback moves, then walk up the gully bed, taking cracks and ramps along its left edge, to below the first giant chockstone. Early in the season the gully can hold snow, so carry an axe and crampons.

Pass the chockstone on the left over blocky ground to an exposed lieback and a delicate slab, then continue on good, bolted rock with a rightward traverse and finish up a loose gully and chimney onto the summit plateau.
wa_cinderella_peak_scramble: Leave the maintained trail on the blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' trail, which branches left at the switchback, and follow it into the Green Creek valley until it reaches the creek. There is no bridge; ford at the best spot you can find, which gets harder at high runoff.
wa_clean_break: Drive SR-20 (the North Cascades Highway) to the small pullout where the highway crosses Silver Star Creek, about 8.5 miles east of Washington Pass near milepost 171, at roughly 3,450 ft. The highway over the pass closes in winter.

Follow the climbers' trail up the east side of Silver Star Creek for a couple of miles, cross the creek, and climb talus and forest up the western edge of the valley. At about 5,000 ft make a rising traverse left through the slide alder to the ledge under Juno Tower's east prow, where the route starts just left of a deep, narrow gully at a low fixed pin. Climb the 15 pitches, simul-climbing the final crest to the summit.
wa_colfax_peak_fords_theatre: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), drive about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS Road 39). Follow it about 8 miles to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead at roughly 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the daily fee is required to park, and a free Mount Baker Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_colfax_peak_kimchi_suicide_volcano: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), drive about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS Road 39). Follow it about 8 miles to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead at roughly 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the daily fee is required to park, and a free Mount Baker Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_colfax_peak_polish_route: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), drive about 1 mile east of the Glacier Public Service Center and turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS Road 39). Follow it about 8 miles to the Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead at roughly 3,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the daily fee is required to park, and a free Mount Baker Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.
wa_complete_south_buttress: From the easy, ledgy slabs at the toe of the lower ridge, follow the crest on 3rd, 4th and easy 5th class ground, making two half-rope rappels from old tat into notches. Where the ridge merges with the standard South Buttress, continue up its crest past a chimney with a big chockstone and a wide stembox, downclimb into the notch, climb a corner and a hand-to-offwidth crack, and cross the big slab to the summit.
wa_concerto_in_c_for_drill_and_hammer: Walk the old roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing to the Squire Creek Trail #654 sign and go 8 to 10 minutes more to two cut logs on either side of the track, with old logging cable beside it. Just past them turn right on a boot track down to Squire Creek and ford it. Go right (downstream) on a climbers' track that turns uphill, crosses a tributary, and climbs through old growth and up two gullies, steep and dirty at the top, to the grassy saddle.

From the grassy saddle, scramble down ramps 60 to 100 ft and cross the granite apron to a two-bolt anchor on a short vertical wall mid-slab, below the Africa Flake. Climb 14 pitches of mostly bolted friction slab, then cracks and ledgy ground up the buttress crest, to the summit chain anchor.
wa_crater_mountain_standard_route: Drive SR 20 to the Canyon Creek Trailhead near milepost 141, about 32.8 miles east of Marblemount or 55.1 miles west of Winthrop, at roughly 1,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the daily fee is required to park, and a free Pasayten Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead. The highway closes in winter.

Take Jackita Ridge Trail #738, fording Canyon Creek (no bridge; hazardous in spring and early summer), and switchback about 4 miles through timber to the junction near 5,000 ft. Turn left on Crater Lake Trail #746 for about 1 mile to Crater Lake, the last water. Climb onto the southeast ridge; where the trail ends in a loose gully near 7,600 ft, traverse across and follow cairns up. Trail resumes for the last quarter mile, passing west of a false top.
wa_crooked_thumb_peak_east_face: From Bellingham, take SR-542 (Mount Baker Highway) east through Glacier. About 12.5 miles east of the Glacier Public Service Center, turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FS Road 32) and follow it about 5.3 miles to the trailhead at the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and overnight camping inside North Cascades National Park requires a backcountry permit.
wa_cutthroat_peak_cauthorn_wilson_couloi: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is gated in winter, so this route's season begins when the highway reopens in spring.

Take the cairned climbers' track from the east end of the pullout down through timber, cross State Creek, and climb toward the basin below the south side of the peak. Cross the rib running south from the South Buttress into the basin east of the peak, climb the big couloir splitting the East Face through its ice steps to the ridgeline, then climb short pitches of about 5.4 rock to the true summit.
wa_cutthroat_peak_northeast_face: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is closed in winter, typically from late fall until spring.
wa_cutthroat_peak_southeast_buttress: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is closed in winter, typically from late fall until spring.

Follow the cairned track from the east end of the pullout down through timber, cross State Creek, and climb the open slopes on the east side of the southeast-draining stream into the basin south of the peak. At the headwall, start up the right-hand of the twin gullies and traverse into the left-hand one to reach the notch at the base of the buttress, then climb near the buttress crest to the summit.
wa_cutthroat_west_ridge: Follow the climbers' track through brush and timber, cross State Creek, and climb meadow slopes into the basin below the peak. Stay left up talus and scree to the saddle at the foot of the west ridge. Traverse ledges east about 100 ft to a shallow gully, climb it to the crest, follow the exposed crest east over a series of horns, then cross a ledge on the summit block's northwest face and climb one low 5th-class pitch to the top.
wa_davis_peak_nc_north_face: Drive SR 20 to milepost 126 and turn into the town of Diablo (not Diablo Dam). The trailhead is just past the Stetattle Creek bridge at the entrance to town; park in the small turnout on the right, leaving room for others. Overnight stays need a North Cascades backcountry permit.

Hike the Stetattle Creek Trail about 2 miles, drop about 200 ft to ford the creek opposite Davis Peak, then bushwhack and scramble a Class 3-4 rib, roped for the slabby sections, through slide alder to flat ground at the toe of the glacier near 4,000 ft. Climb the glacier to the bergschrund, then the face and couloir to the summit ridge near 6,700 ft, and follow the ridge about an hour to the summit.

Descend the south ridge crest past the 5,720 ft saddle, over or around Point 5872, then straight down the trackless south-slope forest. The cliff bands near 2,800 and 2,400 ft must be turned on the right line, so do the top 1,500 ft in daylight and steer by compass to avoid drifting toward Stetattle Creek. You reach SR 20 at the Gorge Creek bridge, about four road miles west of Diablo.
wa_davis_peak_nc_south_slope_and_ridge: Drive SR 20 to the bridge over Gorge Creek, about 2.6 miles east of Newhalem and about the same distance west of the Gorge Lake causeway and the Diablo turnoff. Watch the sharp curve at the east end of the bridge. Park in the lot at the west end; the east lot is signed for motorhomes and oversize vehicles. There is no trail: the route leaves the highway directly.

From the east end of the bridge, cross the highway and head straight uphill into the woods. Climb the brushy lower gully and steep, trackless timber, where cliff bands near 2,400 and 2,800 ft must be turned, to granite slabs at about 4,850 ft. Scramble the Class 2-3 South Buttress, passing Point 5872 on its north side, to the 5,720 ft saddle, climb about 200 ft of slab to the sharp ridge, then follow the broad ridge to the summit.
wa_del_campo_peak_standard: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 31 miles to Barlow Pass, where the pavement ends, and park at the trailhead lot at about 2,360 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required.

Walk the gated Monte Cristo road about a mile to the signed junction and turn right onto Gothic Basin Trail #724. It climbs steeply through timber, fords Weden Creek, and about 3 miles from the trailhead crosses a steep avalanche gully that can hold a firm snow tongue into July, then breaks out into the meadows and rock slabs of Gothic Basin near 5,000 ft.
Follow the boot path across the basin past a small tarn and up boulder and talus slopes to Foggy Lake at about 5,200 ft, the last reliable water.

Cross the boulder field on the climbers' trail along the lake's north side and climb Del Campo's south slopes to the snowfield below the summit wall near 6,200 ft. Avoid the obvious gully, which dead-ends at a vertical wall; take the blocky Class 3-4 ledges just left of it to the notch at about 6,350 ft, then turn left (west) for the short scramble to the summit.
wa_direct_north_buttress: From Bellingham, drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) east to Glacier and continue about 12.5 miles past the Glacier Public Service Center, then turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FS Road 32) and follow it about 5.3 miles to the road end at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park, and overnight stays in the park need a backcountry permit.

Climb Trail #674 to Hannegan Pass, drop east into the Chilliwack valley, bear right at the park boundary onto the Chilliwack River Trail and follow it across the river and down-valley to Bear Creek. Ford Bear Creek, climb brushy timber east to meadows above Ruta Lake and traverse the divide to the 6,480 ft saddle camp. Drop down scree to the glacier remnant, tie in at the buttress toe, climb the 21 pitches, then scramble right to the summit ridge.
wa_direct_southwest_buttress: From SR 20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River and follow the Cascade River Road about 20 miles, gravel for the second half, to the small Eldorado trailhead lot on the right near milepost 20, about 2,100 ft. Overnight stays need a North Cascades backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.
wa_direct_west_face: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to the unmarked pullout on the south side of the highway near milepost 166, about 0.7 mile west of the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff (east of Washington Pass and its hairpin). No pass is needed to park at this roadside pullout.

Take the climbers' boot path down to Early Winters Creek at about 4,080 ft and cross on logs, then climb steeply through forest between two feeder gullies to the bench camp near 6,500 ft. From the bench leave the Burgundy Col trail and go up and right (east) past two minor buttresses into the broad talus gully under the tallest wall, then climb the eight pitches of the West Face to the summit block.
wa_dolphin_chimney: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway, about 1 mile west of Washington Pass, at roughly 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.25 miles to the signed clearing northwest of Liberty Bell, then take the climbers' path up talus and heather into the basin below the spire's west side, aiming for the Y-shaped larch at the base of the Southwest Rib. Climb two or three pitches of the rib, traverse left to the dark chimney about 100 ft left of the Boving Roof, climb it, and finish on easier cracks up the rib to the summit.
wa_doorway_flake: Walk the old roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing to the Squire Creek Trail #654 sign and continue 8 to 10 minutes to two cut logs with old logging cable, then turn right on the boot track down to Squire Creek and ford it. Follow the climbers' track downstream and up through old-growth forest, across a tributary and up two gullies; the top of the second is steep and dirty and opens onto the grassy saddle, about 3 hours from the car.
wa_east_face: From Darrington drive SR 530 north about 8 miles to the Suiattle River Road (FS Road 26) and follow it east about 20 miles to the Downey Creek Trailhead, just past the Downey Creek bridge; the trail starts on the north side and parking is on the south side. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Hike the Downey Creek Trail about 6 miles up the valley, then turn up Bachelor Creek on a faint, brushy path toward Cub Lake and Itswoot Ridge. From the ridge cross the Dome Glacier to the Dome-Chickamin col, the usual base camp, then cross the Chickamin Glacier to the Gunsight Range and climb the six to seven pitches of the East Face to the summit. Plan on two days to reach the base.
wa_east_face_2: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) east past Washington Pass and its hairpin to the pullout on the south side of the highway near milepost 166, about 0.7 mile west of the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff. No pass is needed to park at this roadside pullout.

Take the boot path down across Early Winters Creek and up the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek to the bench camp near 6,500 ft, then on to Burgundy Col at about 7,720 ft. Drop 200 to 300 ft down the col's east side (steep snow, loose rock or moats by season) and traverse south beneath the east faces to Chablis, the southernmost spire, then climb the four pitches of the East Face to the summit.
wa_east_ridge_2: Walk the closed roadbed to where a pink-flagged climbers' trail leaves it and climbs steeply through old growth, about 1,700 ft in the first mile, to a ridge saddle near Point 5116. At this easy-to-miss junction take the branch that climbs about 1,000 ft along Kindy Ridge to Point 5791, then follow the crest over minor humps and heather benches to Cyclone Lake, where the camping is in the meadows on its east side.

From the lake, cross heather benches and easy slabs onto Snowking's east ridge and follow it west, sidehilling around minor gendarmes and cliff bands and staying off the Snowking Glacier. The final few hundred feet steepen to about 30 degrees on easy snow or scree below the summit block, which is a short Class 3 scramble topping out from the south-southeast.
wa_east_ridge_3: On SR-20, park at the broad roadside pullout near milepost 166, about 4 miles east of Washington Pass on the Mazama side. This is where the descent over Burgundy Col comes back to the highway, so leave a shuttle car here; the East Ridge itself starts from the Cedar Creek Trailhead near Mazama.
wa_east_ridge_4: Drive SR-20 east to Newhalem. Just after crossing Goodell Creek, take the first left onto a small road, turn immediately left at the T, and follow the road uphill to the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp at about 600 ft; park there, and the climbers' path starts just down the road. Overnight stays in Terror Basin need a North Cascades backcountry permit, issued walk-up only at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Follow the old Goodell Creek roadbed about 4 miles to a cairned flat near 1,600 ft, the last water, then climb the steep boot path to timberline and traverse to the 6,200-ft notch above Terror Basin camp. From camp cross slabs onto the Terror Glacier, rope up, and go east beneath the South Face past the West Ridge and South Face starts; cross the moat near its eastern end and climb broken gullies to the East Ridge crest and the summit.
wa_east_slope: Continue south on the Thunder Creek Trail about 1.5 miles, crossing the bridge over Fisher Creek, to Tricouni Camp in open salal forest just beyond it, around 8 miles from the trailhead. This is where the climbers' path to Lucky Ridge leaves the maintained trail.
wa_east_twin_needle_south_route: Drive SR-20 east to Newhalem. Just after crossing Goodell Creek, take the first left onto a small road, turn immediately left at the T, and follow the road uphill to the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp at about 600 ft; park there, and the climbers' path starts just down the road. Overnight camps in Crescent Creek Basin need a North Cascades backcountry permit, issued walk-up only at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Follow the old Goodell Creek roadbed, an unmaintained climbers' path with deadfall and washouts, about 4 miles upvalley to a large cairn where the path leaves the roadbed. Cross Terror Creek here by wading or on a big log just upstream when one is in place; it runs higher with snowmelt in the afternoon.

Climb straight up the steep, brushy crest of the Barrier, with no water until snowmelt puddles appear around 5,400 ft, to timberline near 5,600 ft. Loose, exposed ledges and talus, harder late in the season without snow cover, lead to the ridge crossing at about 6,100 ft.
Cross slabs and heather through Stump Hollow, between the Barrier crest and the Chopping Block, to the established bivy sites on the saddle northeast of the Chopping Block at about 6,400 ft.

Drop about 200 ft into Crescent Creek Basin, cross its talus, slabs and snow, and work around buttresses to the loose south-facing gullies beneath the Eye Col. Keep the party together against rockfall; the small chockstones low in the gully are scrambled, the larger ones higher up are fifth class and usually roped, and a short scree walk finishes at the notch.
Climb the steep summit block of East Twin Needle directly above the col, roped; the crux is a short hand crack near the top, which can hold ice early in the season.
wa_east_wilmans_spire: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 30 miles, past the Verlot Public Service Center, to Barlow Pass at about 2,360 ft, where the pavement ends and the Monte Cristo road is gated to vehicles. Park at the Barlow Pass lot; a Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free self-issued wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.

Walk or bike the gated, nearly flat Monte Cristo road about 4 miles along the South Fork Sauk River to the old townsite. Where the road washed out near the old Twin Bridges site, the river has to be forded or crossed on logs.

Take the Glacier Basin Trail out of the townsite for less than a mile, then leave it and head up toward the spire: snow early in the season, loose talus once it melts out, up a narrowing gully of 35 to 45 degrees to the lower col. Avoid the left-hand branch where the gully narrows. From the col, scramble around the south face to the upper east notch and climb three short pitches (to 5.6) to the tiny table-top summit.
wa_easy_getaway: Start up the maintained Cutthroat Creek Trail #483 from the kiosk. After a few minutes, still on the old roadbed beside the main trail, leave it on climber's left and head uphill into the forest. Follow a climbers' path through light brush, trees and talus, trending right toward the buttress, to a flat granite slab platform under the cliff. Allow about 1 to 2 hours. Not every cairn marks the route, so steer by the buttress.
wa_eldorado_peak_east_ridge: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber for about 1,500 ft to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb it to camp near 7,500 ft.

Roped, cross the nearly flat Inspiration Glacier toward the obvious low gap near the east end of Eldorado's East Ridge. Take a bearing from camp, because the glacier is featureless in cloud. Pass north through the gap onto the glacier slopes north of the ridge.

Climb west up the glacier slopes north of the ridge, keeping the crest on your left and probing suspect snow bridges, to where the slope steepens below the knife-edge. Follow the narrow, often corniced snow crest to the small summit. An axe and crampons are essential, and many parties place pickets along the crest.
wa_eldorado_peak_eldorado_glacier_nw: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber for about 1,500 ft to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb it to camp near 7,500 ft.

Roped, cross the glacier past the East Ridge and head for the obvious notch between Eldorado's North Ridge and the first rock spire (Dean's Tower), at about 8,100 ft. Rappel from the piton anchor on the far side into the Marble Creek cirque (one 60 m rope does it), then traverse a few hundred feet across the small glacier to the foot of the couloir near 7,800 ft. A moat or bergschrund there widens through the summer.

Climb the couloir that splits the northwest face, about 1,000 ft of short ice steps separated by lower-angle snow, to a small flat area just below the summit ridge. From there follow the exposed snow knife-edge to the summit.
wa_eldorado_peak_north_ridge: In Marblemount, where SR 20 turns, go straight onto Cascade River Road and cross the Skagit River bridge. Follow the road about 20 miles to the small Eldorado parking area on the right at about 2,100 ft, with a pit toilet. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel. The road usually opens in late May or June. Overnight stays need a park backcountry permit, picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb to the East Ridge camp near 7,500 to 7,600 ft.

Climb steep snow out of the notch onto the rock crest, then follow the ridge on its east side, where the rock is solid with good friction and incut holds (moves to 5.7). Near the top, either finish directly up steeper ice and rock or join the East Ridge knife-edge to the summit.
wa_eldorado_peak_northeast_face: In Marblemount, where SR 20 turns, go straight onto Cascade River Road and cross the Skagit River bridge. Follow the road about 20 miles to the small Eldorado parking area on the right at about 2,100 ft, with a pit toilet. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel. The road usually opens in late May or June. Overnight stays need a park backcountry permit, picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Cross the Cascade River on the log and climb the climbers' path and boulder field into Eldorado Creek Basin, then go over the ridge into Roush Basin and up the Eldorado Glacier. Near 7,500 ft, leave the East Ridge track to climber's right onto the Northeast Face. Traverse below the rock band near 8,200 ft to a point northeast of the summit, climb the face (up to 60 degrees) to the start of the knife-edge, and follow the crest to the summit.
wa_eldorado_peak_west_arete: From SR-20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles (pavement gives way to gravel around mile 10) to the parking area at about 2,100 ft near Eldorado Creek. Overnight stays in North Cascades National Park need a backcountry permit. The road is often not open this far until late June.

Cross the Cascade River on logs a short way downstream of the parking and follow the steep climbers' trail up beside Eldorado Creek into the Roush Creek basin and onto the Eldorado Glacier. From the glacier, descend west into the Marble Creek cirque to the toe of the arete near 6,000 ft, then climb the arete, about 2,800 ft of loose 4th class to 5.8 on and near the crest, to the summit.
wa_elephant_butte_standard_route: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 20 miles to milepost 126 and turn left at the sign for Diablo. Cross the Stetattle Creek bridge, bear right, and park beside the river across from the domed swimming pool; the Sourdough Mountain Trail starts behind the pool building at about 900 ft. Overnight stays in North Cascades National Park need a backcountry permit.

Climb the Sourdough Mountain Trail's steep switchbacks to an unmarked junction near 4,300 to 4,400 ft and turn left, heading north up the ridge crest just west of Sourdough Creek to tree line near 6,000 ft on Stetattle Ridge. Follow the open crest northwest, keeping on or southwest of the top, past the 6,495 ft high point, down to a saddle with a short class 3 step, then up to Elephant Butte's summit.
wa_ellation: From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, drive the Mt. Baker Highway (SR-542) east through Glacier and about 12.5 miles beyond it, then turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (Forest Road 32). Follow it 5.3 miles to the road end at the Hannegan Pass Trailhead, about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_ellen_pea: There is no trail. Climb from the highway to the talus at the foot of the gully that splits the wall; the gully forces you briefly out to the left before you rejoin it higher. Pass the first, lower ledge system and keep going to the upper ledge, where the long routes start, about an hour and 10 minutes from the car.

Walk right along the upper ledge, a treed third-class ledge slanting up and right out of the gully, to its far end with the big cave directly overhead. The first pitch is the left-facing corner about 40 m long that ends below a pair of left-slanting twin cracks.
wa_excavation_aka_the_crack: Walk or scramble around the side of the cliff, about 50 ft high, to the tree on top above the crack, where a static line is normally left rigged. Inspect that line before trusting it; the bolts on the face are old and should not be used.
Rig a top-rope from the tree above the crack and lower down the line to the base, at the foot of the wall's most obvious continuous crack system beside the road.
wa_first_amendment: Follow the cairned climbers' path down into the trees, cross Early Winters Creek on logs, and climb the rocky drainage and talus to the base of Spontaneity Arete, marked by tree snags on the left before the gully.
