wa_the_rake_traverse_route: Drive SR-20 east to Newhalem. Just after crossing Goodell Creek, take the first left onto a small road and turn immediately left at the T, then take the right branch uphill to the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp; the climbers' path starts just back down the road from the camp. An overnight North Cascades wilderness permit, walk-up only from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center, is required to camp in Terror or Crescent Creek basins.
Follow the unmaintained climbers' path up the old roadbed along Goodell Creek; about 1.5 miles in it fords two branches of the creek, which can run high and fast during snowmelt.
Continue up the old roadbed along Goodell Creek to roughly 4 miles, where a stone cairn marks the boot path leaving the roadbed to climb steeply into the Terror Creek drainage.

Climb the steep boot path up the Terror Creek drainage on faint tread through dense brush, including a Class 3 root-pull section at a cliff band, then break out onto heather and talus to the camp at treeline in Terror Basin.
From camp, climb west toward the Barrier, the steep headwall of the basin: a loose, grassy ledge near 6,100 ft leads to class 3 scrambling on rotten rock up to the crossing notch.
Cross the notch and descend the easy snow ramp on the far side into Crescent Creek Basin, then contour north to the high camp on the south side of Mount Terror.

From camp, head north up to the deep, rubble-choked gully that leads to the notch between Mount Terror and The Rake, and climb it staying right on slightly harder but far more solid class 3 rock rather than in the debris of its bed.

Finish the gully to the Terror-Rake notch. The ridge starts immediately above on very steep rock with old fixed pins; follow roughly half a mile of serrated crest, mixed 4th and 5th class up to 5.9, to the summit.
wa_the_west_face: Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles and turn left onto the climbers' trail marked by wooden posts into the basin below the Liberty Bell Group. Walk past South Early Winters Spire and the chockstone-filled chasm that splits the two spires, then traverse left along the base of North Early Winters Spire to the shared start with the Northwest Corner.
wa_three_fingers_r1: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east to about milepost 7 and turn left (north) onto Forest Road 41, Tupso Pass Road. The road is closed to vehicles at the washed-out Canyon Creek bridge; park there and walk or bike the remaining 8 to 9 miles, staying on FR 41 past the side roads and then turning right onto FR 4160 to the trailhead at its end. A free self-issued wilderness permit is required.
wa_three_fingers_r2: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east to about milepost 7 and turn left (north) onto Forest Road 41, Tupso Pass Road. The road is closed to vehicles at the washed-out Canyon Creek bridge; park there and walk or bike the remaining 8 to 9 miles, staying on FR 41 past the side roads and then turning right onto FR 4160 to the trailhead at its end. A free self-issued wilderness permit is required.
wa_three_fingers_south_peak_lookout: Follow Trail #641 up through forest to Saddle Lake at about 2.5 miles, the last easy water; there is no camping within 200 ft of the lake and no fires from here on. Continue climbing out of the timber into the open meadows of Goat Flats at about 4.5 miles, the best camping on the route.
From Goat Flats the trail contours and climbs about 2 more miles along the ridge to Tin Can Gap, where the maintained tread effectively ends. Snow can cover this stretch well into summer.

Past the gap, cross to the north side of the ridge and drop off-trail onto the top of the Queest-Alb Glacier. Cross it with axe and crampons, minding the moat between ice and rock and any open crevasses, then scramble rock and snow on the far side to the foot of the summit block. Three stacked ladders pinned into the rock climb the final band to the lookout; the move from the second to the third is the awkward one.
wa_tomyhoi_peak_southeast_ridge: From Glacier, follow SR 542 (Mount Baker Highway) east about 12 miles and turn left onto Twin Lakes Road (FR 3065) at the east end of the WSDOT Shuksan maintenance facility. Drive 4.5 miles up the switchbacks to the Tomyhoi Lake / Yellow Aster Butte Trailhead, where roadside parking is limited. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.
wa_trapper_mountain_north_couloir: Follow the Cascade Pass Trail as it switchbacks up through forest and then traverses open slopes to the pass, about 3.7 miles and 1,700 ft above the lot.

From the pass descend east into Pelton Basin. Beyond the basin there is no trail: cross Pelton Creek, work southeast up the shoulder of Pelton Peak to the saddle above Trapper Lake, then descend very steeply to the lake at about 4,170 ft. The peak and its north couloir stand directly across the water to the southwest.
wa_trapper_mountain_south_slopes: From SR-20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River and drive the Cascade River Road about 23 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, around 3,650 ft. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is narrow gravel with potholes, steep near the top. Overnight stays in the park need a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Follow the Cascade Pass Trail about 3.7 miles to the pass and down the east side into Pelton Basin. From the lowest tent sites take a faint boot path down toward Pelton Creek, cross at the cairns, and continue through low scrub, alder and braided streams on an on-and-off fisherman's path, then make a flat, marshy walk along the inlet stream to the lake at about 4,170 ft.
wa_true_grit_2: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, around 2,400 ft, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Take Sunrise Mine Trail No. 707 across the unbridged South Fork Stillaguamish, up Wirtz Basin and the loose, narrow couloir to Headlee Pass at about 4,720 ft, 2.7 miles in. Beyond, drop briefly, cross talus to Vesper Creek and follow it to Vesper Lake at about 4,950 ft, the last reliable water, then climb talus and slabs to the two large cairns on the saddle at about 5,700 ft, with Copper Lake below to the northwest.

Climb third-class slabs about 30 ft above the cairns onto the heather ledge system of the north face and follow the goat trail across the ledges to the start. Expect steep snow on the ledges into early-to-mid summer. The first pitch ends at a bolted belay directly beneath an obvious narrow chimney; with no chimney above, you are not on the route.

Climb five pitches: easy granite to the bolted belay under the chimney, the chimney or the corner to its right, slab and a small overhang to a cramped stance, the long finger-to-hand splitter crack, and an easy finishing pitch to the top of the headwall.
wa_up_in_arms: Drive SR-20 to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway between mileposts 161 and 162, about a mile west of Washington Pass, at roughly 5,200 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The highway over the pass is closed in winter.

Hike the Blue Lake Trail and take the climbers' path toward the Beckey Gully. As you reach Concord Tower's west face, head uphill staying close to the wall to the base, about 25 ft left of a large corner and well left of the South Face routes, then climb six pitches to the summit.
wa_vesper_peak_north_face_ragged_edge: Follow Sunrise Mine Trail No. 707 across the South Fork Stillaguamish on logs, a real obstacle in high runoff, then up through Wirtz Basin onto cairned talus and up the narrow, loose couloir to Headlee Pass at about 4,720 ft, roughly 2.7 miles in. Watch for rockfall from parties above.

Continue past the pass into the lake basin between Sperry and Vesper and follow the main summit trail up talus and slabs to about 5,600 to 5,700 ft. Leave it there and head north-northwest across the slabs to the two large cairns on the saddle, with Copper Lake in view to the northwest.

Do not drop into the saddle floor. Climb third-class slabs about 30 ft above the cairns onto the heather-covered ledges of the north face and traverse them roughly 800 ft to the original start, gained by fourth-class moves on an up-then-right arch. In June expect steep snow on the ledges and carry an axe and crampons.

Climb six pitches: traverse hard right on a grassy ledge to the white dike, up the bolted dike slab, the arete past old pins, stacked blocks, the airy traverse out the ragged east edge, and a long easy arete to the summit.
wa_vesper_peak_standard_route: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Take Trail 707 across the unbridged South Fork Stillaguamish and up through forest and a talus basin to the steep, loose couloir and Headlee Pass, about 2.7 miles in. Traverse below Sperry Peak into the upper Vesper Creek basin, leave the lake trail at the creek crossing, and climb the steep bootpath to treeline, then about 1,000 ft of granite slabs on the central rib, following cairns, to the summit.
wa_waterfall_buttress: Walk the old roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing to the original road end, then 20 to 30 minutes on the old trail to a dry streambed about 50 feet wide full of white boulders. Go down the bed about 200 feet, then left into the alder for the informal path; follow it upvalley to the ford of Squire Creek and on along the fading trail and dry creek bed into the open basin. The buttress is the rib just left of the big slab waterfall; hike talus to its toe.
wa_west_face: From Darrington, drive SR 530 north about 8 miles to the Suiattle River Road (FS Road 26) and follow it east about 20 miles to the Downey Creek Trailhead at about 1,450 feet, just past the Downey Creek bridge; the trail leaves the north side of the road and parking is on the south side. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required. The Suiattle River Road is prone to washout closures, so check its status first.

Follow the Downey Creek Trail to the footlog over Bachelor Creek, then the unmaintained, brushy Bachelor Creek path to Cub Lake, over Itswoot Ridge and across glacier ground to the Dome-Chickamin col. Cross the Chickamin Glacier to the west side of the peak and stop directly beneath the summit; the West Face starts in the chimney on the left side of the face and climbs four pitches, finishing up the face and left to the summit.
wa_west_face_2: From Darrington, drive SR 530 north about 8 miles to the Suiattle River Road (FS Road 26) and follow it east about 20 miles to the Downey Creek Trailhead at about 1,450 feet, just past the Downey Creek bridge; the trail leaves the north side of the road and parking is on the south side. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required. The Suiattle River Road is prone to washout closures, so check its status first.

From the col, make a descending traverse across the Chikamin Glacier, watching for crevasses and crossing the bergschrund on a snow bridge, to the foot of the West Face. Scramble along the ramp beneath the left side of the face to where it splits; the route starts just past the split at a small cairn. Climb five pitches to the terminal terrace, then move right along the terrace to a chimney that leads to the summit.
wa_west_ridge_2: From the pullout, follow the unmarked boot path down the talus and into the forest, cross Early Winters Creek on a log, and climb steeply up the timbered rib on the north side of Burgundy Creek. About two hours of steep walking reaches the bench camp at about 6,500 feet, where a spring provides the last reliable water.

Leave the trail to the col at the bench and contour right, south, around the bench to the toe of the pinnacle's west ridge; the start is marked by a chockstone jammed at the foot of the ridge. Climb seven or eight pitches of hand and finger cracks along the crest, with the crux steep twin finger cracks about halfway, and finish on an exposed, runout face pitch to the summit.
wa_west_twin_needle_south_route: Follow the old, overgrown Goodell Creek logging road up the valley for about 3.5 miles to the fork where the road tread ends and a cairned climbers' path continues toward Terror Creek.

From camp, drop about 300 feet below the moraine to the head of Crescent Creek, then make a rising traverse beneath the gully system on the peak's south side, past the buttress that divides it. Avoid the right-hand gully, which ends in a closed chimney; take the minor rib on its climber's left and pitch through the chockstones in the gully above to the Eye Col notch at about 7,400 feet.
From the Eye Col, climb a 5.7 pitch up the white slabs on the east face, then scramble the easier ground above to the true summit.
wa_western_dihedral: Walk the old Squire Creek roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing to two cut logs, one on either side of the road, with old logging cable visible, and turn right there onto a well-beaten boot track. It drops to a ford of the creek, then climbs steeply through old growth, steep and dirty near the top, into open grassland and the main grassy saddle at the foot of the South Face, about three hours from the car.
wa_whitehorse_mountain_nw_shoulder: From Darrington, drive SR 530 west about 5 miles to the community of Whitehorse and turn left (south) onto 387th Ave NE, also called Old Mine Road, at the gas station and convenience store. Follow it 0.6 mile to its dead end at a steel gate and a barricade of large boulders, at about 900 ft, and park there. A free self-issued Boulder River Wilderness permit applies.

Cross the boulders and wooden bridge on foot and walk the old road about 1.25 miles to the signed start of Trail #653, which switchbacks up to the flat near 3,200 ft. A brushy boot path continues to snow; traverse south into a broad snow couloir and climb it to Lone Tree Pass, go east and drop southeast to a small lake bench, make the long rising traverse east to High Pass, then cross the glacier to the summit.
wa_wilmans_peak_scramble: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 31 miles to Barlow Pass, at about 2,360 ft, where the pavement ends, and park in the Barlow Pass lot. The gated gravel road to Monte Cristo leaves from here and is open only to foot and bike traffic. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.
Walk around the gate and follow the gravel Monte Cristo road about 1 mile to where the Weden Creek trail toward Gothic Basin branches off, just before the road reaches the South Fork Sauk River.
Cross the South Fork Sauk River on a large log or by fording, since there is no bridge, and continue up the road about 3 miles to the old Monte Cristo townsite.

From the townsite, cross the bridge and pick up the Glacier Basin Trail #719 at the old Dumas Street sign. It runs fairly level through forest for about three-quarters of a mile, then turns rough and rocky up to the falls, where it climbs wet, slick bedrock beside them.

Continue up the Glacier Basin Trail above the falls through about half a mile of steep, rocky scrambling, then up smooth steep slopes until the ground levels out in Glacier Basin, where established campsites sit on the timbered knoll of Mystery Hill and the maintained trail ends.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_finger_of_fatwa: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_north_ridge: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_middle_finger_b: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Hike Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles to Andrews Pass, keeping left near 5.5 miles and turning right at the Peepsight Trail junction. Descend 3 miles to the Spanish Camp guard station; just before the cabin take the trail on the right 3 miles up to Upper Cathedral Lake. Middle Finger, the biggest buttress on the wall above the lake, is a 15-minute walk and scramble from the shore.

From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Hike Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles to Andrews Pass, keeping left near 5.5 miles and turning right at the Peepsight Trail junction. Descend 3 miles to the Spanish Camp guard station; just before the cabin take the trail on the right 3 miles up to Upper Cathedral Lake. The route is on the right side of Middle Finger, the biggest buttress on the wall above the lake, about 15 minutes from the shore.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_pilgrimage_to_m: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Hike Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles to Andrews Pass, keeping left near 5.5 miles and turning right at the Peepsight Trail junction. Descend 3 miles to the Spanish Camp guard station; just before the cabin take the trail on the right 3 miles up to Upper Cathedral Lake. Walk around the lake to Kaʼaba, the stepped buttress two left of Middle Finger (the biggest), and scramble to the large block at its base.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_west_route: From Highway 20 in Winthrop, turn onto County Road 1213 (West Chewuch Road) and follow it about 6 miles to where it joins Forest Road 51. Continue north on FR 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park, and a free self-issued Pasayten Wilderness permit is required.

Hike Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles over Andrews Pass, then 3 miles down to the Spanish Camp guard station, and take the trail on the right just before the cabin 3 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. From the lake follow the trail around the toe of the west ridge about half a mile to a boot path at about 7,200 ft; climb grass and scree into the basin at 8,000 ft, then walk the plateau to its highest point.
wa_cathedral_peak_southwest_route: From SR 20 in Winthrop, turn north onto West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213), which joins FS Road 51 after about 6 miles. Continue up the Chewuch valley on FS 51 to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at about 3,050 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

Hike Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles to Andrews Pass, descend Spanish Creek past the Spanish Creek Trail junction, and just before the guard station cabin take the Cathedral Lakes trail on the right about 3 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. Walk 0.6 mile toward Cathedral Pass, leave the trail just short of it, and climb sandy slopes, ducked class 2-3 granite and a hidden cleft below the west ridge to the chockstone step-across and the summit.
wa_lake_mountain_pasayten_scramble: From SR 20 about 14 miles west of Winthrop, turn onto Lost River Road (County Road 9140) and follow it through Mazama to the end of the pavement at about 7.5 miles, where it becomes Harts Pass Road (FS 5400). In about a quarter mile turn right into the Monument Creek Trailhead at about 2,400 ft. No parking pass is needed; self-issue a free wilderness permit at the kiosk.
wa_mount_ballard_south: Drive SR 20 to the Canyon Creek Trailhead just past milepost 141, about 33 miles east of Marblemount or 55 miles west of Winthrop; the large parking area is at about 1,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee (self-pay station on site) is required to park.
Follow the Canyon Creek trail upstream along Canyon Creek about 5.7 miles to the ford of Mill Creek, the last easy water before the long climb.
From the ford continue a short way to the junction where the Mill Creek Trail toward Azurite Pass leaves the Canyon Creek trail.
Turn up the Mill Creek Trail and follow it up the Mill Creek valley. Within a couple of miles the tread begins to vanish under slide alder and downed timber, and the going becomes a slow bushwhack.

From the basin, push north through the brush band low on the south slopes onto steep, rocky ground, where several look-alike chutes split the face around 7,400 ft. Read the ground before committing to one, and do not follow the clean-looking south ridge, which is blocked higher by a notch with a gendarme.
wa_mount_carru_scramble: From Fred's Lake, switchback up the open slope to the ridge-crest pass directly above the lake, with views back down to the lake and east into the Eureka Creek headwaters.
Drop east off the pass into the Eureka Creek headwater basin and rock-hop the creek.
wa_mount_lago_south_slope_south_face: Follow Robinson Creek Trail #478 up Robinson Creek to Robinson Pass (6,220 ft) and drop north into the Middle Fork Pasayten. Continue north down the valley past the Whistler Cutoff and the first Eureka Creek Trail junction, and about 4.8 miles beyond the Whistler Cutoff turn east on the Eureka Creek Trail and climb along Berk Creek to Fred's Lake.

From Fred's Lake, climb to the pass on the crest above the lake and drop east into the upper Eureka Creek basin on the faint, unmaintained middle section of the Eureka Creek Trail; the crossing of upper Eureka Creek can be difficult in snowmelt. Continue east and up into Shellrock Basin on the south side of the Lago-Carru ridge.

Climb north up Lago's broad south slope, leaving the heather for continuous scree, talus and loose rock ribs; there is no path and no single line. Gain the summit ridge and follow the faint boot path along the crest to the true high point, staying back from the north side, which drops off in a huge cliff.
Descend Lago's southwest slope to the Lago-Carru saddle at about 7,600 ft, then scramble up Carru's southeast slope and ridge to its summit.
wa_ne_couloir: From Winthrop, take the East Chewuch River Road north about 6.5 miles and, before it crosses the Chewuch River, turn right onto FR 37. Follow FR 37 about 13 miles, turn left onto FR 39 and drive about 7.5 miles, past Freezeout Pass, to Tiffany Springs Campground at about 6,760 ft. FR 37 from Conconully reaches the same junction. The gravel is rough, closed to trailers and usually snowbound until late June. Northwest Forest Pass required.

Take Trail #373 from across the road past Tiffany Lake and up to Honeymoon Pass at about 7,150 ft (about 45 minutes). Leave the trail and traverse south along the grassy east slope below the crest into the small cirque under the north face at about 7,360 ft, then climb the longest, most continuous snow gully on the left side of the face to the summit ridge and the summit.
wa_ne_ridge: From SR 20 in Winthrop, take the West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213) about 6 miles to where it joins FR 51, then follow FR 51 up the Chewuch valley about 22 miles to the end of the pavement and turn right into the Andrews Creek Trailhead at about 3,050 ft. Fill out the free self-issue Pasayten Wilderness permit at the trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park.

Follow Andrews Creek Trail #504 about 12 miles to Andrews Pass, descend to Spanish Creek and cross it to join the Boundary Trail, then follow the Boundary Trail to the Cathedral Lakes basin below the peak, about 19 miles in all. From the Boundary Trail, scramble the grassy southeast slope directly up from the trail to gain the ridge and follow its long broken crest, past the dike about 400 ft below the top, to the summit.
wa_north_tower_ridge_route: From Winthrop, take the East Chewuch River Road north about 6.5 miles and, before it crosses the Chewuch River, turn right onto FR 37. Follow FR 37 about 13 miles, turn left onto FR 39 and drive about 7.5 miles, past Freezeout Pass, to Tiffany Springs Campground at about 6,760 ft. FR 37 from Conconully reaches the same junction. The gravel is rough, closed to trailers and usually snowbound until late June. Northwest Forest Pass required.

Take Trail #373 from across the road past Tiffany Lake to Honeymoon Pass at about 7,150 ft, then traverse south on the grassy east slope into the small cirque under the north face (about 7,360 ft) and climb the boulder field to the foot of the rock at about 7,600 ft. Climb the lower rock on the right side of the face onto the ridge, go straight up the North Tower by its flaring chimney, and walk the crest to Tiffany's summit.
wa_ptarmigan_peak_pasayten_scramble: Turn onto the Eureka Creek Trail and climb east along Berk Creek to Freds Lake, the last reliable water and a common camp, then continue up the fading tread to Freds Pass at about 7,100 ft.

Drop east from the pass into the head of the Eureka Creek basin and cross it eastward on faint tread that is often lost in blowdown, so cairns and map work are needed; the creek crossing can be difficult in snowmelt. Climb to the broad bench just southwest of Shellrock Pass at about 7,500 ft.
wa_robinson_mountain_southeast_ridge: From Winthrop, drive Highway 20 west about 15 miles and turn right onto Lost River Road (County Road 9140). After half a mile turn left to stay on Lost River Road, drive 7.5 paved miles, then continue about 1.25 miles on gravel Forest Road 5400 to the Robinson Creek Trailhead on the right, at about 2,500 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is needed to park.

Take Trail #478 about 2.5 to 2.8 miles to the bridge over Beauty Creek (~3,560 ft); just past it turn right uphill onto the unmarked Beauty Creek trail. Follow it 1.5 miles on the creek's northwest side to a tributary crossing near 5,200 ft, then turn left and climb northwest through meadow to the tarn at ~6,750 ft. Climb scree to a gap in the southeast ridge and follow the crest about a mile northwest, past Point 8,280, to a short exposed Class 3 step below the top.
wa_tower_arete: From Winthrop, drive north on East Chewuch Road about 6.5 miles and, before it crosses the Chewuch River, turn right onto FR 37. Follow it about 13 miles, then turn left onto FR 39 for about 7.5 miles to Tiffany Springs Campground at about 6,760 ft. From Conconully, take County Road 2017 about 3 miles to FR 37, follow it about 21 miles, and turn right onto FR 39 for 8 miles. Long gravel either way; display a Northwest Forest Pass.

Cross FR 39 to Tiffany Lake Trail #373, pass Tiffany Lake and climb to Honeymoon Pass at about 7,150 ft, then leave the trail and traverse south across open grassy slopes into the small cirque under the North Face. Scramble the rocky ridge onto the arete, follow the exposed crest, bypass the vertical step on its left at fourth class, then go over the top of the tower and along the crest onto the summit slope, which leads to the top.
wa_west_craggy_peak_standard_route: Follow Copper Glance Trail #519 up the old mining road about 1.5 miles to the ruins of the Copper Glance mine, cross Copper Glance Creek (a ford when the bridge is out, high in early season), and continue through burned forest past a small pond to Copper Glance Lake at about 6,260 ft. Carry on into the open basin above the lake to the creek crossing at about 6,400 ft; fill water here, as there is none higher up.
From the crossing, walk a short way north-west up the basin to the knoll at about 6,600 ft that serves as the usual camp.

Walk up into the cirque directly beneath the peak and take the chute that slants up and right across the headwall to a col on the south ridge; it often holds a streak of snow into summer, and the right one heads for a notch in the skyline rather than steepening into a wall. Above the col, class 2 rock and a short upper couloir lead onto the easy summit ridge and the top.
wa_windy_peak_iron_gate_trail: From Loomis, drive north on County Road 9425 for 2 miles, then turn left onto Toats Coulee Road (County Road 4066), which becomes FR 39. Follow it about 14 miles to the spur signed for Iron Gate, FR 3900-500, and drive that about 6 miles to the trailhead. FR 3900-500 is a rough high-clearance road, not for passenger cars or trailers. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park, plus a free self-issue wilderness permit.

Hike north on the Boundary Trail #533, going straight through the four-way junction with the Clutch Creek and Deer Park trails, to Sunny Pass. There turn west onto the Windy Peak Trail, keep left at the next two junctions with the Basin Creek and Windy Creek trails, and take the short spur that climbs the last 200 ft to the summit.
wa_windy_peak_trail: From the trailhead, Windy Peak Trail #342 climbs steeply on switchbacks through burned lodgepole pine for about 2.5 miles and 1,300 ft to the signed Pasayten Wilderness boundary. There is no reliable water on this stretch, so carry what you need from the car.
wa_wolframite_mountain_scramble: Follow Chewuch River Trail #510 north from the trailhead, staying near the river. Chewuch Falls is a landmark about 2.5 miles in; farther on the trail crosses the 2001 burn, where standing snags can fall in wind. Continue about 8.5 miles in all to the established camp on the river roughly a quarter mile before the Tungsten Creek ford.
Continue about a quarter mile up the trail to the unbridged ford of Tungsten Creek. It runs knee-deep and fast in snowmelt or after rain, so cross early in the day.
Just beyond the ford, reach the signed junction where Tungsten Creek Trail #534 leaves the Chewuch River Trail, and take the Tungsten Creek Trail.

Tungsten Creek Trail #534 climbs about 6.2 miles and 2,100 ft, steeply at first through trees with a few switchbacks, then along a sidehill through meadows, crossing Cinch Creek. The creek the trail follows on its last stretch is the final dependable water. The trail ends at its junction with Boundary Trail #533 at the old mine camp, with ruins and iron pipe on the slope.
wa_andersons_thumb_standard: Ride or walk the closed Dosewallips Road to the old ranger station, then follow the Dosewallips River Trail to Dose Forks and turn onto the West Fork Dosewallips Trail. It climbs the valley through old-growth forest past Big Timber and Diamond Meadows camps to Honeymoon Meadows, about 15 miles from the washout. The West Fork crossing at Honeymoon Meadows can be hazardous in spring or after heavy rain.

Continue up the West Fork Dosewallips Trail past the La Crosse Pass junction and Camp Siberia, switchbacking to Anderson Pass at 4,464 ft, the Dosewallips-Quinault divide, where the trail meets the one descending to Enchanted Valley. This is the end of maintained tread.

At the pass leave the main trail and follow the climbers' boot path north over talus and heather benches, about a mile and 700 ft of gain, to the small tarn camp on the old Anderson Glacier moraine near 5,100 ft. Fill water here; above the moraine there is only snowmelt.
wa_buckhorn_marmot_pass: From Quilcene, drive US 101 south about 1.5 miles and turn right (west) onto Penny Creek Road. After about 1.5 miles bear left onto Big Quilcene River Road, FR 27, and follow it about 9.25 miles to FR 2750. Turn left and drive about 4.75 miles on this narrow, single-lane road to the Upper Big Quilcene Trailhead at its end, about 2,600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park; no wilderness permit is required for a day trip.
wa_chimney_peak_the_chimney: Follow the East Fork Quinault River Trail from Graves Creek, along an old roadbed for the first 2 miles and then down to cross the river on Pony Bridge at about 2.5 miles. Continue up the rainforest valley on a gentle grade past O'Neil Creek, No Name Creek and Pyrites Creek camps, then cross the river again on a high bridge to reach the meadows of Enchanted Valley and the chalet at about 2,000 ft, nearly 14 miles from the trailhead.
wa_honeymoon_route: Follow Upper Dungeness Trail #833.2 about 1 mile and turn right onto Royal Basin Trail #832, a few steps before the footlog over Royal Creek. The trail switchbacks up through old growth into the national park, stays left at the Maynard Burn Trail junction, and climbs the Royal Creek valley past talus fields and a waterfall to Royal Lake at about 7.2 miles and 5,100 ft.

Continue about a mile into Upper Royal Basin, then cross the moraine southwest to the big snow slope on the west edge of the northeast face. Climb it nearly to the low point of the Deception-Martin ridge, branch left into the steep side gully, then traverse left up a second gully to the summit ridge. Drop to the glacier remnant, traverse west around Gilhooley Tower, and walk class 2 ground to the summit.
wa_inner_constance_northwest_buttress: From US 101 across from Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Road, go about a mile and turn left on Palo Alto Road, which becomes FS Road 28 at the forest boundary. Turn right on FS 2880 past Dungeness Forks Campground, then stay left on FS 2870 for 8.7 miles to the trailhead just across the Dungeness River bridge. Large lot and vault toilet, no water; a Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required.
wa_inner_constance_seans_route: From US 101 across from Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Road, go about a mile and turn left on Palo Alto Road, which becomes FS Road 28 at the forest boundary. Turn right on FS 2880 past Dungeness Forks Campground, then stay left on FS 2870 for 8.7 miles to the trailhead just across the Dungeness River bridge. Large lot and vault toilet, no water; a Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required.

Hike Upper Dungeness Trail #833 past Camp Handy (about 3.4 miles) and Boulder Shelter (about 6.2 miles), then the Constance Pass trail into the park to Home Lake at about 9.3 miles. Work south-southwest up the Home Creek basin to the boulder camp northwest of the peak, climb the scree to the ramp and the crack system, exit the cave under the roof, and rejoin the Northwest Buttress for its last low-angle pitch to the summit.
wa_lena_lake_to_mt_stone_traverse: From Hoodsport, drive north on US 101 about 14 miles and turn left onto Hamma Hamma River Road (FS Road 25) near milepost 318. Follow it about 7.5 paved miles to the Lena Lake Trailhead, a lot for about 30 cars. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park.
wa_mount_anderson_eel_glacier: Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips Road about a mile to the washout, take the short bypass trail around it, and follow the old roadbed about 5.6 more miles to the Dosewallips Ranger Station. Take the Dosewallips River Trail 1.4 miles to the West Fork junction, then the West Fork Dosewallips Trail upstream past Big Timber and Diamond Meadows to Honeymoon Meadows, fording the West Fork on the way, and climb past Camp Siberia to Anderson Pass.
wa_mount_angeles_standard: From the east end of the visitor center lot, follow the paved High Ridge Trail uphill to the junction with the short spur to Sunrise Point; stay on the main trail toward Klahhane Ridge.
wa_mount_barnes_scramble: From Port Angeles, drive west on US 101 about 29 miles, past Lake Crescent, and turn left onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road. Follow it about 14 miles, past the hot springs resort, to the parking lot at the end of the road. A national park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit.
wa_mount_cameron_standard: From Obstruction Point follow the Grand Pass Trail south along the open crest of Lillian Ridge, descend into Grand Valley and follow the trail up the valley past Moose and Gladys Lakes to Grand Pass, about 6 miles from the trailhead.

Drop steeply south off Grand Pass on the Cameron side, a descent that is slick in wet weather or lingering snow, through brushy overgrowth to the wet meadow where the trail crosses several unbridged branches of Cameron Creek. The tread is easy to lose here in fog or high brush.
Continue up along Cameron Creek into the upper basin below Cameron Pass to the established camp sites at about 6,000 ft. A bear canister is required and there are no fires.
Continue up the Cameron Pass Trail from the basin to Cameron Pass. Steep snow can cover the climbers' path on the final slopes into late July or August, so carry an ice axe.
wa_mount_carrie_se_route: Hike past Sol Duc Falls and stay on the Sol Duc River Trail past the Deer Lake junction, climbing about 7 more miles up the valley to Heart Lake, the last reliable water. Climb about half a mile to the High Divide crest and turn east on the primitive trail toward Cat Basin.

Follow the High Divide trail to its end, then the thin path along the exposed south side of Cat Peak to the Catwalk, a narrow class 2-3 rock and heather ridge where a fall could be fatal. Push through brush to Boston Charlie's Camp, switchback up Carrie's southwest ridge, contour around the top of the loose south-facing scree basin near 6,500 ft, and finish at the true summit on the basin's far right (east) end.
wa_mount_christie_west: Follow the North Fork Quinault River Trail upstream through old-growth rainforest about 2.5 miles to Wolf Bar, a gravel bar beside the river with several roomy sites.
Continue up the river trail to Halfway House Camp, a forested camp near the 5-mile mark.
Continue upstream to Elip Creek: ford the creek and pass the junction with the Elip Creek Trail, staying on the North Fork Quinault River Trail. A streamside camp sits right at the junction.
Stay on the North Fork Quinault River Trail upstream to Trapper Shelter, a three-sided shelter near 8 miles that is for day or emergency use only.

Continue up the valley on the North Fork Quinault River Trail, fording the North Fork at Sixteen Mile Camp, which can run thigh-deep in high water, and climb to Low Divide on the Quinault-Elwha divide.

From Low Divide take the rough path into Martins Park and the Martin Lakes basin. From lower Martins Park climb the broad snow-and-rock couloir that runs south toward the peak, about 2,100 ft, to the saddle on the north ridge near 5,600 ft. Crampons and an axe are standard on firm morning snow.

From the saddle drop down loose gravelly slopes to the lower edge of the Christie Glacier, rope up and cross it, stepping over the moat at its top to the high col east of the summit. Climb the loose Class 4 cliff above the col, push through dense krummholz, and scramble the Class 2-3 southeast ridge to the summit.
wa_mount_clark_standard: Follow the trail upstream along the Dungeness River about 1 mile to where it forks a few steps before a footlog bridge over Royal Creek.

Bear right at the fork onto the Royal Basin Trail without crossing the bridge, and follow it up the Royal Creek valley past the Royal Creek camp area to Lower Royal Meadow, a broad, stream-crossed meadow at about 4,700 ft.
Continue up the trail about a mile and 400 ft more to Royal Lake at about 5,100 ft.
Continue past the lake about a mile and 500 to 600 ft more into the meadows and tarns of Upper Royal Basin, where you leave the maintained trail.
Leave the trail and climb heather and talus to the rim of the glacial moraine ringing Surprise Basin, then drop onto its snowfields. They are icy early in the season and soft by afternoon.
wa_mount_claywood_standard: From US-101 in Port Angeles, follow Hurricane Ridge Road about 17 miles up to Hurricane Ridge, then take the unpaved Obstruction Point Road about 8 miles east to its end at about 6,150 ft. The road is narrow, one-lane gravel, unsuitable for trailers, and usually open only from about July into October. A national park entrance fee applies, and overnight trips need a wilderness permit reserved in advance and a bear canister.
From the trailhead follow the Grand Pass Trail south onto the open crest of Lillian Ridge, a narrow, wind-exposed ridge with steep drops into the Badger and Lillian River valleys on either side.
Continue along the ridge, then descend well over 1,000 ft into Grand Valley and follow the Grand Pass Trail up the valley past Moose Lake to Gladys Lake at about 5,490 ft.
Fill water at the lake, then climb the trail about 1.5 miles and 1,000 ft up the head of the valley to Grand Pass.
Drop steeply south off Grand Pass into Cameron Basin, then climb steeply up the basin to Cameron Pass. The last part is loose and rocky in spots and holds snow into midsummer, so carry an ice axe.
wa_mount_constance_finger_traverse: From US-101 at Brinnon, turn west onto the Dosewallips Road and drive about 9 miles to its end, where the road is bermed off at the washout; park here at about 550 ft. No parking pass is needed, but camping at Lake Constance requires an Olympic National Park wilderness permit.

Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips Road about 5 miles to the unsigned Lake Constance climbers' trail at about 1,450 ft. Climb the steep, unmaintained boot path, roughly 3,300 ft in about 2 miles with roots and rock steps that need hands, to Lake Constance, and follow its east shore to the camps at the north end.

From the north-end camps go north up Avalanche Canyon about 0.6 mile and turn east up the South Chute as soon as the Cat Ears tower comes into view, to the notch beside it. Cross the saddle, drop about 150 ft, climb a second scree gully to a notch, and follow ledges marked by cairns and faded white paint to the Finger Traverse. Past it, cross the snow basin, climb the ramp and scree to the ridge, and take the summit tower from its north side.
wa_mount_constance_north_chimney: From US 101 at Brinnon, turn west onto Dosewallips Road (FR 2610) at milepost 306, just north of Dosewallips State Park, and drive about 8.5 miles to where the road is closed to vehicles at the washout; park along the roadside. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips roadbed about 5 miles up the valley to the Lake Constance climbers' path at about 1,400 ft. The steep, unmaintained path gains about 3,300 ft in roughly 2 miles, past Half Acre Rock at 0.8 mile and over exposed rock ledges and short cliff bands above 1.3 miles, to the lake; camps are at its north end.

From the north end of the lake, head into Avalanche Canyon and turn east up the South Chute as soon as the Cat Ears come into view, climbing about 1,900 ft of scree to the saddle near 6,600 ft. Drop about 150 ft, climb a second scree gully to the notch near 7,300 ft, cross the Terrible or Finger Traverse to the base of the summit block, and climb the chimney on its north side to the top.
wa_mount_constance_north_chute: From US 101 at Brinnon, turn west onto Dosewallips Road (FR 2610) at milepost 306, just north of Dosewallips State Park, and drive about 8.5 miles to where the road is closed to vehicles at the washout; park along the roadside. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

Walk or bike the closed road about 5 miles to the Lake Constance climbers' path and climb it about 2 miles to the lake. Head north up Avalanche Canyon past the Cat Ears and the mouth of the South Chute to the North Chute, the last major chute on the canyon's east side, and climb it to the ledge where the South Chute line joins. Cross the Finger Traverse (or the Terrible Traverse) and finish over the summit block.
wa_mount_constance_terrible_traverse: From US 101 at Brinnon, turn west onto Dosewallips Road (FR 2610) at milepost 306, just north of Dosewallips State Park, and drive about 8.5 miles to where the road is closed to vehicles at the washout; park along the roadside. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips roadbed about 5 miles up the valley to the Lake Constance climbers' path at about 1,400 ft. The steep, unmaintained path gains about 3,300 ft in roughly 2 miles, past Half Acre Rock at 0.8 mile and over exposed rock ledges and short cliff bands above 1.3 miles, to the lake; camps are at its north end.

Go up Avalanche Canyon past the Thumb and climb the South Chute, turning east as soon as the Cat Ears come into view, to the saddle near 6,600 ft. Drop a little, climb the second scree gully to the notch near 7,300 ft, then lose a little height and traverse north on ledges to cross the Terrible Traverse at about 7,435 ft. Beyond it, follow the Key Ledge onto the upper scree slope and finish up the summit block.
wa_mount_constance_west_arete: From US 101 at Brinnon, turn west onto Dosewallips Road (FR 2610) at milepost 306, just north of Dosewallips State Park, and drive about 8.5 miles to where the road is closed to vehicles at the washout; park along the roadside. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips roadbed about 5 miles up the valley to the Lake Constance climbers' path at about 1,400 ft. The steep, unmaintained path gains about 3,300 ft in roughly 2 miles, past Half Acre Rock at 0.8 mile and over exposed rock ledges and short cliff bands above 1.3 miles, to the lake; camps are at its north end.

From camp, go north up Avalanche Canyon past the Thumb, staying in the canyon past the South Chute turnoff, for about 1.5 miles of loose talus or firm snow to Crystal Pass at its head. From the pass, climb the West Arete, starting around a small tower and up a crack with fixed webbing, for about five pitches of mostly class 3-4 rock with a few low-fifth steps to the summit ridge, then scramble to the true summit.
wa_mount_cruiser_nw_face_corner: From US 101 in Hoodsport, follow SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) about 9 miles to a T-intersection, turn left and continue about 5.4 miles on what becomes FR 24, then turn right into Olympic National Park and drive about 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station and its large trailhead parking area. The last miles are gravel. A national park entrance pass is required.
wa_mount_cruiser_south_corner: From US 101 in Hoodsport, follow SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) about 9 miles to a T-intersection, turn left and continue about 5.4 miles on what becomes FR 24, then turn right into Olympic National Park and drive about 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station and its large trailhead parking area. The last miles are gravel. A national park entrance pass is required.

Follow the North Fork Skokomish River Trail about 3.7 miles to the Flapjack Lakes Trail junction, then climb the Flapjack Lakes Trail about 4 miles to the lakes. Continue about 1.5 miles up-basin toward Gladys Divide; just before the divide, leave the trail, cross a short stretch of talus and climb the steep snow or scree couloir southeast to Needle Pass, often firm enough to need crampons and an axe.

From Needle Pass, turn left (east) and scramble exposed class 3 to the top of Beta Peak, descend its right-most summit notch with one class 4 move and a short gully, then traverse high toward Cruiser and drop down a longer gully to its base. Climb the class 4 gully to the big chockstone, pass it on the left through the tunnel to the platform, and climb the two low-fifth pitches of the South Corner to the summit.
wa_mount_dana_scramble: From US-101 about 8 miles west of Port Angeles, turn south on Olympic Hot Springs Road into the Elwha Valley and drive to the Madison Falls parking area at the park boundary, where the road is closed to vehicles by flood damage. From there walk or bike the closed road and the Whiskey Bend Road, about 6 miles one way, to the trailhead. An Olympic National Park entrance pass applies, and overnight trips need a wilderness permit.
wa_mount_deception_standard: Follow the Upper Dungeness Trail about a mile to the junction just before the footlog over Royal Creek, turn right onto the Royal Basin Trail, and follow it up Royal Creek, through old growth and then open talus slopes, to Royal Lake at about 5,100 ft, roughly 7 miles from the trailhead.

Continue past Shelter Rock and Arrowhead Meadow into Upper Royal Basin at about 5,700 ft, then leave the trail and cross the moraine southwest to the snow or scree slope on the west edge of the northeast face. Climb it to the Deception-Martin saddle, drop about 100 ft onto the glacier remnant, go around the west side of Gilhooley Tower and finish on loose class 2 slopes to the summit.
wa_mount_ellinor_standard: From US-101 at Hoodsport, take SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) 9.3 miles to its end, turn right on FS Road 24 for 1.6 miles, then left on FS Road 2419 for 4.9 miles to the lower trailhead. Continue 1.7 miles farther and turn left on FS Road 2419-014 to the upper trailhead lot at its end, about 3,500 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Climb Trail #812's stacked switchbacks 0.3 mile to where the lower-trailhead trail joins at about 3,900 ft, then continue up the south ridge to the signed junction at timberline, about 4,500 ft. In summer take the trail left, switchbacking across rocky slopes and meadows through a notch to the summit; when snow fills it, most parties climb the chute to the right instead, with ice axe and traction.
wa_mount_ferry_standard: From Port Angeles drive US-101 west about 28 miles; just past Lake Crescent turn left on Sol Duc Hot Springs Road at the park sign, pay at the entrance station, and drive about 12 miles past the resort to the trailhead at the road end. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required to park, and overnight camps need a wilderness permit.
Follow the Sol Duc Falls Trail about 0.8 mile through old-growth forest to the bridge overlooking Sol Duc Falls.
Cross the bridge and bear right, pass the Lover's Lane Trail junction, and climb the Deer Lake Trail about 3 miles alongside Canyon Creek and its waterfalls to Deer Lake.

From Deer Lake continue south on the High Divide Trail, climbing through subalpine meadow onto the divide, then follow it east past Bogachiel Peak to the junction with the Sol Duc River Trail and drop a short way north to Heart Lake.
Climb back to the High Divide junction above the lake and continue east on the Cat Basin primitive trail to Cat Basin, where maintained tread ends.
Leave the maintained trail on the faint primitive route east, traversing the slopes of Cat Peak to the start of the Catwalk, the narrow exposed ridge linking Cat Peak to Mount Carrie.

From camp in Ferry Basin, climb to the broad bench east of the true summit, then up the slope of loose, sharp, shifting scree to the summit. It is sustained class 2-3 scrambling with no technical climbing; watch for the elk trails in the basin, which contour convincingly but do not lead to the summit.
wa_mount_johnson_standard: From US 101 at Blyn, head west toward Sequim for 1.7 miles and turn left on Louella Road, then left on Palo Alto Road for about 5.8 miles. Turn right on FR 2880, cross the Dungeness River past Dungeness Forks Campground, and go straight onto FR 2870. Bear right after 2.5 miles to stay on FR 2870, take the left fork 4.9 miles later, and in 1.6 miles cross the Dungeness again to the trailhead lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

Start up the Upper Dungeness Trail through forest along the Dungeness River for about 1 mile to the signed Royal Basin Trail junction, just before the footlog bridge. Bear right onto the Royal Basin Trail; the left fork continues up-valley toward Boulder Shelter.
Follow the Royal Basin Trail as it climbs gradually beside Royal Creek to the first designated trailside campsites at about 3,500 ft.

Continue up the valley alongside Royal Creek, crossing it on log bridges. Around mile 6 the grade steepens sharply, and the last mile gains about 500 ft on loose, eroded tread to Royal Lake at 5,100 ft.
Continue up-valley past Shelter Rock and Arrowhead Meadow on the climbers' path, about 0.8 mile and 500 ft, to the tarns and meadows of Upper Royal Basin, where the maintained trail ends.

Head cross-country west up heather benches and talus to the moraine rim of Surprise Basin, drop into the basin, and cross its snowfields to the 6,900 ft notch between Johnson on the left and Clark on the right. The talus above the rim is loose; wear helmets from the rim up.

From the notch, drop about 100 ft and climb Johnson's lower snowfield to its upper-left corner. There a ledge only a few feet wide leads left (south), squeezing past an outcrop onto the upper snowfield above a loose, outsloping drop.

Cross the upper snowfield to a little left of its center and exit up a rubbly, low-angle gully, then follow the base of a low wall around behind Sweat Spire and Gasp Pinnacle to the summit block. Leaving the snowfield too far right lands you in gullies that steepen and are hard to reverse. Climb the rightmost chimney (Class 4) and walk the crest to the top.
wa_mount_la_crosse_scramble: From US 101 about 15 miles south of Quilcene, turn west at the Duckabush Recreation Area sign onto Duckabush Road (FR 2510); the pavement ends at 3.6 miles. About 6 miles in, pass the horse parking area and bear right uphill onto spur FR 2510-060, reaching the trailhead in 0.1 mile. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required to park.
Follow the Duckabush River Trail up the valley, climbing over Little Hump and then the steeper Big Hump at about 4.2 miles before dropping back to the river at Five Mile Camp.
Continue up the Duckabush River Trail, entering Olympic National Park at about 6.2 miles, on a gentle grade along the river to Ten Mile Camp.

Continue up the Duckabush River Trail through the upper valley, which can be brushy with blowdown early in the season, to the signed junction where the La Crosse Pass Trail branches north and immediately begins switchbacking up the valley wall.
wa_mount_lawson_standard: From US 101 at Amanda Park on Lake Quinault, turn east on North Shore Road and follow it about 17 miles, the upper part on gravel, to its end at the North Fork Ranger Station and trailhead. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.
Follow the North Fork Quinault River Trail upstream through lowland rainforest about 2.5 miles to the riverside camps at Wolf Bar.
Continue up-valley on the North Fork Quinault River Trail to Wild Rose Creek at about 4.9 miles, an unbridged ford that can be difficult during snowmelt or after rain.
About a quarter mile past the Wild Rose Creek ford, the trail reaches the sandy riverside camps at Halfway House.
Continue about 1.5 miles up the trail to Elip Creek Camp, near the junction with the Skyline Trail.

Continue up the North Fork Quinault River Trail past Trapper Shelter and the flats around Twelve Mile to the North Fork ford at Sixteen Mile, about 12 miles from the trailhead. The ford can be difficult or impassable at high water; this is where the route leaves the trail.
wa_mount_lincoln_standard: From US 101 at Hoodsport, turn west on SR 119 and drive a little more than 9 miles past Lake Cushman to the T with FR 24. Turn left; the pavement ends after 1.7 miles. Continue 3.7 miles on gravel to a junction, bear right, and drive 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station, with parking across from the campground. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.
wa_mount_mathias_scramble: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on the paved Upper Hoh Road and follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.

Follow the Hoh River Trail up the valley through the rainforest, mostly on a gentle grade, for about 17 miles to Glacier Meadows. The trail climbs steadily only in the last few miles out of the valley, and a washed-out slope near the top is crossed on a fixed ladder.

Take the way trail about 0.8 mile to the top of the Blue Glacier's lateral moraine and follow the crest another 0.2 mile, then descend onto the glacier, rope up, and climb snow around rock islands to Snow Dome at 6,600 ft. Continue roped up the upper Blue Glacier to Glacier Pass, the low saddle between Mathias and the East Peak of Olympus.

From just above the pass, climb the narrow 35 to 40 degree snow finger between the pass and Mathias onto the summit ridge, then scramble the exposed, loose Class 4 ridge to the top, with the Blue Glacier on one side and the Hoh Glacier on the other.
wa_mount_mystery_standard: Follow the Upper Dungeness Trail #833.2 about 1 mile up the valley to the fork just before the Royal Creek footlog bridge.
Bear right onto the Royal Basin Trail #832 and follow it up the Royal Creek valley through mossy forest to the camp beside the creek.
Continue up the Royal Basin Trail along Royal Creek, climbing steadily to Royal Lake at about 5,100 ft, the main basecamp and the last dependable water before the climb to the divide.

Continue up into upper Royal Basin, then leave the trail and climb a moraine and a snowfield of roughly 35-40 degrees to the notch on the Royal-Deception divide at about 6,500 ft. Carry an ice axe; crampons help on the snow.

Descend loose shower-tile scree on the far side to grass and heather benches above Deception Basin, drop into the basin and cross a dark moraine to the jade-green lake at the foot of the Mystery Glacier.
wa_mount_norton_scramble: Follow the Elwha River Trail south up the valley through forest, past the Lillian River, to Mary's Falls Camp beside the river at about 8.8 miles.
Continue up the Elwha River Trail past Canyon Camp to the historic Elkhorn Guard Station and its grassy river-flat camp.
Continue up the Elwha River Trail about 4.5 miles to the Hayes River Guard Station, where the Hayes River joins the Elwha.
wa_mount_noyes_standard: From US 101 near Amanda Park, follow North Shore Road along the north side of Lake Quinault and up the Quinault valley to its end at the North Fork ranger station and campground, about 17 miles from the highway; the last miles are narrow gravel. Overnight stays need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance.

Follow the North Fork Quinault Trail about 16 miles up the valley to camp at Low Divide, about 3,600 ft. From there the peak is an off-trail day: talus and heather and a long sidehill traverse across eroded gullies to the col beside Noyes, then a Class 2-3 scramble along the summit ridge to the top.
wa_mount_olson_standard: From US 101 north of Shelton, turn west on West Skokomish Valley Road, follow it about 5.6 miles and continue uphill onto Forest Road 23. Stay on FS 23, keeping left at intersections, then turn right onto FS 2361 and drive about 5 miles to the road end at about 1,100 ft. FS 2361 is rough and potholed and is closed to vehicles October 1 to April 30.

Follow the Upper South Fork Skokomish Trail #873 up the valley on brushy but obvious tread, crossing Rule Creek on a bridge, to the unbridged ford of the South Fork at about 2.4 miles. It is ankle-deep only in late-summer low water.
Continue up the valley on the far bank to the Olympic National Park boundary near 5.1 miles, where the trail begins to climb steeply and the tread grows fainter.
Climb steeply on faint, broken tread through wet subalpine meadows to the forested saddle of Sundown Pass at about 4,125 ft, marked by a broken signpost.
From the pass, continue about 0.4 mile to Lake Sundown, a designated camp in a subalpine basin.

Climb steeply from the lake to Six Ridge Pass, then follow the primitive Six Ridge Trail east along the sawtooth crest past McGravey Lakes and Belview Camp to about 4,650 ft, the point on the crest nearest Olson, where the unsigned Mount Olson Way leaves the trail.
Follow the faint, overgrown Mount Olson Way on a steep sidehill traverse, crossing a loose notch and dropping into the basin to the boulder-field tarn below the summit block.

Climb to the pass immediately east of the summit, then scramble the steep Class 3 grass and heather slope above it, around 55-60 degrees in places. It eases and curves around the north side of the peak onto a heather bench, then it is an easy walk to the true summit.
wa_mount_olympus_blue_glacier: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

Follow the Hoh River Trail east up the valley past the Olympus Guard Station and Lewis Meadow, cross the High Hoh Bridge over the gorge, and climb past Elk Lake to Glacier Meadows at about 4,300 ft, roughly 17.5 miles. About a quarter mile below the meadows the trail crosses a washout on a ladder of roughly 100 ft with a fixed rope.

Take the climbers' way trail about 0.8 mile up onto the crest of the lateral moraine, follow the narrow, loose crest about 0.2 mile, then drop onto the toe of the Blue Glacier and rope up. Cross the glacier and climb roped to Snow Dome at about 6,600-6,800 ft.

Stay roped and continue over Crystal Pass, scouting the large crevasse there for a usable snow bridge, then traverse south of and below Five Fingers Ridge toward the West Peak, which is hidden from the north. Cross the moat or bergschrund and climb the 80-ft summit tower by loose Class 4 ramps or the 5.4 north face.
wa_mount_olympus_west_ridge: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

Follow the Hoh River Trail about 17.5 miles to Glacier Meadows at about 4,300 ft, crossing the ladder and fixed rope at the washout just below the meadows. Take the way trail onto the lateral moraine crest, drop onto the Blue Glacier and rope up, then climb about 2 miles of glacier to Snow Dome.

Cross the Blue Glacier to the southwest, keeping Crystal Pass, Five Fingers Ridge and the West Peak in view as references, to the moat at the ridge's lowest point near 7,260 ft. If you find yourself climbing toward Crystal Pass, you have drifted onto the standard route.

Cross the moat and climb about 600 ft of ridge in roughly seven pitches, never harder than 5.4, staying high but slightly south of the loose crest and using shallow gullies, to the base of the summit block, then climb the roughly 100-ft block to the top.
wa_mount_pershing_standard: Pick up the faint, flagged path on the north side of the creek where the road fords it and follow the north bank through old growth, boulders and windfall. Fill water here; the route is dry above.

As the brush thickens, the path makes a rising traverse into a rocky gully. Climb the gully, talus and sometimes snow, to a small basin at about 4,300 ft. Fix it in mind: on the way down it is the aiming point before dropping back to the creek.
From the 4,300 ft basin continue straight up, then cut left up a second gully into the basin east of the summit at about 5,400 ft, the base of the climb proper.

Two gullies leave the upper basin for the south ridge. Take the left-hand one up 45 to 50 degree snow to a short, loose and brushy Class 4 rock step; reaching that step confirms you are in the right gully.
Climb the step to gain the summit ridge and follow the crest, mostly Class 2 to 3, to where it narrows into a knife edge.
Cross the knife edge, with one or two exposed Class 3 to 4 moves, to the south summit, the highest of Pershing's three tops.
wa_mount_pulitzer_standard: From Port Angeles, drive about 29 miles west on US 101 and turn left onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road. Follow it about 14 miles, past the resort, to the trailhead at road's end. A national park entrance pass is required, and an overnight wilderness permit for the traverse.

Follow the Sol Duc River Trail to Heart Lake and the High Divide, then leave maintained trail at the Catwalk below Mount Carrie for the cross-country Bailey Range: sidehill below Carrie and Ruth, drop to Cream Lake and climb into Upper Ferry Basin to camp. From camp, go up to the Ferry-Pulitzer col and scramble the loose Class 3 east ridge to the summit. Plan on two to three days.
wa_mount_queets_south: From Port Angeles, drive about 8 miles west on US 101 and turn left onto Olympic Hot Springs Road just past the Elwha River bridge. Follow it about 2 miles to the Madison Falls parking area at the park boundary, where the road is closed to vehicles. An overnight wilderness permit is required.
Walk or bike the closed Olympic Hot Springs Road past the washout, then follow Whiskey Bend Road up to the old Whiskey Bend trailhead, about 6 to 7 miles in all. Bikes are allowed on both roads.

Follow the Elwha River Trail south up the valley past Lillian River, Elkhorn and Hayes River to Chicago Camp, about 25 miles, where the trail fords the Elwha; the ford can be hazardous in high water. Leave the trail there and continue about 3 miles cross-country up the brushy upper valley into Elwha Basin, fording the river repeatedly.

Climb cross-country out of the head of Elwha Basin to Dodwell-Rixon Pass at about 4,750 ft, the divide between the Elwha and Queets drainages, with a small tarn just below it. Do not count on the old snow ramp near the pass.

Leave the pass up the ridge toward Queets, Class 2 on crumbly rock, steep heather and some brush. About a third of the way along, where the crest ahead becomes impassable, drop a couple of hundred feet off the east side onto steep, firm scree and traverse at about 5,300 ft.

Hold the scree traverse until you have passed below the steep cliff about halfway along the east side, then climb talus, heather and crumbly slabs back to the crest. Scramble easy Class 2 around the west side of the ridge, then take the moderately steep snow slope on the east side to the summit; carry an axe.
wa_mount_seattle_south: From US 101 at the west end of Lake Quinault, near Amanda Park, turn east onto North Shore Road and follow it about 17 miles to its end at the North Fork Quinault trailhead and ranger station. A national park entrance pass is required, plus a wilderness permit for overnight stays.

Follow the North Fork Quinault River Trail up the valley past Wolf Bar and Halfway House, fording Wild Rose and Elip creeks, to the ford of the North Fork at Sixteen Mile Camp, about 12 miles in; it is hazardous or impassable in heavy rain or snowmelt. Beyond it the trail climbs steeply to Low Divide at about 3,600 ft, 16 miles from the trailhead.
wa_mount_skokomish_standard: From Hoodsport, drive about 14 miles north on US 101 and turn left at milepost 318 onto Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25). Follow it about 12 miles, paved for the first 7.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead and gravel beyond, to the Putvin Trailhead pullout on the right at about 1,600 ft. No parking pass is required; camping at the lake needs a national park wilderness permit.

Follow the Putvin Trail (#813) along Boulder Creek, then switchback up across several drainages into the open Whitehorse Creek basin. Above it a steep root-and-rock headwall takes hand-and-foot scrambling; the trail then passes a small pond and reaches Lake of the Angels, about 3.5 miles and 3,400 ft from the trailhead.

Go around the right-hand side of the lake and climb west up heather slopes and a broad gully to the 5,800 ft saddle just north of Point 5945. From the saddle follow the boot path contouring south and southwest around the east and south flanks; above the large tarn, turn up the loose scree and rotten rock, through the hanging traverse, to the broad true (south) summit.
wa_mount_steel_first_divide: From US 101 at Hoodsport, take SR 119 about 9 miles to its end at FR 24 and turn left. Pavement ends after 1.7 miles; continue on gravel 3.7 miles to a junction, turn right, and drive 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station trailhead parking. A national park entrance pass is required.
wa_mount_steel_standard: From US 101 about 15 miles south of Quilcene, turn west at the Duckabush Recreation Area sign onto Duckabush Road. Pavement ends at about 3.6 miles; just past the horse parking area at about 6 miles, bear right and uphill onto FS Road 2510-060 to the trailhead in 0.1 mile. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and an Olympic National Park wilderness permit for any night inside the park.
wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels: Follow the Putvin Trail #813 up the west side of Boulder Creek, then switchback steeply to the old Boulder Creek road; turn left and walk downhill about 200 yards to where the trail resumes. Keep climbing steeply to a meadow, scramble the root-and-rock headwall, and continue past the Pond of the False Prophet, which is not the lake, to Lake of the Angels in its cirque below Mount Stone.

From the lake, climb toward St. Peter's Gate, the obvious notch above the basin. Short of the Gate, turn left and traverse along the base of the cliffs to a notch in the west ridge, turn right and climb a short low Class 3 chimney to a sub-summit, cross a brief exposed ridge to the summit spire, and follow the groove on its left side, which bends right, to the top.
wa_mount_townsend_standard: From US 101 about 0.9 mile south of the Quilcene Ranger Station, bear right onto Penny Creek Road. In about 1.5 miles take the left fork onto Forest Road 27 and follow it about 10 miles to a junction; turn right for the upper trailhead, a small gravel lot at about 3,300 ft. No parking pass is required.

Start up Trail #839 at the Buckhorn Wilderness sign and climb the first switchbacks through old-growth forest with a thick rhododendron understory, alongside Townsend Creek, to the small creek crossing about half a mile up. It can be dry by late summer.

Continue on #839 through forest and a second set of switchbacks, then a steep, sun-exposed third set that breaks onto a ridge crest and open meadow. At about 5,300 ft an unmarked spur leads off to Camp Windy and Windy Lake, the last water.
Back on the main trail, climb a short way above Camp Windy to the signed junction with the Silver Lakes Trail #842 at about 5,500 ft.

Stay right and uphill on #839, leaving the Silver Lakes Trail to the left. The forest opens into subalpine meadow and the trail climbs to the open slope below the south summit ridge, which can hold snow into early summer.
Climb the open slope onto the broad summit ridge and follow it north over grassy, rocky ground to the south summit, the true high point.
wa_mount_washington_olympic_standard: From the road-end parking, follow the boot path into the forest. Within a few hundred yards it steepens into narrow rock gullies laced with tree roots, climbed hand over hand in places.
Climb the rooty gullies directly up through the timber until the grade eases at an open meadow bench around 3,800 ft, where the ridgeline and Mount Ellinor come into view.
Above the meadow, climb onto the broad scree and talus slopes and keep to the climber's-left side of the large, loose rocky gully. Spread the party out so nobody knocks rock onto those below.
Continue up the climber's-left side of the gully to about 5,600 ft, where the path swings west onto a ramp along the base of the headwall.

Follow the ramp briefly along the headwall, duck back through the trees, and wind above the gully onto the southern ridgeline at the saddle, about 5,950 ft, the first spot where the true summit comes into view.
From the saddle, follow the faint goat trail along the ridge crest toward the summit to the Catwalk, where the tread narrows to a boot-width with exposure on both sides. Move one at a time.

Past the Catwalk, continue along the ridge to the scree field below the false summit, take the goat trail up its climber's-right edge to a stone wind shelter on the ridge, then scramble the final short Class 3-4 step to the true summit.
wa_mount_tom_scramble: From Forks, drive south on US 101 about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, where the Hoh River Trail begins. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight wilderness permits must be reserved in advance.
wa_mount_wilder_scramble: From Port Angeles, drive west on US 101 and turn left onto Olympic Hot Springs Road, following it into the Elwha Valley to the Madison Falls parking area. The road is closed to vehicles beyond a washout here, so walk or bike roughly 7 miles up Olympic Hot Springs Road and then the Whiskey Bend Road to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead, where the Elwha River Trail begins.
wa_mount_worthington_standard: From US 101 across from Sequim Bay State Park, turn west onto Louella Road and go about 0.9 mi, then turn left onto Palo Alto Road. Follow it about 6 mi as it becomes FS Road 28, turn right onto FS Road 2880 (steep, not suited to trailers), pass Dungeness Forks Campground, and stay left onto FS Road 2870 for about 12.5 mi to the Tubal Cain Trailhead at about 3,300 ft. A recreation pass such as the Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
Start up the Tubal Cain Trail #840, passing the Silver Creek shelter, and cross Silver Creek on a footlog early in the forested lower section.

Climb gently on well-graded trail through forest and rhododendrons high above Copper Creek. At about 3 mi the Tull Canyon Trail #847 doubles back sharply to the left toward the B-17 crash site, and old mine adits show on the hillside; stay on #840 for the Tubal Cain Mine tailings just beyond.

Continue on #840 past the mine, cross Copper Creek on a log bridge, the last easy water, and switchback up through subalpine meadows toward Buckhorn Pass. Near 5,200 ft, about 5.7 mi from the trailhead, watch for the lightly signed spur to Buckhorn Lake; it is easy to walk past while the main trail carries on toward Marmot Pass.

Take the spur down to Buckhorn Lake. From the south end of the lake the tread stops: cross the inlet stream where a small waterfall comes in, then follow a faint boot path southwest through avalanche-flattened timber and blowdown to the broad, flat debris bench about 200 ft above the lake.

From the bench climb the wide talus and scree gully, trending south and then curving east, breaking treeline near 5,800 ft onto loose rock and light Class 2-3. Angle east and southeast up increasingly loose slopes to the col between Iron Mountain and Worthington at about 6,420 ft. Cairns are sparse, so read the terrain.

From the col, angle northeast up open slopes toward the base of Worthington's summit fin, where the ground steepens into a band of rotten, loose rock. Test every hold and keep the party out of each other's fall line.

For the final Class 3 scramble, step a few feet left of the ridge crest to a short crack about 10 ft high, climb it, then follow the top of the fin to the true summit. Some parties rope up for the exposed summit block.
wa_olympus_blue_glacier_east_ramps: From Forks, drive south on US 101 about 13 miles and turn east onto the Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, where the Hoh River Trail begins. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need a wilderness camping permit.
Follow the Hoh River Trail east up the valley through flat old-growth rain forest, passing Five Mile Island, to the Olympus Guard Station near mile 9.

From Snow Dome go up and over Crystal Pass, minding the large crevasse near it, then traverse below the south side of Five Fingers Ridge and over the false summit. Drop into the sharp saddle and climb the short steep snow slope to the flat platform at the foot of the 80 ft summit tower. Turn right around the corner onto the east face and climb the loose ramps angling across it to the final Class 4/5.4 step to the top.
wa_olympus_summit_block_west_edge: From Forks, drive south on US 101 about 13 miles and turn east onto the Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, where the Hoh River Trail begins. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need a wilderness camping permit.

Follow the Hoh River Trail east about 17.4 miles past Five Mile Island, the Olympus Guard Station, Lewis Meadow, the High Hoh Bridge and Elk Lake, then climb to Glacier Meadows. A washed-out cliffside stretch about a quarter mile below camp is crossed on a fixed ladder; check the rungs before trusting them.

Climb the way path onto the Blue Glacier's lateral moraine, drop onto the ice and rope up, then thread the rock islands to Snow Dome. Cross Crystal Pass, traverse below Five Fingers Ridge, go over the false summit and up the short snow slope to the flat platform at the foot of the 80 ft summit tower. Traverse anticlockwise around the base of the block to the northwest edge and climb it, with several 5.3-5.4 moves, to the top.
wa_olympus_traverse: From Forks, drive south on US 101 about 13 miles and turn east onto the Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to its end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, where the Hoh River Trail begins. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need a wilderness camping permit.

Follow the Hoh River Trail about 17.4 miles to Glacier Meadows, then take the way path onto the moraine and drop onto the Blue Glacier. Rope up and climb through the rock islands to Snow Dome, cross Crystal Pass, traverse below Five Fingers Ridge and over the false summit, then climb the short snow slope to the platform below the 80 ft summit tower and climb the tower to the West Peak.
wa_ruth_peak_olympics_scramble: From Port Angeles, drive west on US 101 about 28 miles, past Lake Crescent, and turn left onto the signed Sol Duc Hot Springs Road. Follow it about 14 miles, past the hot springs resort and campground, to the trailhead at the road's end. An Olympic National Park entrance pass is required, and overnight permits must be arranged in advance.
wa_se_ridge_aka_shield_wall: From US 101 in Hoodsport, take SR-119 (North Lake Cushman Road) about 9.4 miles to the T intersection, turn right on Forest Road 24, and in about 1.5 miles turn left on Forest Road 2419. Follow it up the Big Creek drainage about 6.6 miles, past the Mount Ellinor trailheads, to the road end at roughly 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

Walk the old roadbed past the standard route's trail entrance about 1,000 ft to just beyond the Big Creek crossing, then take the climbers' trail up a rock rib.
