At the base of the ridge's big rock section (about 3,700 ft) bear right around the rocks, follow the ridgeline until gendarmes force you right, then climb a gully up and left to the notch at the wall's left corner (about 4,850 ft). Climb the Shield Wall and the ridge above to the summit.
wa_the_brothers_traverse: From Hoodsport, drive north on US 101 about 14 miles and turn left onto Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25) at milepost 318. Follow it about 7.5 paved miles to the Lena Lake Trailhead, where parking lines the road. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.
wa_the_incisor_scramble: Follow the Upper Dungeness Trail #833 upstream about 1 mile; a few steps before the footlog over Royal Creek, bear right onto Royal Basin Trail #832.
About 0.2 mile up Trail #832, stay left at the Maynard Burn Trail junction. The trail enters Olympic National Park shortly beyond.
Continue up the Royal Creek valley through forest, crossing the creek several times, until the trail breaks out into open, talus-strewn stretches with small stream crossings.
Past the talus the trail returns to the creek near some campsites, then climbs open slopes in long traverses and steep switchbacks to Royal Lake at about 5,100 ft, 7.2 miles from the trailhead.

Continue past the lake and the big overhang of Shelter Rock, cross a short footlog and climb to Arrowhead Meadow, then cross an unbridged stream and climb into Upper Royal Basin at about 5,700 ft, under a mile beyond the lake.
Leave the trail and pick a line west up loose talus and steep heather benches (Class 2-3) toward the Needles ridge crest.
From the crest, finish with exposed Class 3-4 scrambling along the ridge to the summit spire of The Incisor.
wa_warrior_peak_standard: Follow the Upper Dungeness Trail #833.2 upstream along the Dungeness River, staying left at the Royal Basin Trail junction, about 3.4 miles and 600 ft of gain to Camp Handy.
Just past Camp Handy take the uphill fork and climb steeply, with two creek crossings, about 3 miles and 1,850 ft to Boulder Shelter.

From Boulder Shelter take the Constance Pass trail south rather than the trail toward Marmot Pass, cross into Olympic National Park, and continue past several creek crossings to Home Lake below Constance Pass.
Leave the trail at Home Lake and climb east into the Warrior/Inner Constance cirque over meadow and talus to about 5,800 ft, where the headwall closes around the basin.

From the cirque head north into the obvious couloir that runs up between the twin summits, and climb it to the saddle at about 7,000 ft: snow early in the season, loose scree once it melts out. Watch for rockfall in the gully.

At the saddle turn right toward the higher southeast summit and cross to the foot of the summit block, where 20 to 50 ft of exposed, poor rock on its northwest side is the crux, often reached over steep snow or a moat.
Climb the Class 4 to low 5th rock step, roped or on a fixed hand line if needed, and scramble the last short distance to the southeast summit.
wa_washington_ellinor_traverse_ridge: Climb the steep boot path through forest to the meadow benches, then scree and talus on climber's left of the large loose gully to the southern ridgeline and across the exposed Dog Walk ledge. Take the goat trail up the right edge of the scree field below the false summit to the stone wind shelter, then a short Class 3-4 scramble to the summit.

Follow the narrow crest southwest: first the Wedge, about 150 ft of low 5th on good holds, then sustained Class 4 past a series of gendarmes using hidden ledges below the obvious line, and a loose 50 ft downclimb. Where the crest gets too hard, drop into the basin and downclimb or bypass on a snow finger to rejoin Mount Ellinor's winter route to its summit.
Descend Mount Ellinor's standard trail through the subalpine slopes and forest to the upper trailhead at about 3,500 ft, where the shuttle car should be waiting.
wa_white_mountain_olympics_scramble: From US-101 at Brinnon, turn west onto the Dosewallips Road and drive about 8.5 miles to where it ends at the washout, and park along the road.

Walk or bike the closed Dosewallips Road past the big washout to the old Dosewallips Ranger Station, then continue on foot on the Dosewallips River Trail to Dose Forks, where the West Fork trail splits off at the river confluence.
At Dose Forks take the West Fork Dosewallips Trail toward Anderson Pass, crossing the West Fork on the high bridge, and follow it up the forested valley about 5 miles to Diamond Meadows camp.
Continue up the West Fork Dosewallips Trail about 1.5 miles to Honeymoon Meadows camp, just below the meadows themselves.
Climb the trail past the meadows about 950 ft to Anderson Pass, the wooded saddle on the Dosewallips-Quinault divide. Fill water before the pass; there is little to none above it.

Ignore the spur that climbs north toward the Anderson Glacier. Step off the trail on the south side of the saddle and climb south, with no path, through open subalpine forest and heather benches to treeline around 5,800 ft.

Continue south up steep heather and loose talus, with hard snow patches in the hollows into midsummer, to the summit. Note landmarks or track the line, since the open slopes all look alike on the way down.
adams_northwest_ridge: From Randle take SR 131 south and stay left on FS Road 23 for about 31 miles, then turn left on FS Road 2329 toward Takhlakh Lake and drive about 6 miles to the Killen Creek Trailhead (from Trout Lake, follow FS Road 23 north about 23 miles to the same turn). Self-issue the free wilderness permit at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams Climbing Pass is required above 7,000 ft in summer.

Hike Killen Creek Trail #113 to the Pacific Crest Trail, then High Camp Trail #10 to the meadow camp at about 6,900 ft. Climb the north-facing slope between the Adams Glacier on your left and the Northwest Ridge crest on your right, entering below the glacier's terminus, up 40-45 degree neve through one narrow rock-band pinch to the crest near 10,000 ft, and on to the summit.
wa_castle_peak_tatoosh_la_villa: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The Pinnacle Peak Trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; Stevens Canyon Road is closed by snow from fall to late spring.

Take the Pinnacle Peak Trail 1.3 miles and about 1,050 ft to Pinnacle Saddle, then leave the trail and contour east across Pinnacle's south-face scree to the base of The Castle's southeast side. Scramble exposed third-class broken ground to the foot of the summit block and climb the dihedral on the taller spire (5.7, 5.8 crux) to a ledge about 10 ft left of the true summit, then step right to the top.
wa_castle_peak_tatoosh_southeast_face: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; when Stevens Canyon Road is snowed in, start from the Narada Falls lot.

Take the Pinnacle Peak Trail 1.3 miles and about 1,050 ft to Pinnacle Saddle. Leave the trail and contour east across Pinnacle's south-face scree at 6,000-6,200 ft, about half a mile, to the Pinnacle-Castle col. Scramble onto the south rib, traverse class 3 onto the east flank, climb the crack-chimney to a notch beside a rock horn, then scramble the exposed crest north to the true summit.
wa_classic_route_2: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance toward Paradise, turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road and drive about 3 miles, 1.5 miles past Reflection Lakes, to the Bench and Snow Lakes trailhead on the south side of the road. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west from SR 123. A park entrance pass is required; Stevens Canyon Road is closed by snow from fall to late spring.

Follow the Snow Lake Trail past Bench Lake to Snow Lake, the last water. From the lake, climb the steep talus and dirt gully southwest of it into the basin below the peak and continue up the bowl, beside the snow patch, to Unicorn Col on the west side of the peak. Traverse east around the south side of the summit block to the base of the horn and climb the middle line, a 40-50 ft blocky 5.4 pitch, to the top.
wa_east_ridge_8: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The Pinnacle Peak Trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; in winter start from the Narada Falls lot.

Take the Pinnacle Peak Trail 1.3 miles and about 1,050 ft to Pinnacle Saddle, then follow the unmaintained boot path east behind Pinnacle to the Castle-Pinnacle col. The east ridge rises directly from the col: scramble mostly class 4 to a ledge at a large dead tree, climb the blocky 5.5 traverse pitch to a sandy bench, then easy ground to the summit.
wa_fantasy_falls: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance toward Paradise, turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road and drive about 3 miles, 1.5 miles past Reflection Lakes, to the Bench and Snow Lakes trailhead on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required. In winter Stevens Canyon Road is gated: park near Narada Falls and ski or snowshoe about 3 miles of unplowed road to the trailhead.
wa_frying_pan_whitman_glaciers: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east about 43 miles and turn west onto the White River (Sunrise) Road. Pass the White River Entrance and drive about 3 miles to the parking area at the Fryingpan Creek bridge; the trail to Summerland starts across the road. A park entrance pass is required, and the road is open only in the summer season.

Follow the Wonderland Trail up Fryingpan Creek about 4.5 miles to Summerland. Take the climbers' path northwest of the campground knoll up the Meany Snowfield to Meany Crest at about 7,400 ft, staying left of the cliffed bowl. Rope up on the Fryingpan Glacier and climb south-southwest to Whitman Notch (about 9,100 ft), then up the Whitman Glacier across the bergschrund to a loose gully, a chimney to the summit notch, and the exposed class 3 crest.
wa_gilbert_peak_meade_glacier: From Naches, follow US 12 west about 22 miles and turn left onto Tieton Road (FR 1200). In 4.5 miles turn left onto South Fork Tieton Road (FR 1000) and follow it 12.6 miles to the trailhead at road's end in Conrad Meadows, about 4,050 ft; the last 7 miles are gravel. A day-use fee or annual recreation pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Goat Rocks Wilderness permit.

Hike Trail #1120 through Conrad Meadows, crossing Conrad Creek, to the Surprise Lake loop and take its right fork to the trail's high point. Leave the trail west into a basin, cross it left of the large mounds and drop briefly to the foot of the Meade Glacier. Climb the Meade right of the rock band and the snow dome to the ridge, then take the goat path on the southwest side to a small saddle and scramble west to the summit.
wa_gilbert_peak_west_route: Join Snowgrass Trail #96 and follow it about 4 miles to cutoff Trail #97, which meets the PCT in half a mile; follow the PCT southbound about 2 miles to Cispus Basin. Climb to the saddle at the basin's northeast end, go up an entry gully to the white band and traverse it at about 7,500 ft to the notch behind the black prow, then take the goat path east across two gullies to the saddle south of Goat Citadel and up the ridge to the summit.
wa_ives_peak_r1: From Packwood, drive US 12 west about 2.7 miles and turn left onto Forest Road 21. Follow it about 13 miles of gravel, bear left onto FR 2150, and in under 3 miles turn right on spur 405 to the Snowgrass Trailhead loop lot at about 4,650 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issued wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

Follow Snowgrass Trail #96, staying right where the connector to Berry Patch Trailhead leaves at 0.1 mile, through open forest for just under 2 miles; the trail dips slightly to a sturdy bridge over Goat Creek.

Continue through a cedar swamp, then climb about 1,100 ft over the next 2 miles, ignoring the bypass trail that leaves on the right at about 3.5 miles, to the Lily Basin Trail #86 junction at the lower edge of Snowgrass Flat.
Stay on Trail #96 up through Snowgrass Flat, climbing about 400 ft in under a mile, to its junction with the Pacific Crest Trail.

Turn north on the PCT and follow it to about 6,700 ft, then leave the trail and head northeast up loose talus and scree, with no tread and only occasional cairns, to the low col between Old Snowy Mountain and Ives Peak at about 7,250 ft. Snow commonly lingers on these slopes and in the col into July.

Follow the ridge crest, or a line just south of it, over a rounded intermediate bump to the base of the summit block. Take the boot path up scree to the notch between two rock outcrops, then downclimb slightly below the short cliff band and traverse the narrow, exposed ledge onto the loose ramp of the south face.
Scramble about 40 ft to climber's right on loose, blocky rock, then up easy ground to the summit.
wa_lane_peak_r1: From the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive about 15 miles past Longmire toward Paradise and bear right onto Stevens Canyon Road. The Reflection Lakes parking is about 1.5 miles on, with the trailhead across the road. A park entrance pass is required. Stevens Canyon Road is closed roughly November to May; then park at Narada Falls and climb about 200 ft through the timber to regain the road.
wa_lane_peak_r2: From the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive about 15 miles past Longmire toward Paradise and bear right onto Stevens Canyon Road. The Reflection Lakes parking is about 1.5 miles on, with the trailhead across the road. A park entrance pass is required. Stevens Canyon Road is closed roughly November to May; then park at Narada Falls and climb about 200 ft through the timber to regain the road.
wa_lane_peak_r3: From the Nisqually Entrance on SR 706, drive the road east past Longmire toward Paradise to the Narada Falls parking area, about a mile below Paradise. The lot is plowed through winter; the road above Longmire is gated overnight in winter and vehicles must carry tire chains. National park entrance fee applies.

Ski or snowshoe along the snow-covered Reflection Lakes road, then traverse the steep hillsides under Denman Peak and turn sharply uphill at the first steep avalanche funnel, the leftmost of Lane's three north couloirs. Climb it to the ridge above the Zipper, rappel more than 100 ft from the tree into the upper Zipper, climb its last few hundred feet, then curl onto the south side and traverse left to the summit.
wa_liberty_cap_ptarmigan_ridge_finish: Mowich Lake has had no public road access since the SR 165 Fairfax Bridge south of Carbonado closed permanently in April 2025; the lake is reached only on foot via the Wonderland Trail from another part of the park, with a wilderness permit. The road in ran from Buckley on SR 165 through Wilkeson and Carbonado, then up the gravel Mowich Lake Road to its end at the lake.

Take the trail 3 to 4 miles up into Spray Park and leave it near 6,400 ft on a beaten path toward the snow. Cross the Flett Glacier between Echo and Observation Rocks, climb to the saddle just east of Observation Rock, then follow the Ptarmigan Ridge crest south to high camp near 10,300 ft. From camp drop west onto the Mowich Glacier, cross the bergschrund near 9,800 ft, and climb the face through the rock band to the Liberty Cap Glacier and Liberty Cap.
Cross the broad, gentle saddle southeast of Liberty Cap and climb the low-angle summit dome to the crater rim.

Descend the Emmons-Winthrop route northeast off the summit dome, keeping to the Emmons track rather than the busier Disappointment Cleaver track on the south side, and follow it down the glacier corridor to Camp Schurman beside Steamboat Prow at about 9,400 ft.
wa_little_tahoma_cowlitz_ingraham_glacie: From the Nisqually Entrance on SR 706, drive east past Longmire and up to Paradise, about 19 miles, and park in the upper lot by the visitor center. National park entrance fee applies, and climbing registration is required for glacier travel. The road above Longmire is gated overnight in winter and vehicles must carry tire chains.

Climb the Camp Muir route from Paradise to about 8,600 ft, below Anvil Rock, then rope up and traverse east across the Paradise and Cowlitz glaciers, holding elevation above the cliff and serac band, through the notch in the Cathedral Rocks cleaver, and across the Ingraham to the ramp at the base of the face near 8,900 ft. Above, climb a loose gully, a short step and a gully-chimney to the summit notch, then scramble the exposed crest to the summit.
wa_little_tahoma_east_shoulder: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River Entrance, then follow White River Road about 3 miles to the parking area by the Fryingpan Creek bridge; the trail starts across the road. The road is open summer only.
wa_mount_adams_lava_glacier_headwall: From Randle on US 12, take Forest Road 23 south about 32 miles, the last stretch gravel, to FR 2329, then turn east past Takhlakh Lake about 6 miles to the trailhead. From Trout Lake, take Mt Adams Road and FR 23 north about 24 miles to the same junction. Roads are seasonal. A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams climbing pass is needed above 7,000 ft May through September.

Follow Killen Creek Trail #113 about 3.1 miles, crossing East Fork Adams Creek near mile 2.5, to the PCT at about 6,100 ft, then continue straight across on High Camp Trail #10 a mile to High Camp. Traverse east off-trail across the lava fields, past the North Ridge, to the Lava Glacier, and climb it to the triangular headwall between the North Ridge and Lava Ridge. Climb the headwall's 45-degree snow and ice to the summit.
wa_mount_adams_lyman_glacier: From Randle on US 12, take Forest Road 23 south about 32 miles, the last stretch gravel, to FR 2329, then turn east past Takhlakh Lake about 6 miles to the trailhead. From Trout Lake, take Mt Adams Road and FR 23 north about 24 miles to the same junction. Roads are seasonal. A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams climbing pass is needed above 7,000 ft May through September.

Follow Killen Creek Trail #113 about 3.1 miles to the PCT at about 6,100 ft and continue straight across on High Camp Trail #10 a mile to High Camp. Traverse east and southeast off-trail across the lava fields, the toe of the Lava Glacier, and around or over the toe of Lava Ridge to the base of the Lyman Glacier near 8,000 ft. Climb either lobe of the glacier to the crux chute near 10,000 ft, then easier snow to the summit plateau and summit.
wa_mount_adams_mazama_glacier_headwall: From the parking area the trail is easy to follow to about 6,700 ft. Above that there is no single path: pick a line up through moraine, scree and glacier remnants to Sunrise Camp, a flat with hand-built rock wind shelters wedged between the toe of the Mazama Glacier and a small rock hill. Carry a map, since finding the camp is the part people get wrong.

Rope up and go straight up the Mazama Glacier from camp, weaving around the crevasses on its lower half. It steepens to about 40 degrees, with a bergschrund near 9,500 ft, and narrows as it climbs; around 11,300 ft veer right onto the 45-degree headwall.

Climb the headwall toward Piker's Peak, the false south summit, exiting left onto easy 25-30 degree snow or right up about 40 ft of 60-70 degree snow and ice on the southeast corner. From Piker's Peak descend its back side to the saddle, then climb the last 600-700 ft of the summit cone to the high point on the east side of the plateau.
wa_mount_adams_north_ridge: From Randle, drive south 1 mile on FR 25, bear left onto FR 23 and follow it about 32 miles to FR 2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Turn onto FR 2329 and continue about 4.5 miles past Takhlakh Lake to the Killen Creek trailhead; from Trout Lake, FR 23 reaches the same FR 2329 junction in about 24 miles. FR 2329 is gravel and holds snow into early summer. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued wilderness permit are required.

Follow Killen Creek Trail #113 through forest, meadow and huckleberry fields, crossing East Fork Adams Creek (the last dependable water) about 2.5 miles up, to the PCT junction at roughly 6,100 ft. Cross straight over onto High Camp Trail #10 and follow it about another mile to its end on the edge of the Adams Glacier moraine, where camps are spread between 7,000 and 7,600 ft.
wa_mount_adams_northwest_ridge: From Randle, drive south 1 mile on FR 25, bear left onto FR 23 and follow it about 32 miles to FR 2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Turn onto FR 2329 and continue about 4.5 miles past Takhlakh Lake to the Killen Creek trailhead; from Trout Lake, FR 23 reaches the same FR 2329 junction in about 24 miles. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued wilderness permit are required.
wa_mount_adams_south_climb: From Trout Lake, drive north on Mt Adams Road to the FR 23 junction and bear right about a mile to the signed FR 80 turn for South Climb. Follow FR 80 for 3.7 miles to FR 8040, then FR 8040 for 8.1 miles to its end at the South Climb / Cold Springs trailhead; it is steep and narrow with sharp switchbacks, so no RVs or trailers. Self-issue a free wilderness permit at the trailhead, and buy the Cascade Volcano Pass online beforehand to go above 7,000 ft.

Follow South Climb Trail #183 up an old roadbed through the burn, across the Round the Mountain Trail and the PCT, and up Crescent Ridge beside the Crescent Glacier to the Lunch Counter, a rocky bench at about 9,250-9,400 ft. Climb the south-facing snowfield of the South Spur about 2,400 ft to Piker's Peak, the false summit, then drop to the saddle and climb the last 600 ft or so of the summit cone to the old lookout on top.
wa_mount_adams_wilson_glacier_headwall: From Trout Lake, drive north on Mt Adams Road to the FR 23 junction and bear right about a mile to the signed FR 80 turn for South Climb. Follow FR 80 for 3.7 miles to FR 8040, then FR 8040 for 8.1 miles to its end at the South Climb / Cold Springs trailhead; it is steep and narrow with sharp switchbacks, so no RVs or trailers. Self-issue a free wilderness permit at the trailhead, and buy the Cascade Volcano Pass online beforehand to go above 7,000 ft.
wa_mount_rainier_curtis_ridge: From Enumclaw, drive WA-410 east about 43 miles to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park and turn right onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Road, following it to its end at White River Campground; the Glacier Basin trailhead is at the upper end of the campground loop. A park entrance pass is required, and the road opens only in summer.
wa_mount_rainier_edmunds_headwall: Mowich Lake is reached from SR 165 south of Wilkeson and Carbonado: cross the Carbon River on the Fairfax Bridge, keep right at the fork onto the gravel Mowich Lake Road and drive to the road end at about 4,900 ft. The Fairfax Bridge has been closed to all traffic since April 2025 with no public detour, so there is currently no public drive to this trailhead.

From Mowich Lake take the Spray Park Trail through Spray Park, then go cross-country up lower Ptarmigan Ridge to the bivy near 9,600 ft between the North Mowich and Edmunds glaciers. Cross the Edmunds Glacier to the headwall near 9,900 ft, pass the bergschrund on the left by the twin gendarmes, climb the headwall to about 13,400 ft, then join the bench atop Sunset Ridge and walk up to Liberty Cap.
wa_mount_rainier_emmons_glacier: From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River Entrance. Turn right on the Sunrise road, take the signed White River Campground turnoff, cross the White River and follow the campground road to its end at about 4,300 ft. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot; the trail starts in Loop D. The road is open only in summer, typically June to October, and a park entrance pass is required.

Take the Glacier Basin Trail up the north side of the Inter Fork of the White River on an old mining road grade. At about 0.9 mile stay right where the Emmons Moraine Trail branches left across the river, and continue past creek crossings and slide paths to Glacier Basin Campground at the end of the maintained trail, about 3.5 miles.

Follow the climbers' path about a mile up the lateral moraine to the toe of the Inter Glacier near 7,000 ft, rope up and climb between the two nunataks, trending left to Camp Curtis on the rocky ridge near 8,700 ft. From there traverse down and right onto the Emmons Glacier and around the south side of Steamboat Prow, about half a mile, to the ranger hut at Camp Schurman.
wa_mount_rainier_fuhrer_finger: From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

Take the Skyline Trail about a mile to Glacier Vista, drop west off the moraine and cross the Nisqually Glacier roped, then climb the boulder gully on the far side and Wapowety Cleaver to camp near 9,000 to 9,500 ft. Cross the Wilson Glacier to the wide couloir with the hourglass, climb it, bear left onto the upper Nisqually above 11,000 ft to the saddle between Point Success and the crater rim, then go up onto the rim to Columbia Crest.
wa_mount_rainier_fuhrer_thumb: From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

Take the Skyline Trail to Glacier Vista, descend the moraine west onto the Nisqually Glacier and cross it roped, then climb the Wilson Gully onto the Wilson Glacier to camp near 9,000 to 9,500 ft. Cross the Wilson to the narrow couloir just west of the Fuhrer Finger and climb it to where it merges with the Finger near 11,500 ft. Follow the east edge of Wapowety Cleaver to its top near 13,000 ft, then go on to the crater rim and around to Columbia Crest.
wa_mount_rainier_gibraltar_ledges: From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

Take the Skyline Trail past Panorama Point to Pebble Creek near 7,200 ft, the last running water, then climb north up the unmarked Muir Snowfield above McClure Rock to Camp Muir, about 4.5 miles in all. In poor visibility hold 355 degrees true from Pebble Creek toward Moon Rocks; crevassed glaciers lie on both sides and a corniced cliff band sits between McClure and Anvil rocks.

Leave camp northwest onto the Cowlitz Cleaver, not east toward Cathedral Gap, and climb past the Beehive and through a notch to the base of Gibraltar Rock near 11,800 ft. Traverse the ledges west along its foot, with one exposed downclimb and gully to regain them, into the Gibraltar Chute and up to Camp Comfort near 12,600 ft. Rope up across the upper Ingraham to the crater rim and cross the crater to Columbia Crest.
wa_mount_rainier_ingraham_direct: Take the Skyline Trail past Panorama Point to Pebble Creek near 7,200 ft, the last running water, then climb north up the unmarked Muir Snowfield above McClure Rock to Camp Muir, about 4.5 miles in all. In poor visibility hold 355 degrees true from Pebble Creek toward Moon Rocks; crevassed glaciers lie on both sides and a corniced cliff band sits between McClure and Anvil rocks.

Rope up and cross the upper Cowlitz Glacier east to Cathedral Gap, climb through its rock band and round onto the Ingraham Glacier to Ingraham Flats near 11,100 ft. Leave the Disappointment Cleaver rib on your left and stay on snow, weaving through the crevasses and up the headwall under the icefall to rejoin the standard line near 12,300 ft, then switchback up to the crater rim and cross the crater to Columbia Crest.
wa_mount_rainier_kautz_glacier: From SR 706 at Ashford, drive east through the park's Nisqually Entrance and follow the Paradise Road past Longmire about 18 miles to Paradise. Climbers park in the upper Paradise lot by the visitor center at about 5,400 ft. A park entrance pass is required, plus the climbing registration and a wilderness permit for the high camps.
wa_mount_rainier_kautz_headwall: From SR 706 at Ashford, drive east through the park's Nisqually Entrance and follow the Paradise Road past Longmire about 18 miles to Paradise. Climbers park in the upper Paradise lot by the visitor center at about 5,400 ft. A park entrance pass is required, plus the climbing registration and a wilderness permit for the high camps.

Take the Skyline Trail to Glacier Vista, drop west onto the Nisqually Glacier roped, cross to the Wilson Glacier and climb past the Castle camps and up the Turtle to Camp Hazard (10,800 ft). Rappel or downclimb off the bivy rock to the glacier below the headwall, climb the lower ice step (35-40 degrees), the snow band and the steeper upper step (45-50 degrees) until the angle eases near 12,000 ft, then continue up the glacier to the crater rim.
wa_mount_rainier_liberty_ridge: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east to the White River Entrance of the park and turn west onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,300 ft; the trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is required.

Follow the Glacier Basin Trail up the White River valley. At about 6,700 ft, before reaching Glacier Basin Campground, leave the trail to the right and climb snow slopes to the notch of St. Elmo Pass at 7,400 ft.

Descend onto the lower Winthrop Glacier and traverse west, holding elevation, across Curtis Ridge to the ramp onto the Carbon Glacier near 7,300 ft. Ascend the Carbon, beneath Willis Wall, to the toe of the ridge, gain it at 8,600-8,800 ft and climb to the Thumb Rock bivy near 10,500 ft. Above, pass the Black Pyramid on its left (east) side, cross the bergschrund near 13,800 ft, and follow easing slopes to Liberty Cap.
wa_mount_rainier_nisqually_icefall: From SR 706 at Ashford, drive east through the park's Nisqually Entrance and follow the Paradise Road past Longmire about 18 miles to Paradise. Climbers park in the upper Paradise lot by the visitor center at about 5,400 ft. A park entrance pass is required, plus the climbing registration and a wilderness permit for any camp on the glacier.

Climb the Skyline Trail to Glacier Vista, then drop west onto the Nisqually Glacier and rope up. Ascend it with the Wapowety Cleaver on your left to the lower bergschrund near 9,900 ft, climb through the icefall and upper basin without stopping, and gain the cleaver near its 13,000 ft saddle. Work back onto the upper Nisqually to the saddle between Point Success and the crater rim, climb the last 500 ft to the rim and cross to Columbia Crest.
wa_mount_rainier_ptarmigan_ridge: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east to the White River Entrance of the park and turn west onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,400 ft; the Glacier Basin Trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is required.
wa_mount_st_helens_worm_flows: From I-5 Exit 21 at Woodland, follow SR 503 east about 30 miles to Cougar. Continue east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the Forest Road 83 junction, turn left and drive about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park, where the road is gated in winter and spring. A Washington Sno-Park permit is required December through March, and a Mount St. Helens climbing permit is required above 4,800 ft year-round.

Follow the Swift Creek Trail #244 north through forest about 2 miles to treeline near Chocolate Falls (about 3,700 ft) and cross to the west side of Swift Creek just above the falls. Follow posts, then cairns and wands, up the Worm Flows onto Worm Flow Ridge past the old seismic station near 6,200 ft, join the Monitor Ridge route near 7,400 ft, climb about 850 ft more to the crater rim and walk a quarter mile west along it to the high point.
wa_open_book_2: From the Nisqually Entrance drive about 15 miles east to the Paradise junction and turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road; drive about 2.7 miles, past Reflection Lakes and Louise Lake, to the Snow Lake trailhead on the south side of the road. From SR 123 it is about 16 miles west of the Stevens Canyon Entrance. Stevens Canyon Road is open to vehicles only in summer, and a park entrance pass is required.

Hike the Snow Lake Trail about a mile to Snow Lake, the last water. Past the lake follow the fading tread over a wooded rise, then work up and right into the talus gully on the peak's northwest side to a heather bench and the basin below the summit block. Climb moraine beside the snowfield to Unicorn Col, follow the use trail below the south-side cliffs to the horn, and climb the two left-leaning cracks about 50 ft right of the Classic Route to the top.
wa_plummer_peak_r1: Follow the signed Pinnacle Peak Trail south from the road, climbing moderately through mountain hemlock and yellow cedar forest for about 0.6 mile to a seasonal cascading creek, the only water on the hike and often dry by late summer.

Continue up the trail; by about 0.7 mile it breaks out of the forest into open talus and heather below Pinnacle's cliffs and steepens, switchbacking beneath the cliff bands on Pinnacle's north face. Lingering snow on these shaded switchbacks is the main hazard into July.
Switchback up the short, exposed final stretch to Pinnacle Saddle at about 1.25 miles and 5,920 ft, where the maintained trail ends.

At the saddle turn right (west) onto the climbers' path across a flat rocky shelf with a seasonal tarn. Where a fork continues straight toward Denman Peak, bear left (south, uphill) onto the thin boot path climbing the open, rocky north slopes of Plummer.
Scramble the last few hundred feet of class 2-3 rock and loose blocks, with brief hands-on moves and mild exposure, to the small summit.
wa_southwest_scramble: From the Nisqually Entrance on SR 706, follow the park road past Longmire toward Paradise and turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road just below Paradise. Drive east to Reflection Lakes and park in the pullouts; the signed trail leaves the south side of the road across from the largest lake. Stevens Canyon Road is gated in winter, typically opening around late May, and a park entrance pass is required.

Follow the maintained trail south about 1.3 miles to the 5,920 ft Pinnacle-Plummer saddle, where it ends. Turn left (east) on the boot path about a quarter mile toward the west side of Pinnacle's south face, scramble scree and loose rock on the most-travelled line to the obvious chute just east of the western prominence, and climb its steepening, cleaner class 4 rock to the summit.
wa_the_roof: From the Nisqually Entrance on SR 706, follow the park road past Longmire about 15.4 miles and turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road just below Paradise. Drive about 3.6 miles east, past Reflection Lakes, to the small Snow Lake trailhead lot on the right. Stevens Canyon Road is open only in summer, and a park entrance pass is required.

Hike the Snow Lake Trail about a mile to Snow Lake, then take the climbers' path up the northwest talus gully into the basin and climb the moraine beside the basin snowfield to Unicorn Col. Traverse east below the summit cliffs on the south side to the horn. The Roof starts about 20 ft left of the Classic Route, where the ridgeline meets the block: climb the gully beneath the roof, step right onto a ledge and continue to the top.
wa_unicorn_peak_r1: From the Nisqually Entrance on SR 706, follow the park road past Longmire about 15.4 miles and turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road just below Paradise. Drive about 3.6 miles east, past Reflection Lakes, to the small Snow Lake trailhead lot on the right; it holds only 15-20 cars. Stevens Canyon Road is open only in summer, and a park entrance pass is required.
Follow the maintained Snow Lake Trail through subalpine forest and meadow, passing the Bench Lake junction, about a mile with roughly 350 ft of up-and-down to Snow Lake, the last reliable water.
Skirt the lake's west shore and leave the maintained tread where a climbers' path breaks off up the steep drainage on Unicorn's northwest side.

Climb the steep gully about half a mile into the large open bowl, staying in the main gully and avoiding the steep headwalls to its left, then climb the moraine beside the small basin snowfield to the saddle on the peak's west side. The gully often holds firm snow through July, so carry an axe.
From the saddle turn east and follow the traversing use trail below the summit cliffs onto the peak's south side, crossing loose talus and blocky class 2-3 ground.
Continue the traverse east and around to the base of the summit horn on its south side, about 50 ft below the top, where the roped climbing begins.
Climb about 40-50 ft of 4th to low 5th class rock up the horn to the cramped summit; most parties rope up and rappel the south side on descent.
wa_scramble_route: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east to the park's Nisqually Entrance and continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire; a park entrance pass is required. Park at the lodge and museum lot, walk past the staff housing and cross the Nisqually River on the suspension bridge; the Eagle Peak trailhead is about 300 ft beyond the bridge on the east side of the river.

Follow the maintained Eagle Peak Trail as it climbs steeply through old-growth forest for about 2 miles to a stream crossing, then about another mile to a meadow, and finally steepens over rocky ground for the last half mile to Eagle Peak Saddle at about 5,700 ft, where the maintained trail ends.
wy_cathedral_traverse: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.
wy_east_face: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

Take the unsigned climbers' trail from the north end of the lot straight toward Teewinot, then up many steep switchbacks to the Apex near timberline. Continue up the ridge past the Idol and Worshipper towers on your left to the big east face snowfield, climb it, then scramble 3rd-class slabs and traverse left into the V-shaped gully; its 4th-class crux leads to the summit.
wy_owen_spalding: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

Hike the Lupine Meadows trail south and up the switchbacks, keeping left into Garnet Canyon at the Amphitheater Lake junction, and follow the canyon trail and boulder field to the Meadows. Climb the Middle Fork past the moraine and up the fixed-line headwall to the Lower Saddle, then ascend to the Upper Saddle and follow the Owen-Spalding route (Belly Roll, Crawl, chimneys) to the summit.
wy_southwest_couloir_3: From Moose Junction on US-26/89/191, turn west onto the Teton Park Road, pass the Moose entrance station, and drive north a little over 7 miles to the Lupine Meadows Road on the left, just south of Jenny Lake. Follow the gravel road to its end at the Lupine Meadows parking area. A Grand Teton National Park entrance pass is required.

Hike the Lupine Meadows trail south and up the switchbacks, keeping left into Garnet Canyon at the Amphitheater Lake junction, and follow the canyon trail to the Meadows. Head up the South Fork of Garnet Canyon toward the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then turn north up the Southwest Couloir to the summit.
wy_cirque_of_the_towers_traverse: From Boulder on US-191 south of Pinedale, follow WY-353 southeast about 18 miles to the end of the pavement, then continue on the Big Sandy-Elkhorn Road and follow the Big Sandy signs at each junction over roughly 25 miles of washboarded gravel to Big Sandy Campground and the road-end trailhead at about 9,100 ft.
